summary_brief: 2026年4月21日，AI Agent生态出现罕见信号——活动高度集中于单一仓库（ErikBjare/gptme），而非典型的多仓库并行推进。今日16个信号中gptme独占8个（50%），是4月历史中前所未有的单项目密度。新增方向明确：① gptme正式宣布移动端战略（Desktop/Mobile split，score=4），通过条件编译将Android/iOS支持与桌面逻辑解耦，是自该仓库追踪以来最大架构演进；② Claude官方插件市场新增Shopify Liquid LSP生态（Liquid开发+LSP语言服务器完整工具链），标志Anthropic从通用能力向垂直行业生态延伸。延续趋势方面：Claude Opus 4.7适配仍是多条线路共同推进的技术主线（gptme今天修复自适应思维模式，Shopify插件也基于4.7+构建），安全护栏文档化持续推进（gptme新增guardrails framing），CLI可观测性工具继续涌现（agents scan命令）。整体信号密度16个（低于近两日均值），但单项目密度创历史新高，生态从"多线程并行"切换至"单项目深度冲刺"模式——这是gptme自身发布节奏所致，还是生态开始出现主导项目集中的信号，值得持续观察。

engineering_signals.title: AI Agent 安全基础设施系统性重构
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenClaw（40+安全修复）、Codex（权限Profile规范化、设备密钥v2）、Vercel（环境变量默认敏感化）、gptme（自主代理护栏文档）同步推进安全升级，标志着 AI Agent 安全设计从补丁式修复转向系统性架构设计，对行业安全标准具有示范意义。

engineering_signals.title: Claude Opus 4.7 快速适配：多项目同步跟进
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: llama_index、gptme、Phoenix 在 24 小时内完成 Opus 4.7 支持，gptme 额外修复了 4.7+ 版本的思维模式兼容性问题。这表明 Claude 模型发布后主流 AI Agent 框架的响应速度显著提升，生态兼容性好。

engineering_signals.title: 多模型生态扩展：Bedrock、NVIDIA、Gemini 多云支持加速
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: CrewAI 新增 Bedrock V4、NVIDIA 模型提供商集成、Agent Framework 新增 Gemini 客户端和 .NET Foundry 集成，多云部署支持成为 Agent 框架标配功能，降低厂商锁定风险。

engineering_signals.title: gptme 项目整合与移动端支持战略
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: gptme 通过条件编译将 sidecar 限制在桌面端（为 Android 支持铺路）、合并 gptme-webui 子项目、新增 agents scan CLI 命令和完善的进程监控，展现了单一项目多维度演进路径，代表 AI Agent 工具链整合趋势。

engineering_signals.title: Shopify 电商生态 AI 开发工具链完善
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Shopify Liquid LSP 语言服务器加入官方插件市场，与 liquid-skills 形成完整工具链，并内置 WCAG 可访问性标准。这表明 AI 辅助开发正向垂直电商平台生态深度扩展。

engineering_signals.title: Agent 自动化与可观测性工具链成熟
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenDevin 新增 GitHub Webhook 自动化，Phoenix 新增属性过滤和 PXI 追踪控制，gptme 新增进程内存监控。这些改进提升了企业级 AI Agent 的运维可见性和事件驱动自动化能力。

engineering_signals.title: 代码库现代化与架构重构
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenDevin 完成 SQLAlchemy 2.0 迁移，Opencode 迁移到 Effect Schema，Codex 重构 TUI 应用和 DeveloperInstructions 分片。这些重构提升了代码类型安全性和可维护性，为后续功能扩展奠定基础。

engineering_signals.title: Vercel 平台深化 AI Agent 集成
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Vercel AI SDK 新增自动工具审批机制，Next.js 新增 'use cache' 可配置超时，Vercel CLI 环境变量默认敏感化。这表明 Vercel 正在成为 AI Agent 前端部署的首选平台。

engineering_signals.title: Anthropic SDK 缓存优化与性能提升
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: gptme 修复 Anthropic 缓存边界优化，将静态 bootstrap 保留在顶级系统提示；Claude Code 大型会话（40MB+）性能提升 67%。这些优化显著降低 API 调用成本。

release_signals.title: Agent Framework Python新增Gemini客户端
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增GeminiChatClient支持，扩大了多模型集成能力，支持Vertex AI和Gemini API双路径，同时引入实验性文件历史提供者和context_providers工作流抽象，增强企业级多Agent编排能力

release_signals.title: OpenClaw大规模安全与权限升级
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增文件系统权限deny-read glob策略、平台沙箱执行、代码执行隔离等40+项安全修复，包括SSRF防护、workspace env注入阻止、gateway工具配置变更Guard等系统性安全加固

release_signals.title: OpenAI Codex权限系统重构
release_signals.why_it_matters: 文件系统权限新增glob deny-read策略、managed deny-read要求、平台沙箱执行和隔离的codex exec运行，同时默认启用工具发现和图像生成能力

release_signals.title: Vercel环境变量默认敏感化
release_signals.why_it_matters: 生产环境和预览环境的环境变量现在默认加密存储且不可检索，需要显式--no-sensitive才能回退到旧行为，从根本上防止敏感信息泄露

release_signals.title: Claude Code大型会话性能提升67%
release_signals.why_it_matters: 40MB以上会话的/resume操作速度提升67%，同时优化了多stdio服务器MCP启动性能和终端滚动体验

release_signals.title: Agent Framework .NET Foundry集成
release_signals.why_it_matters: .NET SDK新增Foundry Hosted Agents全面支持，包括Toolboxes、Handoff编排和Evals集成，强化企业微软生态

release_signals.title: Phoenix新增Claude Opus 4.7与PXI控制
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增Claude Opus 4.7支持，同时引入PXI同意和追踪共享控制，增强AI可观测平台的合规性

release_signals.title: OpenCode新增NVIDIA模型提供商
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增NVIDIA作为内置提供商选项，支持连接文档和必需的头部属性，扩展了支持的模型生态

release_signals.title: OpenAI Agents Python新增BoxMount支持
release_signals.why_it_matters: 新增BoxMount支持增强沙箱临时挂载生命周期管理，简化云存储集成

releases.author: steipete
releases.summary:
## 2026.4.20

### Changes

- Onboard/wizard: restyle the setup security disclaimer with a single yellow warning banner, section headings and bulleted checklists, and un-dim the note body so key guidance is easy to scan; add a loading spinner during the initial model catalog load so the wizard no longer goes blank while it runs; add an "API key" placeholder to provider API key prompts. (#69553) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- Agents/prompts: strengthen the default system prompt and OpenAI GPT-5 overlay with clearer completion bias, live-state checks, weak-result recovery, and verification-before-final guidance.
- Models/costs: support tiered model pricing from cached catalogs and configured models, and include bundled Moonshot Kimi K2.6/K2.5 cost estimates for token-usage reports. (#67605) Thanks @sliverp.
- Sessions/Maintenance: enforce the built-in entry cap and age prune by default, and prune oversized stores at load time so accumulated cron/executor session backlogs cannot OOM the gateway before the write path runs. (#69404) Thanks @bobrenze-bot.
- Plugins/tests: reuse plugin loader alias and Jiti config resolution across repeated same-context loads, reducing import-heavy test overhead. (#69316) Thanks @amknight.
- Cron: split runtime execution state into `jobs-state.json` so `jobs.json` stays stable for git-tracked job definitions. (#63105) Thanks @Feelw00.
- Agents/compaction: send opt-in start and completion notices during context compaction. (#67830) Thanks @feniix.
- Moonshot/Kimi: default bundled Moonshot setup, web search, and media-understanding surfaces to `kimi-k2.6` while keeping `kimi-k2.5` available for compatibility. (#69477) Thanks @scoootscooob.
- Moonshot/Kimi: allow `thinking.keep = "all"` on `moonshot/kimi-k2.6`, and strip it for other Moonshot models or requests where pinned `tool_choice` disables thinking. (#68816) Thanks @aniaan.
- BlueBubbles/groups: forward per-group `systemPrompt` config into inbound context `GroupSystemPrompt` so configured group-specific behavioral instructions (for example threaded-reply and tapback conventions) are injected on every turn. Supports `"*"` wildcard fallback matching the existing `requireMention` pattern. Closes #60665. (#69198) Thanks @omarshahine.
- Plugins/tasks: add a detached runtime registration contract so plugin executors can own detached task lifecycle and cancellation without reaching into core task internals. (#68915) Thanks @mbelinky.
- Terminal/logging: optimize `sanitizeForLog()` by replacing the iterative control-character stripping loop with a single regex pass while preserving the existing ANSI-first sanitization behavior. (#67205) Thanks @bulutmuf.
- QA/CI: make `openclaw qa suite` and `openclaw qa telegram` fail by default when scenarios fail, add `--allow-failures` for artifact-only runs, and tighten live-lane defaults for CI automation. (#69122) Thanks @joshavant.
- Mattermost: stream thinking, tool activity, and partial reply text into a single draft preview post that finalizes in place when safe. (#47838) thanks @ninjaa.

### Fixes

- Exec/YOLO: stop rejecting gateway-host exec in `security=full` plus `ask=off` mode via the Python/Node script preflight hardening path, so promptless YOLO exec once again runs direct interpreter stdin and heredoc forms such as `node <<'NODE' ... NODE`.
- OpenAI Codex: normalize legacy `openai-completions` transport overrides on default OpenAI/Codex and GitHub Copilot-compatible hosts back to the native Codex Responses transport while leaving custom proxies untouched. (#45304, #42194) Thanks @dyss1992 and @DeadlySilent.
- Anthropic/plugins: scope Anthropic `api: "anthropic-messages"` defaulting to Anthropic-owned providers, so `openai-codex` and other providers without an explicit `api` no longer get rewritten to the wrong transport. Fixes #64534.
- fix(qqbot): add SSRF guard to direct-upload URL paths in uploadC2CMedia and uploadGroupMedia [AI-assisted]. (#69595) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- fix(gateway): enforce allowRequestSessionKey gate on template-rendered mapping sessionKeys. (#69381) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Browser/Chrome MCP: surface `DevToolsActivePort` attach failures as browser-connectivity errors instead of a generic "waiting for tabs" timeout, and point signed-out fallbacks toward the managed `openclaw` profile.
- Webchat/images: treat inline image attachments as media for empty-turn gating while still ignoring metadata-only blank turns. (#69474) Thanks @Jaswir.
- Discord/think: only show `adaptive` in `/think` autocomplete for provider/model pairs that actually support provider-managed adaptive thinking, so GPT/OpenAI models no longer advertise an Anthropic-only option.
- Thinking: only expose `max` for models that explicitly support provider max reasoning, and remap stored `max` settings to the largest supported thinking mode when users switch to another model.
- Gateway/usage: bound the cost usage cache with FIFO eviction so date/range lookups cannot grow unbounded. (#68842) Thanks @Feelw00.
- OpenAI/Responses: resolve `/think` levels against each GPT model's supported reasoning efforts so `/think off` no longer becomes high reasoning or sends unsupported `reasoning.effort: "none"` payloads.
- Lobster/TaskFlow: allow managed approval resumes to use `approvalId` without a resume token, and persist that id in approval wait state. (#69559) Thanks @kirkluokun.
- Plugins/startup: install bundled runtime dependencies into each plugin's own runtime directory, reuse source-checkout repair caches after rebuilds, and log only packages that were actually installed so repeated Gateway starts stay quiet once deps are present.
- Plugins/startup: ignore pnpm's `npm_execpath` when repairing bundled plugin runtime dependencies and skip workspace-only package specs so npm-only install flags or local workspace links do not break packaged plugin startup.
- MCP: block interpreter-startup env keys such as `NODE_OPTIONS` for stdio servers while preserving ordinary credential and proxy env vars. (#69540) Thanks @drobison00.
- Agents/shell: ignore non-interactive placeholder shells like `/usr/bin/false` and `/sbin/nologin`, falling back to `sh` so service-user exec runs no longer exit immediately. (#69308) Thanks @sk7n4k3d.
- Setup/TUI: relaunch the setup hatch TUI in a fresh process while preserving the configured gateway target and auth source, so onboarding recovers terminal state cleanly without exposing gateway secrets on command-line args. (#69524) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- Codex: avoid re-exposing the image-generation tool on native vision turns with inbound images, and keep bare image-model overrides on the configured image provider. (#65061) Thanks @zhulijin1991.
- Sessions/reset: clear auto-sourced model, provider, and auth-profile overrides on `/new` and `/reset` while preserving explicit user selections, so channel sessions stop staying pinned to runtime fallback choices. (#69419) Thanks @sk7n4k3d.
- Sessions/costs: snapshot `estimatedCostUsd` like token counters so repeated persist paths no longer compound the same run cost by up to dozens of times. (#69403) Thanks @MrMiaigi.
- OpenAI Codex: route ChatGPT/Codex OAuth Responses requests through the `/backend-api/codex` endpoint so `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` no longer hits the removed `/backend-api/responses` alias. (#69336) Thanks @mzogithub.
- OpenAI/Responses: omit disabled reasoning payloads when `/think off` is active, so GPT reasoning models no longer receive unsupported `reasoning.effort: "none"` requests. (#61982) Thanks @a-tokyo.
- Gateway/pairing: treat loopback shared-secret node-host, TUI, and gateway clients as local for pairing decisions, so trusted local tools no longer reconnect as remote clients and fail with `pairing required`. (#69431) Thanks @SARAMALI15792.
- Active Memory: degrade gracefully when memory recall fails during prompt building, logging a warning and letting the reply continue without memory context instead of failing the whole turn. (#69485) Thanks @Magicray1217.
- Ollama: add provider-policy defaults for `baseUrl` and `models` so implicit local discovery can run before config validation rejects a minimal Ollama provider config. (#69370) Thanks @PratikRai0101.
- Agents/model selection: clear transient auto-failover session overrides before each turn so recovered primary models are retried immediately without emitting user-override reset warnings. (#69365) Thanks @hitesh-github99.
- Auto-reply: apply silent `NO_REPLY` policy per conversation type, so direct chats get a helpful rewritten reply while groups and internal deliveries can remain quiet. (#68644) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- Telegram/status reactions: honor `messages.removeAckAfterReply` when lifecycle status reactions are enabled, clearing or restoring the reaction after success/error using the configured hold timings. (#68067) Thanks @poiskgit.
- Web search/plugins: resolve plugin-scoped SecretRef API keys for bundled Exa, Firecrawl, Gemini, Kimi, Perplexity, Tavily, and Grok web-search providers when they are selected through the shared web-search config. (#68424) Thanks @afurm.
- Telegram/polling: raise the default polling watchdog threshold from 90s to 120s and add configurable `channels.telegram.pollingStallThresholdMs` (also per-account) so long-running Telegram work gets more room before polling is treated as stalled. (#57737) Thanks @Vitalcheffe.
- Telegram/polling: bound the persisted-offset confirmation `getUpdates` probe with a client-side timeout so a zombie socket cannot hang polling recovery before the runner watchdog starts. (#50368) Thanks @boticlaw.
- Agents/Pi runner: retry silent `stopReason=error` turns with no output when no side effects ran, so non-frontier providers that briefly return empty error turns get another chance instead of ending the session early. (#68310) Thanks @Chased1k.
- Plugins/memory: preserve the active memory capability when read-only snapshot plugin loads run, so status and provider discovery paths no longer wipe memory public artifacts. (#69219) Thanks @zeroaltitude.
- Plugins: keep only the highest-precedence manifest when distinct discovered plugins share an id, so lower-precedence global or workspace duplicates no longer load beside bundled or config-selected plugins. (#41626) Thanks @Tortes.
- fix(security): block MINIMAX_API_HOST workspace env injection and remove env-driven URL routing [AI-assisted]. (#67300) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Cron/delivery: treat explicit `delivery.mode: "none"` runs as not requested even if the runner reports `delivered: false`, so no-delivery cron jobs no longer persist false delivery failures or errors. (#69285) Thanks @matsuri1987.
- Plugins/install: repair active and default-enabled bundled plugin runtime dependencies before import in packaged installs, so bundled Discord, WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, and provider plugins work without putting their dependency trees in core.
- BlueBubbles: raise the outbound `/api/v1/message/text` send timeout default from 10s to 30s, and add a configurable `channels.bluebubbles.sendTimeoutMs` (also per-account) so macOS 26 setups where Private API iMessage sends stall for 60+ seconds no longer silently lose messages at the 10s abort. Probes, chat lookups, and health checks keep the shorter 10s default. Fixes #67486. (#69193) Thanks @omarshahine.
- Agents/bootstrap: budget truncation markers against per-file caps, preserve source content instead of silently wasting bootstrap bytes, and avoid marker-only output in tiny-budget truncation cases. (#69114) Thanks @BKF-Gitty.
- Context engine/plugins: stop rejecting third-party context engines whose `info.id` differs from the registered plugin slot id. The strict-match contract added in 2026.4.14 broke `lossless-claw` and other plugins whose internal engine id does not equal the slot id they are registered under, producing repeated `info.id must match registered id` lane failures on every turn. Fixes #66601. (#66678) Thanks @GodsBoy.
- Agents/compaction: rename embedded Pi compaction lifecycle events to `compaction_start` / `compaction_end` so OpenClaw stays aligned with `pi-coding-agent` 0.66.1 event naming. (#67713) Thanks @mpz4life.
- Security/dotenv: block all `OPENCLAW_*` keys from untrusted workspace `.env` files so workspace-local env loading fails closed for new runtime-control variables instead of silently inheriting them. (#473)
- Gateway/device pairing: restrict non-admin paired-device sessions (device-token auth) to their own pairing list, approve, and reject actions so a paired device cannot enumerate other devices or approve/reject pairing requests authored by another device. Admin and shared-secret operator sessions retain full visibility. (#69375) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Agents/gateway tool: extend the agent-facing `gateway` tool's config mutation guard so model-driven `config.patch` and `config.apply` cannot rewrite operator-trusted paths (sandbox, plugin trust, gateway auth/TLS, hook routing and tokens, SSRF policy, MCP servers, workspace filesystem hardening) and cannot bypass the guard by editing per-agent sandbox, tools, or embedded-Pi overrides in place under `agents.list[]`. (#69377) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Gateway/websocket broadcasts: require `operator.read` (or higher) for chat, agent, and tool-result event frames so pairing-scoped and node-role sessions no longer passively receive session chat content, and scope-gate unknown broadcast events by default. Plugin-defined `plugin.*` broadcasts are scoped to operator.write/admin, and status/transport events (`heartbeat`, `presence`, `tick`, etc.) remain unrestricted. Per-client sequence numbers preserve per-connection monotonicity. (#69373) Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Agents/compaction: always reload embedded Pi resources through an explicit loader and reapply reserve-token overrides so runs without extension factories no longer silently lose compaction settings before session start. (#67146) Thanks @ly85206559.
- Memory-core/dreaming: normalize sweep timestamps and reuse hashed narrative session keys for fallback cleanup so Dreaming narrative sub-sessions stop leaking. (#67023) Thanks @chiyouYCH.
- Gateway/startup: delay HTTP bind until websocket handlers are attached, so immediate post-startup websocket health/connect probes no longer hit the startup race window. (#43392) Thanks @dalefrieswthat.
- Codex/app-server: release the session lane when a downstream consumer throws while draining the `turn/completed` notification, so follow-up messages after a Codex plugin reply stop queueing behind a stale lane lock. Fixes #67996. (#69072) Thanks @ayeshakhalid192007-dev.
- Codex/app-server: default approval handling to `on-request` so Codex harness sessions do not start with overly permissive tool approvals. (#68721) Thanks @Lucenx9.
- Cron/delivery: keep isolated cron chat delivery tools available, resolve `channel: "last"` targets from the gateway, show delivery previews in `cron list/show`, and avoid duplicate fallback sends after direct message-tool delivery. (#69587) Thanks @obviyus.
- Cron/Telegram: key isolated direct-delivery dedupe to each cron execution instead of the reused session id, so recurring Telegram announce runs no longer report delivered while silently skipping later sends. (#69000) Thanks @obviyus.
- Models/Kimi: default bundled Kimi thinking to off and normalize Anthropic-compatible `thinking` payloads so stale session `/think` state no longer silently re-enables reasoning on Kimi runs. (#68907) Thanks @frankekn.
- Control UI/cron: keep the runtime-only `last` delivery sentinel from being materialized into persisted cron delivery and failure-alert channel configs when jobs are created or edited. (#68829) Thanks @tianhaocui.
- OpenAI/Responses: strip orphaned reasoning blocks before outbound Responses API calls so compacted or restored histories no longer fail on standalone reasoning items. (#55787) Thanks @suboss87.
- Cron/CLI: parse PowerShell-style `--tools` allow-lists the same way as comma-separated input, so `cron add` and `cron edit` no longer persist `exec read write` as one combined tool entry on Windows. (#68858) Thanks @chen-zhang-cs-code.
- Browser/user-profile: let existing-session `profile="user"` tool calls auto-route to a connected browser node or use explicit `target="node"`, while still honoring explicit `target="host"` pinning. (#48677)
- Discord/slash commands: tolerate partial Discord channel metadata in slash-command and model-picker flows so partial channel objects no longer crash when channel names, topics, or thread parent metadata are unavailable. (#68953) Thanks @dutifulbob.
- BlueBubbles: consolidate outbound HTTP through a typed `BlueBubblesClient` that resolves the SSRF policy once at construction so image attachments stop getting blocked on localhost and reactions stop getting blocked on private-IP BB deployments. Fixes #34749 and #59722. (#68234) Thanks @omarshahine.
- Cron/gateway: reject ambiguous announce delivery config at add/update time so invalid multi-channel or target-id provider settings fail early instead of persisting broken cron jobs. (#69015) Thanks @obviyus.
- Cron/main-session delivery: preserve `heartbeat.target="last"` through deferred wake queuing, gateway wake forwarding, and same-target wake coalescing so queued cron replies still return to the last active chat. (#69021) Thanks @obviyus.
- Cron/gateway: ignore disabled channels when announce delivery ambiguity is checked, and validate main-session delivery patches against the live cron service default agent so hot-reloaded agent config does not falsely reject valid updates. (#69040) Thanks @obviyus.
- Matrix/allowlists: hot-reload `dm.allowFrom` and `groupAllowFrom` entries on inbound messages while keeping config removals authoritative, so Matrix allowlist changes no longer require a channel restart to add or revoke a sender. (#68546) Thanks @johnlanni.
- BlueBubbles: always set `method` explicitly on outbound text sends (`"private-api"` when available, `"apple-script"` otherwise), and prefer Private API on macOS 26 even for plain text. Fixes silent delivery failure on macOS setups without Private API where an omitted `method` let BB Server fall back to version-dependent default behavior that silently drops the message (#64480), and the AppleScript `-1700` error on macOS 26 Tahoe plain text sends (#53159). (#69070) Thanks @xqing3.
- Matrix/commands: recognize slash commands that are prefixed with the bot's Matrix mention, so room messages like `@bot:server /new` trigger the command path without requiring custom mention regexes. (#68570) Thanks @nightq and @johnlanni.
- Gateway/pairing: return reason-specific `PAIRING_REQUIRED` details, remediation hints, and request ids so unapproved-device and scope-upgrade failures surface actionable recovery guidance in the CLI and Control UI. (#69227) Thanks @obviyus.
- Agents/subagents: include requested role and runtime timing on subagent failure payloads so parent agents can correlate failed or timed-out child work. (#68726) Thanks @BKF-Gitty.
- Gateway/sessions: reject stale agent-scoped sessions after an agent is removed from config while preserving legacy default-agent main-session aliases. (#65986) Thanks @bittoby.
- Doctor/gateway: surface pending device pairing requests, scope-upgrade approval drift, and stale device-token mismatch repair steps so `openclaw doctor --fix` no longer leaves pairing/auth setup failures unexplained. (#69210) Thanks @obviyus.
- Cron/isolated-agent: preserve explicit `delivery.mode: "none"` message targets for isolated runs without inheriting implicit `last` routing, so agent-initiated Telegram sends keep their authored destination while bare `mode:none` jobs stay targetless. (#69153) Thanks @obviyus.
- Cron/isolated-agent: keep `delivery.mode: "none"` account-only or thread-only configs from inheriting a stale implicit recipient, so isolated runs only resolve message routing when the job authored an explicit `to` target. (#69163) Thanks @obviyus.
- Gateway/TUI: retry session history while the local gateway is still finishing startup, so `openclaw tui` reconnects no longer fail on transient `chat.history unavailable during gateway startup` errors. (#69164) Thanks @shakkernerd.
- BlueBubbles/reactions: fall back to `love` when an agent reacts with an emoji outside the iMessage tapback set (`love`/`like`/`dislike`/`laugh`/`emphasize`/`question`), so wider-vocabulary model reactions like `👀` still produce a visible tapback instead of failing the whole reaction request. Configured ack reactions still validate strictly via the new `normalizeBlueBubblesReactionInputStrict` path. (#64693) Thanks @zqchris.
- BlueBubbles: prefer iMessage over SMS when both chats exist for the same handle, honor explicit `sms:` targets, and never silently downgrade iMessage-available recipients. (#61781) Thanks @rmartin.
- Telegram/setup: require numeric `allowFrom` user IDs during setup instead of offering unsupported `@username` DM resolution, and point operators to `from.id`/`getUpdates` for discovery. (#69191) Thanks @obviyus.
- GitHub Copilot/onboarding: default GitHub Copilot setup to `claude-opus-4.6` and keep the bundled default model list aligned, so new Copilot setups no longer start on the older `gpt-4o` default. (#69207) Thanks @obviyus.
- Gateway/status: separate reachability, capability, and read-probe reporting so connect-only or scope-limited sessions no longer look fully healthy, and normalize SSH targets entered as `ssh user@host`. (#69215) Thanks @obviyus.
- Slack: fix outbound replies failing with "unresolved SecretRef" for accounts configured via `file` or `exec` secret sources; the send path now tolerates the runtime snapshot retaining an unresolved channel SecretRef when a boot-resolved token override is already available. (#68954) Thanks @openperf.
- Control UI/device pairing: explain scope and role approval upgrades during reconnects, and show requested versus approved access in the Control UI and `openclaw devices` so broader reconnects no longer look like lost pairings. (#69221) Thanks @obviyus.
- Gateway/Control UI: surface pending scope, role, and device-metadata pairing approvals in auth errors and Control UI hints so broader reconnects no longer look like random auth breakage. (#69226) Thanks @obviyus.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-04-21

### Added
- **agent-framework-gemini**: Add `GeminiChatClient` ([#4847](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4847))
- **agent-framework-core**: Add `context_providers` and `description` to `workflow.as_agent()` ([#4651](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4651))
- **agent-framework-core**: Add experimental file history provider ([#5248](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5248))
- **agent-framework-core**: Add OpenAI types to the default checkpoint encoding allow list ([#5297](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5297))
- **agent-framework-core**: Add `AgentExecutorResponse.with_text()` to preserve conversation history through custom executors ([#5255](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5255))
- **agent-framework-a2a**: Propagate A2A metadata from `Message`, `Artifact`, `Task`, and event types ([#5256](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5256))
- **agent-framework-core**: Add `finish_reason` support to `AgentResponse` and `AgentResponseUpdate` ([#5211](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5211))
- **agent-framework-hyperlight**: Add Hyperlight CodeAct package and docs ([#5185](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5185))
- **agent-framework-openai**: Add search tool content support for OpenAI responses ([#5302](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5302))
- **agent-framework-foundry**: Add support for Foundry Toolboxes ([#5346](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5346))
- **agent-framework-ag-ui**: Expose `forwardedProps` to agents and tools via session metadata ([#5264](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5264))
- **agent-framework-foundry**: Add hosted agent V2 support ([#5379](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5379))

### Changed
- **agent-framework-azure-cosmos**: [BREAKING] `CosmosCheckpointStorage` now uses restricted pickle deserialization by default, matching `FileCheckpointStorage` behavior. If your checkpoints contain application-defined types, pass them via `allowed_checkpoint_types=["my_app.models:MyState"]`. ([#5200](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/issues/5200))
- **agent-framework-core**: Improve skill name validation ([#4530](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4530))
- **agent-framework-azure-cosmos**: Add `allowed_checkpoint_types` support to `CosmosCheckpointStorage` for parity with `FileCheckpointStorage` ([#5202](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5202))
- **agent-framework-core**: Move `InMemory` history provider injection to first invocation ([#5236](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5236))
- **agent-framework-github-copilot**: Forward provider config to `SessionConfig` in `GitHubCopilotAgent` ([#5195](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5195))
- **agent-framework-hyperlight-codeact**: Flatten `execute_code` output ([#5333](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5333))
- **dependencies**: Bump `pygments` from `2.19.2` to `2.20.0` in `/python` ([#4978](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4978))
- **tests**: Bump misc integration retry delay to 30s ([#5293](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5293))
- **tests**: Improve misc integration test robustness ([#5295](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5295))
- **tests**: Skip hosted tools test on transient upstream MCP errors ([#5296](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5296))

### Fixed
- **agent-framework-core**: Fix `python-feature-lifecycle` skill YAML frontmatter ([#5226](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5226))
- **agent-framework-core**: Fix `HandoffBuilder` dropping function-level middleware when cloning agents ([#5220](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5220))
- **agent-framework-ag-ui**: Fix deterministic state updates from tool results ([#5201](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5201))
- **agent-framework-devui**: Fix streaming memory growth and add cross-platform regression coverage ([#5221](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5221))
- **agent-framework-core**: Skip `get_final_response` in `_finalize_stream` when the stream has errored ([#5232](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5232))
- **agent-framework-openai**: Fix reasoning replay when `store=False` ([#5250](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5250))
- **agent-framework-foundry**: Handle `url_citation` annotations in `FoundryChatClient` streaming responses ([#5071](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5071))
- **agent-framework-gemini**: Fix Gemini client support for Gemini API and Vertex AI ([#5258](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5258))
- **agent-framework-copilotstudio**: Fix `CopilotStudioAgent` to reuse conversation ID from an existing session ([#5299](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/5299))

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/compare/python-1.0.1...python-1.1.0

新增 `context_providers` 和 `description` 参数到 workflow.as_agent()

releases.summary:
## Mem0 Node SDK (v3.0.1)

**Release date:** 2026-04-20
**Package:** [`mem0ai`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mem0ai) on npm
**npm tag:** `ts-v3.0.1`

## Summary

Patch release that fixes telemetry's reported `client_version` drifting from the actual package version. Both telemetry clients (`MemoryClient` and OSS `Memory`) now always report the installed package version, driven by `package.json` at build time.

## Bug Fixes

- **Telemetry:** Inject SDK version into telemetry at build time via esbuild's `define`, replacing the two hardcoded `let version = "..."` strings in `mem0-ts/src/client/telemetry.ts` and `mem0-ts/src/oss/src/utils/telemetry.ts`. Previously these were set to `2.1.36` and `2.1.34` respectively, while the published package was on `3.x` — every telemetry event was reporting the wrong version. The placeholder is substituted with a string literal at bundle time, so there is no extra runtime I/O and no `require("./package.json")` in the shipped bundle. ([#4897](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/pull/4897))

## Internal

- Added `mem0-ts/src/global.d.ts` declaring the `__MEM0_SDK_VERSION__` ambient constant used by the telemetry modules.
- `mem0-ts/tsup.config.ts` now reads `pkg.version` and passes `{ __MEM0_SDK_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(pkg.version) }` to `define` for both `client` and `oss` builds.
- `mem0-ts/jest.setup.ts` exposes the same value on `globalThis` so `ts-jest` test runs continue to resolve the symbol.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install mem0ai@3.0.1
# or
pnpm add mem0ai@3.0.1
# or
yarn add mem0ai@3.0.1
```

No code changes required — this release is a drop-in replacement for `3.0.0`. After upgrading, telemetry events will report `client_version: "3.0.1"` (and future bumps to `package.json` will flow through automatically with no further source edits).

## Full Changeset

- `fix(ts-sdk): inject SDK version into telemetry at build time`
- `chore(release): bump TS SDK to 3.0.1`

**Diff:** https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/compare/ts-v3.0.0...ts-v3.0.1

移除了 telemetry.ts 中硬编码的 2.1.36 和 2.1.34 版本号
添加 global.d.ts 声明文件定义 __MEM0_SDK_VERSION__ 常量
更新 tsup.config.ts 从 package.json 读取版本并注入构建
ai_summary.summary_cn: 这是一个修复版本，解决了遥测数据（telemetry）中报告的客户端版本与实际包版本不一致的问题。此前 MemoryClient 和 OSS Memory 的遥测事件一直报告错误的版本号（如 2.1.x），而实际包版本已是 3.x。修复方案通过 esbuild 的 define 机制在构建时从 package.json 读取版本并注入，避免了硬编码且无需额外的运行时 I/O。此版本是完全兼容的 drop-in 替换，无需代码修改。

## New Features
- Standalone installs are more self-contained, and `codex app` now opens or installs Desktop correctly on Windows and Intel Macs (#17022, #18500).
- The TUI can open `/side` conversations for quick side questions, and queued input now supports slash commands and `!` shell prompts while work is running (#18190, #18542).
- Plan Mode can start implementation in a fresh context, with context-usage shown before deciding whether to carry the planning thread forward (#17499, #18573).
- Plugin workflows now include tabbed browsing, inline enable/disable toggles, marketplace removal, and remote, cross-repo, or local marketplace sources (#18222, #18395, #17752, #17751, #17277, #18017, #18246).
- Filesystem permissions now support deny-read glob policies, managed deny-read requirements, platform sandbox enforcement, and isolated `codex exec` runs that ignore user config or rules (#15979, #17740, #18096, #18646).
- Tool discovery and image generation are now enabled by default, with higher-detail image handling and original-detail metadata support for MCP and `js_repl` image outputs (#17854, #17153, #17714, #18386).

## Bug Fixes
- App-server approvals, user-input prompts, and MCP elicitations now disappear from the TUI when another client resolves them, instead of leaving stale prompts behind (#15134).
- Remote-control startup now tolerates missing ChatGPT auth, and MCP startup cancellation works again through app-server sessions (#18117, #18078).
- Resumed and forked app-server threads now replay token usage immediately so context/status UI starts with the restored state (#18023).
- Security-sensitive flows were tightened: logout revokes managed ChatGPT tokens, project hooks and exec policies require trusted workspaces, and Windows sandbox setup avoids broad user-profile and SSH-root grants (#17825, #14718, #18443, #18493).
- Sandboxed `apply_patch` writes work correctly with split filesystem policies, and file watchers now notice files created after watching begins (#18296, #18492).
- Several TUI rough edges were fixed, including fatal skills-list failures, invalid resume hints, duplicate context statusline entries, `/model` menu loops, redundant memory notices, and terminal title quoting in iTerm2 (#18061, #18059, #18054, #18154, #18580, #18261).

## Documentation
- Added a security-boundaries reference to `SECURITY.md` for sandboxing, approvals, and network controls (#17848, #18004).
- Documented custom MCP server approval defaults and exec-server stdin behavior (#17843, #18086).
- Updated app-server docs for plugin API changes, marketplace removal, resume/fork token-usage replay, and warning notifications (#17277, #17751, #18023, #18298).
- Added a short guide for the responses API proxy (#18604).

## Chores
- Split plugin and marketplace code into `codex-core-plugins`, moved more connector code into `connectors`, and continued breaking up the large core session/turn modules (#18070, #18158, #18200, #18206, #18244, #18249).
- Refactored config loading and `AGENTS.md` discovery behind narrower filesystem and manager abstractions (#18209, #18035).
- Stabilized Bazel and CI with flake fixes, native Rust test sharding, scoped repository caches, stronger Windows clippy coverage, and updated `rules_rs`/LLVM pins (#17791, #18082, #18366, #18350, #18397).
- Added core CODEOWNERS and a smaller development build profile (#18362, #18612).
- Removed the stale core `models.json` and updated release preparation to refresh the active model catalog (#18585).

## Core

- Prevented compiled binaries from failing on startup because of a circular session schema dependency.
- Renamed the compaction setting to `preserve_recent_tokens` for the budget that keeps recent turns verbatim.
- Preserved concurrent edits to the same file instead of letting parallel edits overwrite each other.
- Fixed managed installs on Windows and added bundled ripgrep support for Windows ARM64.
- Added NVIDIA as a built-in provider option, including connection docs and required attribution headers. (@anniesurla)
- Kept recent conversation turns verbatim during session compaction so follow-up work keeps more local context.
- Fell back to summarizing the full conversation when preserved recent turns include too much media to fit safely.

## Desktop

- Reduced loading flicker when opening projects and bringing prompt controls online.
- Added a separate terminal font setting and bundled JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono.

## 🚀 ClawX v0.3.10

ClawX - Graphical AI Assistant based on OpenClaw

### 📦 Downloads

Please select the appropriate installer for your operating system and architecture:

#### macOS
- **Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4)**: `ClawX-*-mac-arm64.dmg`
- **Intel (x64)**: `ClawX-*-mac-x64.dmg`

#### Windows
- **Installer (x64)**: `ClawX-*-win-x64.exe`
- **Installer (ARM64)**: `ClawX-*-win-arm64.exe`

#### Linux
- **AppImage (x64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (Universal format, recommended)
- **AppImage (ARM64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-arm64.AppImage`
- **Debian/Ubuntu (x64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-amd64.deb`
- **Debian/Ubuntu (ARM64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-arm64.deb`
- **RPM (x64)**: `ClawX-*-linux-x86_64.rpm`

### 📝 Release Notes

See the auto-generated release notes below for detailed changes.

### ⚠️ Installation Notes

- **macOS**: On first launch, you may see "cannot verify developer". Go to System Preferences → Security & Privacy to allow the app to run
- **Windows**: SmartScreen may block the app. Click "More info" → "Run anyway" to proceed
- **Linux AppImage**: First run `chmod +x ClawX-*.AppImage` to add execute permission. On Ubuntu 22.04 you may also need `sudo apt install libfuse2`; on Ubuntu 24.04 use `sudo apt install libfuse2t64`
- **Linux .deb (Ubuntu 24.04)**: If installation fails due to missing dependencies, use `sudo apt install libgtk-3-0t64 libnotify4t64 libxss1t64` before installing

Sensitive values are encrypted at rest and cannot be retrieved later via the dashboard or CLI; they are still resolved for builds, deployments, `vercel env pull`, and runtime. ([#16041](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/pull/16041))

    Behavior per target:

    -   **Production** or **Preview**: defaults to `sensitive`. Pass `--no-sensitive` to opt back in to the previous `encrypted` behavior (value remains readable later).
    -   **Development**: always stored as `encrypted` (sensitive is not supported by the Vercel API for Development). Passing `--sensitive` alongside a Development target now errors up-front instead of silently falling back.
    -   **Mixed selection** (e.g., interactive checkbox picks `production + preview + development`): errors and asks you to run `vercel env add` separately for Development, because Development cannot share a record type with Production/Preview.

    Flag summary:

    -   `--sensitive`: unchanged in meaning (request a sensitive variable); now errors when combined with Development.
    -   `--no-sensitive`: new; opt out of the new default for Production/Preview.
    -   `--sensitive --no-sensitive` together: errors.

    On teams that enable the "Enforce Sensitive Environment Variables" policy in team settings, the CLI now reads the policy from the team object and notes in the output that the policy is active; the server already promotes Production/Preview variables to sensitive silently, and the CLI's own logs are now honest about it. Passing `--no-sensitive` on a policy-on team for Production/Preview now emits a warning — the flag is a no-op because the server promotes the variable regardless — and the CLI sends `type: 'sensitive'` so its own `--debug` output matches what gets stored.

issue_insights.summary_brief: 本期监测到 5 类跨仓库共性问题，影响范围涵盖 20-54 个仓库，其中 Path Traversal 漏洞（auth_permission）、配置泄漏（session_state）和 Settings 状态管理缺陷（ui_interaction）构成最广泛的生态风险；与此同时，多个 SDK 仓库在 streaming/code_execution 工具调用路径上存在系统性 ToParam/Accumulator 缺陷，导致 agentic loop 阻断。
global_highlights: Path Traversal 漏洞影响 20 个仓库，agentscope-ai/agentscope（CVSS 9.1）和 TransformerOptimus/SuperAGI 均存在文件写入路径遍历风险
Settings UI 状态管理缺陷导致 23 个仓库的配置项数据丢失，OpenDevin/OpenDevin 等核心项目受影响
Mem0 2.0 API breaking change 影响 9 个仓库的长期记忆功能，agentscope-ai/agentscope 等已确认中断
Anthropic 多 SDK（Go/Python/JS）streaming 路径存在系统性缺陷，code_execution 多轮循环被阻断（如 container 丢失、omitzero 丢弃零值字段、server_tool_use 事件未触发）

top_pain_points.review_reason: Security vulnerability with concrete exploit evidence. The path traversal flaw allows arbitrary file writes outside the intended upload directory (confirmed by /tmp/superagi_traversal_1.txt creation). With CVSS 9.1 and demonstrated ability to overwrite Python modules or system configs, this can lead to remote code execution. While only 1 issue, the severity is critical and the exploit is confirmed in the report — not theoretical.

signals.topic: Azure managed identity / Entra ID authentication causes server startup crash on AsyncEngine dispose
signals.summary: Self-hosted Phoenix (v14.8.0) crashes at startup with AttributeError when `PHOENIX_POSTGRES_USE_AZURE_MANAGED_IDENTITY` is enabled, because the code attempts to monkey-patch `engine.dispose` on a SQLAlchemy AsyncEngine which uses `__slots__` and marks dispose as read-only. Two independent reporters both stuck — no workaround exists.
signals.review_reason: Two independent self-hosted users (different reporters, same day) hit an identical server startup crash when enabling Azure managed identity for PostgreSQL. This is a hard block — the Phoenix server fails to start entirely with no workaround. Severity meets P0 despite count=2 because the crash is at the earliest point of the main flow (server boot), and both reporters are actively blocked with no viable alternative. The `__slots__` restriction in SQLAlchemy's AsyncEngine makes this a systemic design flaw for any Azure cloud deployment scenario.

signals.summary: When viewing traces in Phoenix, the dashboard overview page shows token counts that are exactly 3x higher than the detailed trace breakdown and framework logs. For one example run: detailed trace = 2,952 tokens vs. overview = 8,856 tokens. This directly inflates cost estimates and makes per-run token metrics unreliable.
aliases: Token count triple counting in dashboard
signals.review_reason: Token usage overcounting by exactly 3x is a data accuracy defect that directly affects cost reporting and metrics-driven decisions. The user provides reproducible steps with exact numbers, comparing three independent sources (detailed trace, framework logs, overview). The bug is reproducible and consistent across runs, indicating a systemic aggregation logic error in Phoenix's dashboard. This is not a UI cosmetic issue — it causes measurable cost inflation for any user relying on Phoenix token metrics for billing or budget tracking.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: Dashboard overview triple-counts token usage compared to trace view and framework logs
source_issues.evidence: User provides concrete numbers showing exact 3x inflation: detailed trace total = 2,952 tokens, step totals = 314+1,183+1,455, overview total = 8,856 (ratio = 3.0). smolagents console logs agree with the lower number. Ratio remains constant regardless of step count, indicating nested span aggregation duplication.

signals.topic: Desktop AppImage on Linux crashes on startup — config schema incompatibility and missing provider setup

Users cannot start the desktop app at all.

signals.topic: gptme-eval silently leaks user-level prompt config into benchmark runs, causing eval false negatives
signals.summary: gptme-eval inherits the user's global config (~/.config/gptme/config.toml) including [prompt] files and user context, which pollutes eval runs. A user with 'files = ["~/work/my-notes.md"]' causes models to write output to paths from their notes instead of the eval workspace, making evals fail on environment leakage rather than actual capability.
signals.review_reason: P1: User config pollution causes eval false negatives — benchmark results are meaningless because environment leakage determines pass/fail rather than model capability. Affects any user running gptme-eval with non-empty user config, silently producing incorrect benchmark data.

source_issues.title: gptme-eval leaks user-level prompt config into eval runs
source_issues.evidence: Observed on gptme v0.31.0 with Qwen3.6-35b: model wrote hello.py to /home/bob/bob/ instead of eval workspace due to absolute path in leaked user config file. When path is removed, model gets it right. Evals are non-reproducible across users with different configs.

signals.topic: WebUI/server fails to handle multi-tool-per-message for capable models, causing undefined tool execution behavior
signals.summary: After #1724 made break_on_tooluse=False the default for capable models (Sonnet 4.5+, Opus 4.6+, GPT-4o/5), the webui/server path (session_step.py) was not updated to handle multiple tool uses in a single assistant message. Three bugs: (1) _start_step_thread fires after each tool ignoring remaining pending tools, (2) call_id not propagated to tool result messages, (3) undefined tool execution ordering. The code even contains an explicit warning about this.
signals.review_reason: P1: WebUI multi-tool execution is broken for capable models, which are now the default behavior. Users of Sonnet 4.6+/Opus 4.6+ via webui experience undefined tool ordering and broken tool-call/results pairing. Not P0 because the CLI path works correctly and workarounds exist.

source_issues.title: webui/server: multi-tool-per-message broken when break_on_tooluse=False (regression after #1724)
source_issues.evidence: Explicit warning in code at session_step.py:L705-708 'Multiple tools per message not yet supported, expect issues'. Three concrete bugs with code references identified. Default behavior change in #1724 means all users with capable models (Sonnet 4.6+, Opus 4.6+) are affected.

This is a main-flow UX failure even with count=1, because the severity and user impact are clearly documented.

signals.topic: File Upload Endpoint Path Traversal Vulnerability Allowing Arbitrary File Write
signals.summary: The /resources/upload endpoint in superagi/controllers/resources.py has a path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22, CVSS 9.1) where user-supplied filenames are used without sanitization, allowing attackers to write files to arbitrary server locations and potentially achieve RCE.
signals.review_reason: Security vulnerability with concrete exploit evidence. The path traversal flaw allows arbitrary file writes outside the intended upload directory (confirmed by /tmp/superagi_traversal_1.txt creation). With CVSS 9.1 and demonstrated ability to overwrite Python modules or system configs, this can lead to remote code execution. While only 1 issue, the severity is critical and the exploit is confirmed in the report — not theoretical.

source_issues.title: File Upload Path Traversal Vulnerability in /resources/upload Endpoint Allows Arbitrary File Write
source_issues.evidence: Attacker can craft filenames with '../' or absolute paths to escape upload directory. Proof of concept confirms file written to /tmp/superagi_traversal_1.txt (outside intended directory). CVSS 9.1 critical. Can overwrite Python modules, config files, or system files leading to RCE.

signals.topic: DeepResearchAgent crashes with KeyError when model returns thinking block before text block

The result is an erroneous 'Error: text' tool output and complete failure of the research agent.
signals.review_reason: DeepResearchAgent crashes (KeyError + AttributeError) when encountering model outputs it doesn't expect, blocking the core research workflow. Two distinct crash modes both in DeepResearchAgent._acting with clear stack traces. These are not edge cases; they fail reliably when certain model response formats are encountered.

source_issues.title: [Bug]:AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get' in DeepResearchAgent._acting
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace: AttributeError at deep_research_agent.py line 341. chunk.metadata is None but code calls chunk.metadata.get('success') without null check. Closed with fix.

signals.topic: Mem0 2.0 API breaking change causes Mem0LongTermMemory to fail
signals.summary: After upgrading mem0ai from 1.x to 2.0, Mem0LongTermMemory's retrieve() method fails because mem0ai 2.0 changed the search() API: top-level user_id/agent_id/run_id parameters are no longer supported and must be wrapped in a filters dictionary. This completely breaks the long-term memory retrieval feature for users who upgrade mem0ai.
aliases: Mem0LongTermMemory retrieve failure after mem0ai upgrade
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-impacting bug: upgrading mem0ai to 2.0 causes the Mem0LongTermMemory feature to completely fail on every retrieval call, returning a clear API error. Users are blocked from using long-term memory with newer mem0ai versions.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Mem0 2.0 API breaking change causes Mem0LongTermMemory to fail in AgentScope
source_issues.evidence: Error message: 'Top-level entity parameters frozenset({"user_id", "run_id", "agent_id"}) are not supported in search(). Use filters={"user_id": "..."} instead.' The retrieve() method throws this error on every call after upgrading mem0ai to 2.0.

signals.topic: vLLM deployment ReActAgent tool calls fail with 'No user query found in messages' error
signals.summary: When using AgentScope's ReActAgent with a locally deployed vLLM server (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B), the agent crashes with a 400 BadRequestError: 'No user query found in messages.' This blocks the entire agent workflow when using local vLLM deployments with tool-calling enabled.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked: ReActAgent completely fails when used with local vLLM deployments that have tool-calling enabled, returning a 400 BadRequestError. Users cannot run their agent workflows with local vLLM models.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: vllm部署的在线API调用时出现 No user query found in messages.
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows openai.BadRequestError 400 with message 'No user query found in messages.' The error occurs in _reasoning() at the model call stage, crashing the entire ReActAgent workflow. 2 comments from other users confirming the issue.

signals.topic: Critical path traversal vulnerabilities in insert_text_file and write_text_file allow arbitrary file write
signals.summary: The file operation functions insert_text_file and write_text_file in AgentScope contain critical path traversal vulnerabilities (CVSS 9.1, CWE-22). They accept arbitrary file paths without validation, allowing any file write anywhere on the host system. The vulnerability was confirmed with real LLM (MiniMax API) + real ReActAgent execution where the agent autonomously generated path traversal attacks.
signals.review_reason: This is a critical security vulnerability with confirmed real-world exploitation via actual LLM agent execution. Arbitrary file writes on the host system can lead to data destruction, backdoor installation, and full host compromise. The vulnerability affects all AgentScope versions and all OS platforms. It directly impacts users who expose ReActAgent with file tools in any environment.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Two Path Traversal in File Operations
source_issues.evidence: CVSS 9.1, CWE-22. Confirmed with real LLM (MiniMax API) + real ReActAgent execution. Attacker LLM autonomously generated and executed path traversal payloads ('Insert PWNED into ../../../../tmp/agentscope_exploit.txt'), writing arbitrary content outside the intended workspace. No validation in vulnerable functions.

signals.topic: glm-5 model CompressionConfig causes ValueError and breaks agent execution
signals.summary: When using glm-5 model with CompressionConfig enabled (memory compression in ReActAgent), the agent crashes with ValueError: 'expected value at line 1 column 1'. The compression feature fails, causing the entire fallback chain to fail and the agent stream to error out. Users lose both the compression feature and the ability to run the agent.
signals.review_reason: Users who enable memory compression (CompressionConfig) with glm-5 model experience a crash that breaks the entire agent execution flow. The error cascades through the fallback chain, making both the compression feature and the agent unusable. This is a real user-facing workflow failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]:glm-5 model enable CompressionConfig Compression failed
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace: ValueError: 'expected value at line 1 column 1' in _compress_memory_if_needed(). This propagates to a RuntimeError: 'All 2 models in fallback chain failed', causing the entire agent stream to error out. Error occurs in _agent_stream_generator.

signals.topic: Claude Haiku/Sonnet via AWS emit false 'does not support structured outputs' warnings despite functional structured outputs
signals.summary: AWS Bedrock Claude Haiku/Sonnet models emit misleading warnings about structured output incompatibility even though structured outputs work correctly. This was introduced in v2.5.17 and regression from v2.5.9.
signals.review_reason: 用户使用 AWS Bedrock 上的 Claude Haiku/Sonnet 时持续看到误导性 WARNING 日志，即使 structured outputs 功能实际正常可用。此问题在 v2.5.17 引入（v2.5.9 无此问题），导致用户无法判断 structured output 是否真正生效，产生认知负担和日志噪音，虽不阻断但显著影响体验。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Model does not support structured outputs WARNING
source_issues.evidence: Users get WARNING logs 'Model does not support structured outputs' for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Haiku via AWS Bedrock, even though structured outputs work correctly. This is a regression from v2.5.9 and generates misleading noise in logs for users relying on structured output features.

signals.topic: InputCheckError exception cannot be properly raised/caught in input validation pre-hooks, breaking documented feature
signals.summary: Following the official docs for input validation pre-hook, InputCheckError cannot be caught by the documented except block. The exception is printed instead of being raised, breaking the expected control flow.
signals.review_reason: InputCheckError 是官方文档明确记录的功能，用户按文档使用却无法工作——异常被打印而非抛出，导致用户无法实现输入验证阻断逻辑。这直接违反文档承诺，属于主流程功能不可用。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Cannot raise InputCheckError
source_issues.evidence: 用户严格按照官方文档配置 input validation pre-hook，但 InputCheckError 无法被 except 语句捕获，而是被直接打印输出。错误日志显示 'ERROR Validation failed' 而非预期的异常抛出，导致用户无法按文档方式处理非法输入，主流程被阻断。

signals.topic: Gemini unknown exception handling loses error details in wrapped ModelProviderError, hindering debugging
signals.summary: Gemini model wraps generic exceptions (e.g. asyncio.TimeoutError) with ModelProviderError where str(e) may be empty, resulting in logs like 'Unknown error from Gemini API:' with no actionable information.
signals.review_reason: Gemini 请求异常时错误信息被吞没，用户在生产环境中无法从日志定位根因（超时？网络？API？），导致调试效率显著下降。虽然不直接阻断，但严重影响生产可观测性。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Gemini unknown exception handling loses error details in wrapped `ModelProviderError`
source_issues.evidence: Gemini 请求失败时，通用异常被包装为 ModelProviderError，但 str(e) 可能为空，导致日志仅显示 'Unknown error from Gemini API:' 而无任何可操作信息，使工作流/流式调用路径的根因调试极为困难。

signals.topic: Gemini timeout configuration ignored when http_options is set via client_params
signals.summary: When Gemini model is configured with both timeout and client_params containing http_options (as HttpOptions object), self.timeout is never applied. Requests use the default long connect timeout (120s) instead of the configured value.
signals.review_reason: 用户配置的 timeout 参数在特定组合下完全失效，请求不会按预期快速超时，在网络受限/边缘场景下导致资源浪费和不可预期的长等待，虽非全面阻断但影响明确。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Gemini timeout is ignored when http_options is set via client_params
source_issues.evidence: 用户显式配置 Gemini model timeout=0.1s 以便快速失败，但当同时使用 client_params={'http_options': HttpOptions(...)} 时，timeout 被忽略，请求仍使用默认 120s 超时。在网络受限环境中，这意味着慢请求不会按预期快速超时，导致资源浪费和响应延迟。

signals.topic: Team.add_learnings_to_context flag is silently ignored; LearningMachine context never injected into Team system prompt across sessions
signals.summary: Team accepts add_learnings_to_context=True but the flag is never read in Team's system message builder. LearningMachine stored user profiles are never injected into Team's system prompt, breaking cross-session memory for Teams while working correctly for Agent.
signals.review_reason: Team 的 learning 功能写路径正常但读路径完全缺失，导致跨 session 记忆失效。用户按官方文档配置 LearningMachine，第一 session 存储的信息在第二 session 完全丢失，而相同配置在 Agent 下正常。官方 cookbook 示例因此无法工作，影响多 session 场景下的核心记忆功能。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Team.add_learnings_to_context flag is never read; LearningMachine context is never injected into Team system prompt
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用 Team 配置了 LearningMachine(user_profile)，第一 session 调用 update_profile 成功写入数据库，但第二 session Team 完全忘记用户信息。相同配置在 Agent 下正常工作，证明是 Team 端的读路径缺失。add_learnings_to_context=True 参数完全无效，官方 cookbook 示例 'cookbook/03_teams/memory/learning_machine.py' 整体失效。

signals.topic: TUI crashes with black screen when session's working directory no longer exists
signals.summary: When resuming a session whose working directory has been deleted or renamed, the TUI crashes and the terminal PTY becomes invalid, resulting in a black screen. No graceful fallback is provided.
signals.review_reason: Clear main workflow blocker: session resume is a primary use case, and the crash completely destroys the terminal state (PTY corruption). The only workaround requires recreating the original directory, which is unacceptable UX.

source_issues.title: TUI crashes with black screen when opening session whose working directory no longer exists
source_issues.evidence: TUI crashes with PTY EBADF (errno 9) after ~15-22s, resulting in complete black screen. The session is bound to its original working directory and crashes regardless of where the command is invoked. Only workaround is to recreate the original directory.

signals.topic: Windows: /exit command regression freezes Hyper and Alacritty terminals, force-closes PowerShell
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.14.19, the /exit command no longer exits cleanly on Hyper Terminal (freezes, must Task Manager kill) and PowerShell standalone (force-closes). VS Code Terminal and Windows Terminal are unaffected. Regression confirmed via downgrade to v1.14.18.
signals.review_reason: Regression in a recent release that breaks a fundamental command (/exit) used at the end of every session. Users are forced to force-kill the terminal, losing state. Clear downgrade evidence confirms the regression was introduced in v1.14.19.

source_issues.title: Regression on Windows: /exit freezes Hyper and alacritty terminal and force-closes PowerShell in v1.14.19, but works in v1.14.18
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: v1.14.18 exits cleanly, v1.14.19 freezes Hyper/Alacritty and force-closes PowerShell. Downgrade resolves issue. Multiple terminals affected (Hyper, Alacritty, PowerShell).

signals.topic: Windows handle leak in sidecar process causes desktop app freeze and resource exhaustion
signals.summary: On Windows 11, the OpenCode Desktop sidecar process leaks handles (HND) from ~355 to 7,000-12,000+ and connections from 32 to 287+ within ~90 seconds during active message processing. Health endpoint becomes unresponsive and the desktop UI freezes.
signals.review_reason: Windows-specific resource exhaustion during active usage: handles and connections grow rapidly, making the health endpoint unresponsive and the desktop app freeze. Strong evidence with Process Monitor data and multi-instance reproduction, though limited to Windows 11.

source_issues.title: Windows: Sidecar handle leak causes desktop freeze + persistent server polling errors
source_issues.evidence: Process Monitor data shows HND: 355→4,629 in 107s, CONN: 41→131. Health endpoint returns ERR. Frontend shows 'error sending request'. App becomes unresponsive during active usage. Reproduced across multiple sidecar instances.

signals.topic: workspace.create() always times out on Windows despite workspace being created successfully
signals.summary: On Windows, workspace.create() for local worktree workspaces always times out with 'Timed out waiting for global event' (~8 seconds) even though the workspace is fully created and functional. The API returns an error for a successful operation.
signals.review_reason: Workspace creation is a core workflow feature. The false-positive timeout error on Windows means users cannot reliably create workspaces through the API despite the operation succeeding, breaking automation and causing confusion. Root cause is clearly identified.

source_issues.title: workspace.create() always times out for local workspaces on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Workspace IS created successfully (git worktree exists, VCS initializes, file watcher starts), but /experimental/workspace returns UnknownError with timeout message after ~8s. Root cause identified as flag guard race and fire-and-forget async. Patched binary returns 200 OK in 4.1s.

signals.topic: Web UI: session changes fail to expand due to Content Security Policy blocking inline scripts
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.14.19, clicking on changed files in the web UI Review tab does not expand them. Console shows CSP violation: 'Executing inline script violates Content Security Policy directive'. This blocks the entire review workflow on the web interface.
aliases: review tab file expansion broken web
CSP blocks file expansion opencode web
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow blockage in the web UI: the Review tab (a core feature for inspecting agent changes) is entirely non-functional due to CSP misconfiguration. Affects both Firefox and Chrome. Clear regression from prior version.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Session Changes do not expand on click on web.
source_issues.evidence: CSP error blocks inline script execution. 'Expand All' and individual file expansion both fail. Reproduced on Firefox 150.0b10 and Chrome 147.0.x on Mac. Regression from v1.3.16 to v1.14.19.

signals.topic: CodeExecutionToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops zero-value fields causing 400 API errors in multi-turn agentic loops
signals.summary: CodeExecutionToolResultBlock.ToParam() 使用 omitzero JSON tag，导致 stdout/stderr/return_code 零值字段在重新序列化时被丢弃，API 返回 400 错误并阻断多轮 agentic loop。这是 #242、#317 同类系统性 ToParam() 模式缺陷的一部分。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户报告在生产多轮 agentic loop 中触发 400 API 错误，阻断 agent 继续执行。可靠复现，属于 #242、#317 同类的系统性 ToParam() omitzero 缺陷。

source_issues.title: CodeExecutionToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops stdout/stderr/return_code via omitzero (same class as #242, #317)
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在多轮 agentic loop 中，API 返回 400 错误: 'messages.21.content.1.code_execution_tool_result.content.RequestCodeExecutionToolResultError.type: Input should be code_execution_tool_result_error'。根本原因是 omitzero 导致零值字段被丢弃，API 无法识别请求。已在生产环境可靠复现（20+ tool calls 循环场景）。

signals.topic: Documentation examples use non-existent SDK types causing integration failures
signals.summary: 官方文档（platform.claude.com/docs）中的 Go 代码示例引用了不存在的 SDK 类型（如 BetaManagedAgentsUserDefineOutcomeEventParams、BetaManagedAgentsTextRubricParams 等），导致用户无法照着文档集成。
aliases: SDK types missing from Go docs
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：文档示例无法编译，用户无法参照文档完成集成，属于关键文档与 SDK 不匹配问题，直接影响新用户接入流程。

source_issues.title: Examples in documentation use types that don't exist.
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用 v1.35.1 时，参照官方文档示例代码发现 BetaSessionEventSendParams、anthropic.BetaManagedAgentsUserDefineOutcomeEventParams、BetaManagedAgentsTextRubricParams 等类型不存在，无法编译运行。

signals.topic: Java SDK structured output schema generator ignores @Nullable annotations and Optional, marking all fields as required, causing LLM hallucination
signals.summary: The Java SDK's internal schema generator for StructuredOutput always places all Java record/class fields into the JSON Schema `required` array, ignoring @Nullable annotations, @JsonProperty(required=false), and java.util.Optional. This forces the LLM to hallucinate values (string 'null', empty strings, dashes) to satisfy required constraints, degrading structured output quality.
signals.review_reason: Issue #321 demonstrates a clear user-impacting bug: the Java SDK's StructuredOutput schema generator always marks all fields as required, ignoring @Nullable annotations and Optional types. This directly causes LLM hallucination of values (string 'null', empty strings, dashes) to satisfy schema constraints, degrading structured output quality — a core feature. Multiple workarounds (annotations, JsonProperty, Optional) all failed. This is a real functional defect affecting anyone using Java structured output with nullable fields, not merely a feature gap.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports LLM forced to hallucinate values (string 'null', empty strings, dashes) because all fields are marked required in generated JSON Schema. Multiple workarounds attempted (@Nullable annotation, @JsonProperty, Optional<T>) all failed. Schema generator defaults to strict/required for all fields due to missing Kotlin KType nullability metadata in Java classes.

signals.topic: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport, breaking Streamable HTTP-only servers (e.g. Apify)
signals.summary: Managed Agents (`client.beta.agents`) only implements SSE transport for MCP server connections, but Streamable HTTP is the current MCP spec. Apify deprecated SSE on 2026-04-01 and now returns 405, causing agents to fail at initialization with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON'. Agents silently fall back and never use the MCP server. Workaround unavailable on the client side.
aliases: Managed Agents MCP Streamable HTTP not supported
signals.review_reason: Two related issues both about Managed Agents MCP transport failure. #1383: entire MCP server (Apify) unusable since 2026-04-01 due to SSE-only transport. #1405: even when CMA falls back to Streamable HTTP successfully, tool call results are silently lost — agents report false errors while tools complete successfully. Both are workflow-blocking: users cannot use popular MCP servers (Apify) at all, and when a compatible server is used, results are silently swallowed. Critical path failure for Managed Agents feature.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE on April 1 2026. Agents fail at initialization with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON', fall back to other tools and never use Apify. No client-side workaround available.

source_issues.title: CMA: Tool call results silently lost when server returns 406 on GET /mcp SSE probe
source_issues.evidence: CMA sends GET /mcp before any session exists; server correctly returns 406 per MCP spec. Tool calls succeed server-side but results are silently lost in the relay — agent reports 'There was an error communicating with Snowflake' even though the tool ran successfully. Tool results silently lost.

signals.topic: Streaming `get_final_message()` missing `message_delta.container` breaks multi-turn code_execution tool loops
signals.summary: When using `AsyncAnthropic.messages.stream()` with `code_execution_20260120`, `stream.get_final_message().container` is `None` because the streaming aggregator never merges `delta.container` from `message_delta` SSE events. This causes `BadRequestError: 400 container_id is required` on the second turn of multi-turn tool-use loops. Workaround requires manual SSE parsing with `RawMessageDeltaEvent`.
aliases: streaming container field missing in get_final_message
signals.review_reason: Streaming aggregator is missing a critical field (`container`) that causes the second turn of multi-turn code_execution loops to fail with a 400 error. This is not a minor cosmetic issue — it breaks the primary workflow for streaming users who need code execution continuation. The data IS present on the wire (`message_delta` SSE event has `delta.container`), but the SDK silently drops it. Workaround of manual SSE parsing is brittle and defeats the purpose of the happy-path streaming API.

source_issues.title: `get_final_message()` does not propagate `message_delta.container` into aggregated Message (breaks code_execution continuation)
source_issues.evidence: Streaming aggregator in `lib/streaming/_messages.py` never merges `delta.container` into accumulated `Message`. `grep container` on the file returns zero non-import matches. Multi-turn tool loops with `code_execution_20260120` + streaming get `400 BadRequestError: container_id is required` on the second turn, breaking the primary use case.

signals.topic: Batch API returns intermittent 404 for `batches.retrieve()` and `batches.results()` causing application crashes
signals.summary: After successfully creating a message batch, `batches.retrieve()` and `batches.results()` intermittently return 404 Not Found due to server-side propagation delay. In Case 2, after `retrieve()` confirmed the batch as `ended`, calling `results()` triggers an internal `retrieve()` that crashes the application with `NotFoundError`, fully breaking batch result retrieval. Workarounds exist but require extra polling logic.
aliases: batches.results() crashes application with 404 after batch ended
signals.review_reason: The batch API is a primary workflow for processing large numbers of requests. When `batches.results()` crashes with 404 after the batch status was confirmed as `ended`, it fully breaks the result retrieval path — this is an application crash (not just an error), blocking the entire batch processing workflow. The fact that all three cases (create, retrieve, results) can return 404 at different points means there's no reliable path for batch processing.

source_issues.title: Intermittent `NotFoundError (404)` on Batch API
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct failure cases observed in same ~15-minute window. Case 2: `retrieve()` previously returned `ended`, then `results()` calls internal `retrieve()` which returns 404, crashing the application with a full traceback through `batches.results() → retrieve() → _make_status_error_from_response`. Application crash is directly triggered by SDK behavior.

signals.topic: Beta streaming accumulator silently drops `tool_search` and `web_fetch` result blocks from `get_final_message()`
signals.summary: `ParsedBetaContentBlock` union is missing `BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock` and `BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock` that exist in the sibling `BetaContentBlock` union. When the streaming accumulator encounters these block types, pydantic's discriminated-union resolution fails and the blocks are silently coerced or dropped. Users see empty results from `stream.get_final_message().content` despite data being present on the wire.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in the beta streaming API — result blocks are present on the wire but disappear from the aggregated message. This is not a transient error but a consistent type definition gap that makes `get_final_message()` return incomplete data. Users relying on `tool_search` or `web_fetch` tools in streaming mode get empty/missing results without any error, making debugging very difficult. Downgraded to P1 (not P0) because only affects beta API and there's no confirmed P0-level workflow block yet.

source_issues.title: ParsedBetaContentBlock union missing tool_search/web_fetch result blocks — stream accumulator drops them from get_final_message()
source_issues.evidence: Code comparison shows `BetaContentBlock` includes `BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock` and `BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock` but `ParsedBetaContentBlock` does not. Accumulator calls `construct_type(type_=ParsedBetaContentBlock, value=event.content_block.to_dict())` and pydantic silently drops mismatched blocks. Users observe `content_block_start` events in raw stream but the result block never appears in `get_final_message().content`.

signals.topic: Beta streaming does not fire `BetaInputJsonEvent` for `server_tool_use` blocks, blocking observable streaming input
signals.summary: `lib/streaming/_beta_messages.py` fires `BetaInputJsonEvent` for `tool_use` and `mcp_tool_use` content blocks but not for `server_tool_use`, despite the API streaming `input_json_delta` events for server tools. The accumulator correctly accumulates the streamed input into `content_block.input` but never fires the parsed event to consumers. Users must bypass the SDK's event helpers and match raw `BetaRawContentBlockDeltaEvent` with `BetaInputJSONDelta` delta.
aliases: streaming server tool input not observable via SDK helpers
signals.review_reason: Beta streaming consumers using `BetaInputJsonEvent` helpers cannot observe server-side tool input (`tool_search_tool_regex`, `web_search`) as it streams in — this is a feature gap in the streaming event model. While the accumulator itself works, the public event interface is incomplete, forcing users to use internal/unstable APIs as a workaround. This degrades the developer experience significantly for beta streaming users. Downgraded to P1 as it affects beta API and there's no crash or workflow block.

source_issues.title: BetaInputJsonEvent not fired for server_tool_use blocks during streaming
source_issues.evidence: Accumulator's `TRACKS_TOOL_INPUT` tuple correctly includes `BetaServerToolUseBlock`, meaning input is accumulated internally, but `BetaInputJsonEvent` is never fired because the event firing code only checks for `tool_use` and `mcp_tool_use`. Workaround requires matching on raw `BetaRawContentBlockDeltaEvent` with `BetaInputJSONDelta`, which is not part of the public API.

signals.topic: ProcessError stripped to generic Exception with hard-coded stderr placeholder, blocking programmatic error diagnosis
signals.summary: When CLI subprocess exits non-zero, ProcessError (with exit_code/stderr) is destroyed during propagation and re-raised as a bare Exception with literal 'Check stderr output for details'. Users cannot catch ProcessError, access exit_code, or retrieve real stderr output — making any CLI failure undebugable without SDK forking.
signals.review_reason: High-impact runtime blocking: every CLI subprocess failure (auth errors, invalid models, permission failures) results in opaque generic Exception with no stderr or exit_code. Users cannot programmatically diagnose failures. Directly caused multiple prior filed issues. The 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder is confirmed hard-coded literal — real stderr never captured. No workaround exists. This is a core SDK error-handling defect.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded "Check stderr output for details" placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Verified reproduction shows: caught type is generic Exception (not ProcessError), .exit_code and .stderr attributes absent, message is hard-coded literal 'Check stderr output for details' — actual CLI stderr never captured. Affects all users who run CLI subprocess failures (invalid model, auth errors, permission failures). Cited as root cause of multiple prior closed issues (#515, #282, #238). Triple defect in 3 files means no workaround exists.

signals.topic: Session resume fails with API 400 due to invalid tool_use.id format (contains '.' and ':')
signals.summary: During session resume, the SDK replays historical messages containing tool_use.id values in format 'functions.{ToolName}:{N}' (e.g. 'functions.AskUserQuestion:1'), which violate the API's pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$. The API rejects these with 400 error, blocking session resume entirely.
aliases: tool_use.id format violates API validation pattern
session resume broken by invalid ID format
signals.review_reason: Session resume is a documented core feature. Any session using tools generates invalid IDs that cause 100% failure on resume. This is a deterministic, reproducible feature blocker — users who complete sessions with tool calls cannot resume them. Clear API-level validation failure with exact error message.

source_issues.title: Invalid tool_use.id format during session resume causes API 400 error
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced: messages replayed verbatim during resume contain 'functions.AskUserQuestion:1' (with '.' and ':'), API returns 400 with validation error 'String should match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'. SDK-generated IDs for new calls are valid (call_xxxxxx format). Session resume is a core feature completely broken for any session that used tools with the SDK's current ID format.

signals.topic: Resource leak: unclosed anyio memory streams in Query.close() causing ResourceWarning
signals.summary: Query.close() cancels the task group and closes transport but never calls aclose() on _message_send and _message_receive (anyio MemoryObjectSendStream/MemoryObjectReceiveStream). This causes ResourceWarning under PYTHONDEVMODE. While a PR may address it, the issue exists in the current release.
aliases: anyio memory object stream not closed
signals.review_reason: Confirmed memory resource leak with reproducible script. Under PYTHONDEVMODE users will see warnings. In long-running agent systems (common SDK use case), unclosed stream objects accumulate. Not a crash but a definite resource leak with developer-visible evidence.

source_issues.title: Resource Leak: anyio memory object stream associated with a query is leaked
source_issues.evidence: Verified reproduction script with PYTHONDEVMODE=1 produces ResourceWarning for unclosed MemoryObjectReceiveStream and MemoryObjectSendStream. Root cause confirmed: aclose() not called on self._message_send or self._message_receive in Query.close(). Leads to resource accumulation in long-running agent systems.

signals.topic: PostToolUse hook with updatedMCPToolOutput crashes renderer with JavaScript H.reduce is not a function
signals.summary: When a PostToolUse hook returns a valid updatedMCPToolOutput, the Claude.ai renderer crashes with 'H.reduce is not a function' and marks all tools as failed. Python-side hook executes correctly and logs proper output — crash is in the JS rendering layer after the hook returns.
aliases: H.reduce is not a function MCP
signals.review_reason: Confirmed renderer crash with full reproduction code.
