Python hook executes correctly (confirmed in logs) but the rendered output causes a JS crash, making all tool results appear failed. This directly breaks the PostToolUse hook workflow — a key extensibility feature. Additionally, docs/runtime inconsistency on tool_response structure adds developer confusion.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes H.reduce is not a function in renderer despite correct hook output
source_issues.evidence: Python hook logs confirm correct execution and proper output shape (content array with text blocks). Renderer crashes with JS error H.reduce is not a function — in H.reduce((_,$)=>_+($.type==='text'?$.text.length:0),0). All three MCP tools reported as failed in the UI. Separate finding: tool_response structure inconsistent between docs (dict with content key) and runtime (bare list), adding to developer confusion.

signals.topic: ClaudeAgentOptions.effort types outdated and CLI validation failures surfaced as opaque ProcessError
signals.summary: The effort type Literal only includes ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'max'] but current CLI supports 'xhigh'. When users pass unsupported effort values, failure is opaque generic ProcessError (linking to pp-001). Type errors may also deter Python devs from using newer effort levels.
signals.review_reason: Two-compound issue: (1) outdated type definitions block legitimate CLI capability through type checkers, and (2) validation failures chain into pp-001's opaque ProcessError. Combined effect is user cannot discover or use 'xhigh' effort level. Lower priority than pp-001 as it's specific to one option rather than all CLI failures.

source_issues.title: ClaudeAgentOptions.effort typings are outdated, and CLI validation failures are surfaced as opaque ProcessError
source_issues.evidence: Type definition in claude_agent_sdk/types.py only has 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'max' but CLI help shows 'low, medium, high, xhigh, max'. Users attempting 'xhigh' get opaque ProcessError (confirming pp-001). Type mismatch means Python type checkers block legitimate use.

signals.topic: Session resume (query resume) silently drops tool_use/tool_result pairs from conversation history on long sessions, causing duplicate external side effects
signals.summary: When resuming a session via query({resume}), tool_use and tool_result entries from earlier turns are silently dropped while text content is preserved. This causes agents to duplicate side-effecting actions (file uploads, external API writes, database mutations) on resume because their prior successful actions are invisible.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow failure for any agent using tools to mutate external state. When a session resumes (container reboot, process restart), prior tool calls are silently dropped from context. The agent proceeds to re-execute those actions, creating duplicate database records, file uploads, and API writes. The impact is concrete and measurable: observed duplicate records in production. This is not a feature gap—it is a data-integrity failure in the core session-resume mechanism that the SDK explicitly provides.

source_issues.title: query({resume}) silently drops tool_use/tool_result sequences from earlier turns when session JSONL grows large
source_issues.evidence: Agents duplicate external side effects (duplicate notebook source, duplicate cloud-storage folder, duplicate file upload) after session resume. Tool_use/tool_result pairs absent from reconstructed context; user/assistant text preserved. Observed across 6+ boots on 1.8MB JSONL session.

signals.topic: SDK writes assistant JSONL entries with dangling parentUuid references, corrupting parent chain and causing session resume to return only the last assistant turn
signals.summary: The SDK writes assistant entries with parentUuid referencing UUIDs that never appear as entry uuid in the session JSONL file. On cold resume, the parent-chain walker stops at the first dangling reference, collapsing history to only the tail of the conversation.
signals.review_reason: This is a core session-state corruption issue that breaks the SDK's own session resume contract. When the SDK writes parentUuid references that cannot be resolved in the JSONL file, resume walks an incomplete parent chain and returns a truncated conversation. The user-visible result is 'entire session context gone after switch'—a complete context-loss failure. This affects any multi-turn session relying on cold resume, which is a primary SDK use case.

source_issues.title: SDK writes assistant entries with parentUuid referencing UUIDs not present in the transcript file
source_issues.evidence: On model switch triggering container restart, entire session context is lost after resume—user messages disappear from reconstructed history. Verified via grep that UUIDs appear only as parentUuid targets, never as entry uuid values. Conversation tree collapses to tail.

signals.topic: SDK initialization race: first user message written to CLI stdin before initialization completes, breaking prompt cache and reducing cache hit rate from ~100% to ~82%
signals.summary: The SDK sends the first user message to Claude Code CLI's stdin before awaiting the initialization acknowledgment. This causes the first API call to lack SDK MCP tools, making tools[] differ between Turn 1 and Turn 2 and breaking Anthropic's prompt cache on Turn 2.
signals.review_reason: This causes measurable cost degradation: prompt cache hit rate drops from ~100% to ~82%, meaning users pay significantly more per token on Turn 2 and all subsequent turns. The root cause is clearly identified (missing await in Rv function) and reproducible. The impact is ongoing for every session start, making this a persistent cost leak for SDK users.

source_issues.title: Rv writes user message without awaiting A.initialization, causing stdin race at CLI
source_issues.evidence: Measured cache read rate dropped from ~100% to ~82% due to MCP tools missing on Turn 1. Traced to Rv function in assistant.mjs not awaiting A.initialization before writing user payload. A one-line fix (await A.initialization) identified.

signals.topic: Linux CLI auto-discovery resolves musl binary before glibc, causing ENOENT spawn failure with misleading 'native binary not found' error
signals.summary: On Linux systems where both musl and glibc platform packages are installed (common with pnpm), the SDK resolver picks the musl variant first, causing a spawn failure because musl-linked ELF cannot execute on glibc. The error message 'Claude Code native binary not found' is misleading since the file exists and is readable.
signals.review_reason: This is a startup failure that blocks the primary SDK workflow (query()) on a common Linux setup. pnpm installing all optional deps for the current CPU is a documented behavior that leaves both musl and glibc packages on disk. The SDK then picks the wrong one and fails with a misleading error message. The user impact is complete SDK failure on startup, which is a P0-level blocker by nature of the signal, though frequency is single-issue.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: On Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) with both platform packages installed via pnpm, query() fails with misleading 'Claude Code native binary not found'. The musl binary exists and is readable but cannot execute due to missing dynamic loader. The glibc variant works correctly. Workaround requires manually specifying pathToClaudeCodeExecutable.

signals.topic: Bundled cli.js IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback failure causes Vertex AI OAuth token refresh to hang on dual-stack networks with non-routable IPv6
signals.summary: The bundled cli.js uses undici as HTTP client. On dual-stack networks where IPv6 ULA addresses are present (e.g., Tailscale) but IPv6 is not routable to Google, undici's autoSelectFamily fails to fall back to IPv4. This hangs OAuth token refresh for Vertex AI, making chat messages fail with empty error while other features work.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the primary chat workflow for Vertex AI users on any network with IPv6 ULA addresses (common with Tailscale, VPNs). OAuth token refresh hangs, making chat messages fail entirely while non-authenticated features work fine. The error message is empty and misleading. Users have no SDK-level workaround without patching Node internals.

source_issues.title: Bundled cli.js fails IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on dual-stack networks
source_issues.evidence: On macOS with Tailscale running (provides fd7a:: IPv6 ULA), OAuth token refresh to Google hangs indefinitely. Verified: Node native https module falls back to IPv4 correctly; undici fetch fails with ETIMEDOUT. Chat messages fail; sessions list, calendar, and UI work. Workarounds include local DNS resolver stripping AAAA records or NODE_OPTIONS preload script patching dns.lookup.

signals.topic: Model thinking config incompatibility causing silent success with no output (Sonnet) or immediate API error (Opus)
signals.summary: Sonnet 4.6 enters an empty-turn retry loop and exits as 'success' with zero artifacts after ~20 minutes; Opus 4.7 throws an immediate API error 'thinking.type.enabled is not supported'. Both stem from thinking configuration parameters being incompatible with specific models.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Sonnet 4.6 退出码为 success 但零产出，CI 误报通过；Opus 4.7 直接 API 错误无法运行。两例均为模型侧 thinking 配置不兼容，action 均无感知/告警，workflow 层面无法区分正常完成与静默失败。count=2，虽未达3但双模型双版本均可复现，用户影响证据充分（误导性 CI 结果、浪费 20 分钟算力）。

source_issues.title: claude-sonnet-4-6 silent-fails with repeated empty turns (stop_reason: null, output_tokens: 8)
source_issues.evidence: Sonnet 4.6 loops at ~2-3 empty turns/sec for ~20 minutes then exits 'success' with no commits, no branch, no result payload. CI reports pass while workflow silently produced nothing.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.7 not working with latest action v1.0.97
source_issues.evidence: Opus 4.7 immediately fails with API error 'thinking.type.enabled is not supported for this model'. Action terminates without processing.

signals.topic: install.sh silently fails on self-hosted runners with restricted network access (no internet to claude.ai), causing bundled Claude binary to be bypassed and runtime crash
signals.summary: In v1.0.100, the install script silently fails (curl SSL error exits 0) when claude.ai is unreachable, and the bundled platform binary fallback was removed, causing a 'native binary not found' crash at runtime.
aliases: install script fails silently in air-gapped/corporate firewall environments
bundled Claude binary fallback removed in v1.0.100
signals.review_reason: v1.0.100 引入的回归：自托管 runner 在企业防火墙环境下（npm 可达但 claude.ai 不可达）安装静默失败，action 误报成功后运行时崩溃，完全阻断该场景下的使用。count=1 但属于明确阻断性回归（regression），有明确 issue 和根因分析，用户影响证据充分（无任何 workaround）。

source_issues.title: v1.0.100 breaks environments where claude.ai is unreachable (install.sh silently fails, SDK bundled binary bypassed)
source_issues.evidence: Self-hosted runners in corporate firewall environments where npm is accessible but claude.ai is not: install.sh curl fails silently (exits 0 despite SSL error), action reports 'installed successfully', then crashes with 'ReferenceError: Claude Code native binary not found'. Prior to v1.0.100 the bundled SDK binary was used as fallback and worked.

signals.topic: Git authentication fails when actions/checkout uses persist-credentials: false, blocking security-hardened workflows
signals.summary: The action runs git fetch before setting up its own credentials, so when persist-credentials: false is set on the checkout step, the fetch fails with 'could not read Username', blocking users from following zizmor's security recommendation.
aliases: checkout persist-credentials: false causes git fetch to fail
zizmor artipacked security recommendation incompatible with claude-code-action
signals.review_reason: 安全加固（persist-credentials: false）与 action 不可兼得，迫使用户放弃 zizmor 推荐的安全最佳实践。虽然 count=1，但属于安全相关阻断，且有清晰的企业安全背景，不可降为 P2。

source_issues.title: claude-code-action fails when actions/checkout uses persist-credentials: false
source_issues.evidence: When checkout step uses persist-credentials: false (security hardening recommended by zizmor's 'artipacked' audit to prevent GITHUB_TOKEN leakage), the action's setupBranch runs git fetch before its own auth is configured, resulting in 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com'. Users must choose between security hardening and using the action.

signals.topic: Bun runtime internal error 'directory mismatch' crashes action on every workflow run, blocking all PRs in affected repos
signals.summary: On GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners, the action crashes with a Bun internal error 'directory mismatch for directory' during action setup, before any user code runs. Every invocation of v1 action fails, blocking green CI.
aliases: Bun internal error directory mismatch crash on GitHub-hosted runners
Bun runtime crash during action setup
signals.review_reason: Bun 运行时内部错误在 action 初始化阶段崩溃，导致受影响仓库的所有 PR CI 均失败，属于主流程阻断。count=1 但影响范围明确（所有 GitHub-hosted runner），用户影响证据充分（每 PR 必现）。

source_issues.title: Bun: Internal error 'directory mismatch for directory' in v1 action on GitHub-hosted runners
source_issues.evidence: Every invocation of v1 action fails on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest with Bun internal error 'directory mismatch for directory /home/runner/work/_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action/v1/tsconfig.json'. The review job fails on every PR, blocking green CI for repos that require all checks to pass.

signals.topic: Bedrock provider returns 400 error because action sends unsupported output_config.effort parameter, blocking AWS Bedrock users
signals.summary: When using Amazon Bedrock with an Application Inference Profile, the action sends output_config.effort which Bedrock rejects with 'Extra inputs are not permitted', causing immediate API error and zero-token processing.
signals.review_reason: Bedrock 作为主要云提供商之一，output_config.effort 参数不兼容导致该路径完全不可用，API 直接返回 400 错误并退出，属阻断性错误。count=1 但为明确阻断且有完整复现步骤。

source_issues.title: Bedrock: 400 error - output_config.effort: Extra inputs are not permitted
source_issues.evidence: Bedrock users with Application Inference Profiles get immediate 'API Error: 400 output_config.effort: Extra inputs are not permitted'. Action exits with code 1, processing zero tokens. This blocks the entire AWS Bedrock integration use case.

signals.topic: Custom MCP server tools fail to discover/load after updating to Claude Code 2.1.116
signals.summary: After updating to 2.1.116, custom MCP servers show as connected but their tools are not loaded into the deferred tools registry, making them inaccessible. Also affects HTTP MCP servers returning 405 on GET health check — tools from spec-compliant servers are silently skipped.
signals.review_reason: Multiple independent users report MCP tool discovery and loading failures across different scenarios: regression from 2.1.116 update, spec-compliant HTTP servers blocked by health check, Slack messages with bot content appearing empty, and inconsistent behavior across platforms. This is a high-frequency (count=4), multi-vector failure blocking a core extensibility feature used by paying users. Direct evidence of tools not appearing despite server connectivity.

source_issues.title: Custom MCP server tools not discovered after update to 2.1.116
source_issues.evidence: Custom MCP server shows 'Connected' in claude mcp list but ToolSearch returns 'No matching deferred tools found' for all custom server tools. Manual JSON-RPC confirms server exposes 50+ tools. Regression from 2.1.116.

source_issues.title: HTTP MCP servers returning 405 on GET health check fail to load tools at session startup
source_issues.evidence: Spec-compliant HTTP MCP servers (e.g., Datadog MCP) only accept POST, not GET. GET returns 405 and tools are silently skipped. Manual POST test returns 200 OK with valid session ID — server works but is blocked by health check.

source_issues.title: slack_read_channel / slack_read_thread drop message attachments and blocks
source_issues.evidence: Slack tools only return top-level text field. Messages from CI bots, alerting systems, and monitoring tools store entire payload in attachments/blocks and appear completely empty. Users miss critical bot messages entirely.

source_issues.title: Tools of a custom MCP server are visible on claude.ai/code but not via Claude Code in mobile app
source_issues.evidence: Custom MCP server tools work on desktop web claude.ai/code but are invisible in sessions initiated from the mobile app on Android. Same MCP server, different surface gives different results. Users cannot access custom MCP tools on mobile.

signals.topic: Windows installation script fails due to SSL certificate error — blocks Claude Code from being installed
signals.summary: On fresh Windows VMs with up-to-date patches, the install script (irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1) fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' when fetching the latest release. The script exits with misleading 'Installation complete!' despite failure. Regression from 2.1.92.
signals.review_reason: Single but well-documented case with clear reproduction steps. The issue blocks new Windows users from installing Claude Code entirely, and additionally reports a misleading success message that hides the failure. Regression from 2.1.92. While count=1 prevents P0, the install-time blocking nature with clear root cause and workaround (UseBasicParsing) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Fail to Fetch Latest Release from Install Script
source_issues.evidence: Fresh Windows VM with latest patches. Script fails with 'unable to get local issuer certificate' when fetching from downloads.claude.ai. Script exits with 'Installation complete!' even though nothing was installed. Regression from 2.1.92. Microsoft security patch KB5018702 changed Invoke-WebRequest behavior to require -UseBasicParsing on untrusted cert chains.

signals.topic: VS Code extension fails on every query with 'Query closed before response received' on Windows 11
signals.summary: VS Code extension 2.1.116 fails immediately on every query with 'Query closed before response received'. Terminal CLI works perfectly on the same machine. Failure is isolated to the VS Code extension subprocess IPC on this Windows 11 configuration.
signals.review_reason: While marked as duplicate (likely related to a parent issue), the evidence shows a consistent, reproducible failure that blocks the primary use case of the VS Code extension on a specific Windows 11 configuration. Terminal CLI works, proving the issue is specific to the VS Code extension IPC layer.

source_issues.title: VS Code extension 2.1.116 'Query closed before response received' on Windows 11
source_issues.evidence: Every query in VS Code extension immediately fails with 'Query closed before response received'. Terminal CLI on the same machine works perfectly. Reproduced across VS Code 1.98 and 1.99.0 with fresh extension installs. Workspace-independent. IPC connection closes unexpectedly. Subprocess exit code 1.

signals.topic: Claude Code desktop app crashes immediately on startup in Code mode (exit code 1)
signals.summary: Claude Code desktop app crashes with exit code 1 on every attempt to use Code mode on macOS. Chat mode works fine. Terminal version works fine. The crash leaves no crash logs in Console.app, making diagnosis difficult. Multiple diagnostic steps (full disk access, clean reinstall, deleting ~/.claude) did not resolve the issue.
signals.review_reason: Desktop app crash blocking the primary Code mode feature on a specific macOS configuration. Chat mode and terminal both work, isolating the issue to the desktop app's Code mode execution context. The lack of crash logs compounds the problem — users cannot diagnose or work around it.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude Code desktop app crashes on startup in Code mode with exit code 1
source_issues.evidence: iMac 24-inch 2024, Apple M4, macOS 15.7.5. Desktop app crashes immediately on Code mode startup (exit code 1). Chat mode works. Terminal version works. Full disk access granted, clean reinstall, deleted ~/.claude, OAuth re-authenticated — crash persists. No crash logs in Console.app.

signals.topic: API stream idle timeout causes partial response loss and blocks paying users
signals.summary: Users on Max plan ($900+ spent in 4 months) experience 'Stream idle timeout - partial response received' errors in both Claude Code and claude.ai web. Work is lost mid-generation. Affects both the CLI and web interface.
signals.review_reason: Labeled as duplicate, indicating this is a known recurring issue affecting paying users. The stream timeout error causes partial response loss and blocks completion of work. High monetary impact ($900 in 4 months) with frequent timeouts represents a critical service quality issue for paying customers.

source_issues.title: [BUG] API Error: Stream idle timeout - partial response received
source_issues.evidence: User is on Max plan, paid $900 to Anthropic in 4 months. Repeatedly gets 'Stream idle timeout - partial response received' in both Claude Code and claude.ai web. Work is lost mid-generation. Issue is labeled duplicate — likely a known recurring problem affecting high-volume paying users.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: server processes leak CPU after Claude Code exits, causing system-wide resource exhaustion
signals.summary: Telegram plugin bun processes are reparented to launchd and survive after Claude Code exits, each spinning at 80-100% CPU indefinitely. Multiple reports show accumulation of 7-14 leaked processes consuming 190MB RAM and 63-230 CPU-hours each, with load averages spiking to 40 on multi-core machines.
signals.review_reason: Severe system-wide resource exhaustion affecting stability of the host machine. Multiple independent reports confirm accumulated orphaned processes each burning 80-100% CPU and 190MB+ RAM. Affects any user of the Telegram plugin on macOS/Linux. This is not an edge case — it actively starves other processes and degrades system performance.

source_issues.title: [telegram] Server leaks and pegs 100% CPU when Claude Code exits without SIGTERM-ing plugin
source_issues.evidence: 14 leaked bun server.ts processes found; oldest at 64 CPU-hours; total ~250 CPU-hours burned in 3 days; M4 Pro Mac mini load avg 40, fan at max

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: orphaned bun server.ts procs survive SIGTERM and orphan-watchdog on macOS
source_issues.evidence: 7 orphaned bun server.ts workers running concurrently after 10 days; each consuming ~90% CPU and ~190MB RAM; workers not terminated by SIGTERM handlers or orphan watchdog

source_issues.title: [telegram] Plugin bun subprocess dies during interactive session on mobile-tethered network
source_issues.evidence: bun subprocess terminates silently multiple times per multi-hour session; main claude process unaffected; plugin disappears without user action

signals.topic: ralph-loop stop-hook aborts with 'No such file or directory' due to race condition on state file removal
signals.summary: The ralph-loop plugin's stop-hook.sh script contains 9 rm calls against the state file with 'set -euo pipefail' enabled. When the state file is already removed (by a concurrent cancel-ralph call or another stop-hook tick), rm returns non-zero and the hook aborts, surfacing a hook error in the Claude Code UI.
signals.review_reason: ralph-loop is a core workflow-automation plugin. The stop-hook is a critical automation path that is expected to run reliably in the background. Aborting on a race condition is a direct workflow blocker — it interrupts the loop lifecycle management and surfaces error messages to users mid-session. The fix is trivial (rm -f) but the impact on loop users is real and reproducible.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: stop-hook rm calls fail on already-removed state file (set -euo pipefail aborts)
source_issues.evidence: 9 rm calls against state file with 'set -euo pipefail' at top; rm returns non-zero if file already gone; race observed against /ralph-loop:cancel-ralph and concurrent stop-hook ticks; hook error surfaced in Claude Code UI

signals.topic: Telegram plugin MCP server dies after long idle periods on Linux with no auto-respawn
signals.summary: After Claude Code goes idle for several hours, the Telegram MCP server process shuts itself down when its stdio pipe is closed by the Claude Code MCP client. Claude Code does not respawn the plugin, leaving reply, react, and other Telegram tools unavailable until the user manually runs /reload-plugins.
signals.review_reason: After idle periods (hours), the Telegram plugin becomes unavailable without any user action or warning. Users must notice the missing tools and manually intervene with /reload-plugins. This is a key functionality loss that affects the remote Telegram workflow — the primary use case of the plugin.

source_issues.title: [telegram] MCP server dies after long idle periods on Linux; Claude Code doesn't auto-respawn (v0.0.6)
source_issues.evidence: MCP server dies after prolonged inactivity; Claude Code's stdio client closes pipe; orphan watchdog detects closed stdin and exits cleanly; no auto-respawn; reply/react tools vanish from tool registry until manual /reload-plugins

signals.topic: Telegram plugin sendMessage returns 'chat not found' on verified healthy bot and chat
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin's sendMessage/reply MCP calls return HTTP 400 'Bad Request: chat not found' even though the bot token and chat ID are verified working via direct Telegram Bot API calls. The getUpdates long-poll also does not ACK updates, causing pending_update_count to grow.
signals.review_reason: The core sendMessage functionality of the Telegram plugin is completely broken for affected users. The fact that direct API calls work rules out infrastructure issues and confirms a bug in the plugin's chat ID resolution or API method usage. Users are blocked from sending outbound messages via the plugin.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: sendMessage returns 'chat not found' and polling does not ACK updates on a known-good bot/chat
source_issues.evidence: Direct curl to Telegram API with same token/chat_id works fine; plugin returns 400 'Bad Request: chat not found'; getUpdates long-poll does not ACK updates; pending_update_count grows monotonically

signals.topic: Discord plugin reply tool fails after bot restart due to broken DM channel auth (recipientId null, dmChannelUsers empty)
signals.summary: After the Discord bot restarts, calling the reply tool on DM channels fails with 'channel is not allowlisted' even though the user IS in the access allowlist and inbound messages are delivered normally. Root cause: Discord.js returns a partial DMChannel with recipientId null after restart, and the in-memory dmChannelUsers map is empty on fresh start.
signals.review_reason: Any bot restart (systemd service update, crash recovery, manual restart) causes immediate breakage of the Discord DM reply feature. Inbound messages continue working but the agent cannot respond to them — this is a complete functional regression for Discord DM workflows. The root cause is deterministic and reproducible on every restart.

source_issues.title: reply fails after bot restart: DM channel auth broken when recipientId is null and dmChannelUsers is empty
source_issues.evidence: After bot restart, outbound reply calls fail with 'channel not allowlisted' despite user being in access.allowFrom; inbound messages still delivered; root cause: Discord.js returns partial DMChannel with recipientId null and in-memory dmChannelUsers map is empty

signals.topic: skill-creator 限制导致 Pro 用户无法完成主流程
signals.summary: Pro 订阅用户在 skill-creator 上遭遇严格限制（5小时×2次），既无法生成任何有效结果，也无力通过 skills/agents/memory 构建上下文，主流程被完全阻断。
aliases: Pro subscription limits blocking skill creation
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但用户明确描述了订阅付费后核心功能完全不可用的场景，属于关键功能不可用+计费损失。reviewer 已在 issue 中确认问题真实存在（last_comment_days=2）。按规则，count<3 时若 review_reason 提供强用户影响证据可升为 P1。此处证据充分：Pro 订阅 + 主流程阻断 + 零产出。

source_issues.title: skill-creator eliminated the whole limits (5 hours x 2 times) without any result
source_issues.evidence: Pro subscription user explicitly reports inability to code or even set up context via skills, agents, and memory after hitting new limits — main workflow completely blocked with no result delivered.

signals.topic: macOS idle sessions fail: goosed process killed by disk-write limits + SSE stream break
signals.summary: When leaving Goose Desktop sessions idle (5-30 min) on macOS with large session databases, the goosed backend process is killed by macOS resource-coalition disk-write limits (SQLite sort spills reaching 137GB), causing all sidebar sessions in that window to fail simultaneously with no automatic recovery. The SSE event stream also breaks on idle open windows, compounding the failure.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断型：用户离开会话几小时后回来，整个会话不可用、输入内容永久丢失。三个独立 issue（#8711/#8717/#8729）均指向同一根因——macOS + 大型 sessions.db + 空闲导致 goosed 进程被终止或 SSE 流断开。无自动恢复路径，用户必须手动开新窗口/新会话。count=3 且有 macOS 诊断报告和具体堆栈证据，满足 P0 条件。

source_issues.title: [BUG] goosed killed by macOS disk-write coalition limits — SQLite sorter/pwrite workload on large sessions.db
source_issues.evidence: Three macOS DiagnosticReports showing goosed exit with code 0 after 2-137GB disk writes from SQLite pwrite/pwrite; sessions.db is ~700MB with 106K messages; multi-window architecture amplifies WAL write pressure; powerSaveBlocker.start() never called.

source_issues.title: [BUG] SSE stream breaks on idle open windows — all sidebar sessions fail simultaneously
source_issues.evidence: SSE event stream breaks after 5-30 min of inactivity; all sidebar sessions in the same window fail simultaneously as they share the same goosed backend; reconnect logic gives up and enters terminal error state; new window works because it spawns a fresh goosed process.

source_issues.title: Chat window breaks when continuing after hour(s)
source_issues.evidence: Chat session breaks upon pressing send/enter after leaving it for hours; typed message is permanently lost; occurs on macOS with many extensions enabled including memory extensions that write to session.db.

signals.topic: Goose CLI launch blocked by tty output error on Linux (process suspended)
signals.summary: Goose CLI (goose session) immediately suspends with a tty output error on RHEL/Linux when invoked from zsh or bash terminals. The root cause is a regression introduced in commit b7aea3dc9 where spawn_blocking with bash -l -i for PATH resolution inherits the parent's terminal control group, causing the shell to suspend. This is a hard block on CLI usage for Linux users.
aliases: login shell tty hang on launch
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断型：Goose CLI 完全无法启动（进程挂起），影响所有 Linux CLI 用户。虽有明确修复方案，但用户侧表现为启动失败而非功能受限，故判定为 P1 而非 P0（因 count=1，单仓问题，且 CLI 启动失败不涉及计费/数据丢失）。

source_issues.title: Goose CLI Will Not Launch
source_issues.evidence: Consistently reproducible on RHEL 9 x86_64 with zsh and bash; goose session immediately suspends with 'zsh: suspended (tty output)'; breaking commit identified as b7aea3dc9; author provided a verified fix using process_group(0) to detach from terminal.

signals.topic: Jira extension silently fails after OAuth token expiration (no recovery, no re-auth prompt)
signals.summary: The Jira MCP extension fails silently after OAuth 2.0 tokens expire — all Jira API calls return authentication errors with no visible error message and no browser window to re-initiate OAuth. The root cause is that ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_SECRET is only bundled in Desktop builds, not CLI, and the token refresh flow is not implemented in either. Users must manually intervene or use Glean as a read-only workaround.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Jira 集成是 Goose 的核心企业功能，OAuth token 过期后完全静默失败（无错误提示、无重试、无重认证入口），用户不知道 extension 已失效。影响 Desktop 和 CLI 两个界面，属于明显的关键功能阻断而非边缘问题。

source_issues.title: Jira auth issue
source_issues.evidence: Root cause confirmed via Slack thread by Walter Ray-Dulany and Tyler Longwell: mcp_jira_python requires ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_SECRET which is only bundled in Desktop app builds; Desktop tokens expire with no auto-refresh; CLI has no client secret at all; extension appears enabled but is non-functional; no re-auth prompt surfaced to user.

signals.topic: Slash commands and tab completion fail to load from configuration file on Linux CLI
signals.summary: Slash commands configured in the Goose configuration file are not recognized or executed on Linux CLI. Tab completion for slash commands is also non-functional. Users cannot invoke custom slash commands that they have configured, degrading the CLI usability and discoverability.
aliases: slash command tab completion broken linux
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：用户配置的自定义 slash commands 完全不可用，tab 自动补全也失效，CLI 核心交互能力受损。虽然 count=1，但 Linux CLI 作为 Goose 的主要使用入口之一，此 bug 直接影响用户的工作流效率。

source_issues.title: slash commands bug
source_issues.evidence: User reported on Linux CLI that configured slash commands are not usable and tab completion is broken; screenshot provided showing configured commands not loading; reproducible on Linux.

signals.topic: Goose 2 UI layout breaks and overlaps in side panel and compact view modes
signals.summary: In Goose 2 UI, opening the right-side panel (Details/Files) causes layout overlap between the chat area and the message composer. The issue is significantly worse in compact view or smaller window sizes, where elements overlap severely and parts of the composer and chat become partially hidden or completely unusable.
aliases: chat composer hidden side panel open
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：Goose 2 UI 在侧边栏打开时布局重叠，关键输入区域（composer）部分被遮挡，在 compact 模式下更严重。虽然 count=1，但 Goose 2 是新架构的主要界面，UI 可用性问题应作为独立痛点记录。

source_issues.title: Bug: UI layout breaks and overlaps in side panel & compact view (Goose 2 UI)
source_issues.evidence: Screenshot provided showing chat area overlapping with other UI elements when right-side panel is open in Goose 2; compact view makes the overlap significantly worse; composer becomes partially hidden; layout does not adapt to available width.

signals.topic: Cloudflare-protected site automation fails — browser opens blank and throws internal errors
signals.summary: Stagehand fails to automate Cloudflare-protected websites (e.g. jiji.ng): the Chromium browser opens stuck at about:blank instead of navigating to the target URL, observe/act calls throw internal errors (Cannot read properties of undefined, StagehandError on empty ObserveResult), and the user cannot complete any web automation tasks on Cloudflare-challenged sites.
aliases: headless browser blank on Cloudflare sites
Stagehand cannot interact with Cloudflare challenge pages
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point: the core automation workflow is completely blocked on Cloudflare-protected sites, which are extremely common in the wild. The browser opens blank (never navigates), all observe/act operations fail with internal errors, and the user has no viable workaround — forcing a migration away from Stagehand's intended API. While count=1 (single issue), the severity is high: it renders Stagehand unusable for any site protected by Cloudflare's challenge layer, which represents a significant portion of real-world websites.

source_issues.title: Stagehand Issue: Unable to Automate Cloudflare-blocked sites (Blank Browser, and Internal Errors)
source_issues.evidence: Browser opens at about:blank instead of navigating to target URL; observe/act throw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)' and 'StagehandError: Invalid argument: you may have called act with an empty ObserveResult'; no workaround resolves the issue; main automation flow fully blocked on Cloudflare-protected sites.

signals.topic: Docker startup/deployment failures on Windows causing main workflow blockage
signals.summary: Docker compose fails to start services on Windows due to file path issues (docker-compose-dev.yaml not found), blocking initial setup for Windows users.
signals.review_reason: Docker deployment is a core setup path; failures at this stage block all new users on Windows and Linux from using the product. Two independent reports (#2416 on Windows with file-not-found error, #2380 on Linux with hang) confirm this is a recurring setup blocker across platforms, not an isolated environment issue.

signals.topic: Event loop closure causing RuntimeError during subagent/MCP execution in long conversations
signals.summary: Long-running conversations crash with RuntimeError: Event loop is closed when MCP services are enabled or subagents use isolated event loops, due to langchain_openai reusing cached async HTTP clients across event loops.
aliases: LLM request failed: Event loop is closed
signals.review_reason: Core runtime error that causes main agent workflow to crash mid-execution during long conversations. Issue #2397 shows it specifically manifests when MCP is enabled, and #2405 provides detailed root cause analysis of langchain_openai client caching across event loops. This breaks the primary use case (sustained agent conversations) and has clear user impact evidence.

signals.topic: Agent creation fails with 403 error during name validation, blocking core user workflow
signals.summary: Creating agents via the web UI fails with 403 Forbidden error on /api/agents, preventing users from setting up agents. Root cause appears to be overly strict name validation logic.
signals.review_reason: Agent creation is a fundamental user workflow that is completely blocked by this bug. Two separate users independently reported the same 403 on the same endpoint, with issue #2378 having 9 comments indicating active user frustration and workaround attempts. This is not a one-off issue.

signals.topic: Thread history collapses to single entry due to checkpoint ID reuse bug
signals.summary: update_thread_state copies the existing checkpoint dict verbatim (including id field) before calling checkpointer.aput, causing INSERT OR REPLACE to overwrite the existing row and resulting in thread history always containing exactly one entry.
signals.review_reason: Data integrity bug that causes permanent loss of conversation history. The bug report includes a clear root cause analysis and self-contained fix description. This is a critical session state issue that affects any user relying on multi-turn conversation history for context continuity.

signals.topic: Per-agent skill filtering configuration does not work as documented
signals.summary: Configuring per-agent skills via skills: [...] in config.yaml has no effect - all skills are still exposed regardless of agent-level filtering settings.
signals.review_reason: Documented feature is completely non-functional, leading to skill permission/configuration expectations mismatch. User provided full reproduction steps with a custom agent that specifies skills: ['report-helper'] but both skills are still returned. This is a clear feature bug in the core agent configuration system.

signals.topic: Qwen3 API regression — 400 Bad Request / invalid_parameter_error blocks all requests on qwen3-coder-plus model
signals.summary: Qwen3-coder-plus model returns 400 Bad Request (invalid_parameter_error) on every request, across both VS Code and JetBrains plugins, following a recent update.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear regression: a previously-working model (qwen3-coder-plus) now fails on every request across two IDE platforms (VS Code + JetBrains), indicating a regression introduced by a recent Cline update that broke Qwen API compatibility. The failure is reproducible and non-conditional. count=2 (issues 10265 and 10253, confirmed distinct reports from different platforms).

source_issues.title: Recent Regression — 400 Bad Request with qwen3-coder-plus
source_issues.evidence: Status 400 Bad Request, code: invalid_parameter_error. Previously working setup now fails on every request (including simple 'Hello' prompts). Regression following recent updates.

source_issues.title: Error when trying to query Qwen
source_issues.evidence: Same 400 bad request / invalid_parameter_error on qwen3-coder-plus, reproduced in both VS Code and JetBrains Rider. Neural network analysis suggests Qwen streaming flag is not being properly sent in the request.

signals.topic: OpenAI Compatible provider token count inflation — usage counter jumps to millions / resets to zero / think tags render as raw text
signals.summary: When using OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g. NVIDIA API), the context-usage bar shows astronomical values (millions of tokens) and resets to zero after each thinking step; additionally, <think> and [TOOL_CALL] blocks render as unparsed raw text in the UI.
aliases: usage bar shows millions of tokens
thinking tags render as plain text
signals.review_reason: This is a clear user pain point: the token counter is functionally useless (shows misleading values), which directly disrupts the user's ability to monitor context window usage — a core UX element of Cline. The raw <think> tags rendering as text further degrades readability of AI output. Count=1 because only one issue explicitly documents this, but the underlying bug is a systematic missing guard in openai.ts affecting any OpenAI-compatible provider.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Compatible providers (NVIDIA) context usage shows high fluctuated values and <think> tags render as plain text
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: OpenAiHandler yields usage on every chunk.usage presence without a didOutputUsage guard, unlike openrouter.ts. Token totals inflate to 15M+ within a few exchanges. Also, NVIDIA reasoning blocks (<think>...</think>) and [TOOL_CALL] blocks are passed through raw without post-processing, rendering as plain text in the UI.

signals.topic: Cline CLI completely unusable on Windows 10 — 'cannot access the file claude' error on every task creation
signals.summary: Cline CLI on Windows 10 throws 'cannot access the file claude' error on every task creation attempt, making the CLI entirely unusable.
aliases: Cline CLI file access error Windows
cannot access the file claude Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a blocking issue: the entire Cline CLI workflow on Windows 10 is broken — users cannot create or execute any tasks. This constitutes a main-flow failure with 100% reproducibility on that platform. Count=1 but impact is severe enough to qualify as P1.

source_issues.title: Cline CLI fails with 'cannot access the file claude' error when creating new tasks on Windows 10
source_issues.evidence: User reports error occurs consistently on every task creation attempt on Windows 10, making Cline CLI completely unusable. Error message: 'cannot access the file claude'. The issue persists across restarts.

signals.topic: Kanban agents fail with NoOutputGeneratedError when using GitHub Copilot API with tool calls
signals.summary: Kanban agents using @ai-sdk/openai-compatible to call GitHub Copilot API with tool definitions receive NoOutputGeneratedError (Claude models) or 400 schema errors (GPT models), breaking the entire Kanban workflow.
aliases: Vercel AI SDK tool schema incompatibility
signals.review_reason: This blocks a specific but legitimate workflow: Kanban agents with tool calls cannot operate against GitHub Copilot API, producing unhandled NoOutputGeneratedError exceptions. The incompatibility is between the Vercel AI SDK's schema serialization and GitHub Copilot's API expectations, making the Kanban+Copilot combination non-functional.

source_issues.title: Kanban agents fail with GitHub Copilot API (OpenAI-compatible provider)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: Vercel AI SDK serializes tool schemas differently from OpenAI SDK. GitHub Copilot API returns 'schema must be a JSON Schema of type object, got type None' for GPT models, and NoOutputGeneratedError for Claude models. Workflow is completely broken when tools are involved.

signals.topic: Extension causes high CPU load on Windows 11
signals.summary: VS Code extension causes sustained high CPU load on Windows 11, indicating a background polling or runaway loop issue.
signals.review_reason: High CPU load indicates a performance degradation that affects system responsiveness and resource consumption. While the root cause is not yet identified, the symptom is measurable and user-reported, suggesting a real impact. Downgraded to P2 due to count=1 and no confirmed root cause.

source_issues.title: Extension causes high cpu load
source_issues.evidence: User reports sustained high CPU load on Windows 11 (OS version 10.0.26200) with extension version 3.79.0. A CPU profile was attached. No specific root cause identified yet.

signals.topic: CLI install script fails silently with no actionable error message on Linux/macOS
signals.summary: The CLI install script (`install.sh`) can exit with a generic 'Installation failed. Cleaning up' message on Linux and macOS without telling the user what went wrong. On Linux the script exits with code 127 due to a missing `npm` binary after partial Node.js installation. On macOS the fnm binary path check is wrong (`$FNM_INSTALL_DIR/fnm` vs `$FNM_INSTALL_DIR`), causing the installer to fail even when fnm is correctly installed via Homebrew. Both cases leave users unable to install the CLI with zero indication of the actual cause.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports (Linux and macOS) confirm the install script silently fails in both environments, completely blocking the CLI installation path. This is a primary adoption blocker — users cannot use the product at all. Both have clear error evidence: exit code 127 on Linux, wrong fnm path check on macOS. Count=2 meets the multi-platform threshold.

source_issues.title: CLI install can fail with no error message
source_issues.evidence: Install script exits with code 127 after Node.js passes its own check but npm is missing. No error description beyond 'Installation failed. Cleaning up'. User has to inspect the shell script to understand the failure.

source_issues.title: Install script is not working due fnm binary
source_issues.evidence: On macOS the fnm check uses `if [ ! -x "$FNM_INSTALL_DIR/fnm" ]` but should check `if [ ! -x "$FNM_INSTALL_DIR" ]` (the fnm shim is at the directory path). Homebrew installs fnm correctly but the path check fails anyway, causing a silent failure.

signals.topic: Continue plugin fails to load sessions in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 Ultimate — session JSON file not created on disk
signals.summary: The Continue IntelliJ plugin (v1.0.67) on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 Ultimate generates a new session ID on each restart but never creates the corresponding `.json` file on disk. This causes the plugin to repeatedly emit 'Session file does not exist' errors and fail to initialize properly. The issue is specific to IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 Ultimate and does not occur in Community Edition. Multiple user troubleshooting steps (clearing .continue, clearing JetBrains config, reinstalling the IDE, verifying permissions) did not resolve it.
aliases: session file does not exist IJ
signals.review_reason: Single-occurrence but extremely severe: the plugin completely fails to initialize in a specific IntelliJ version, making Continue unusable for affected users. The evidence is comprehensive — user performed exhaustive troubleshooting including clean reinstalls of both the IDE and plugin without resolution. The repeated error on every startup constitutes a startup-blocking crash for the IntelliJ plugin.

source_issues.title: Session file does not exist
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'Session file C:\Users\...\.continue\sessions\[ID].json does not exist.' The plugin cannot load or persist sessions in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 Ultimate (Build #IU-261.22158.277). All workaround attempts failed: clearing .continue, clearing JetBrains config, reinstalling the IDE, verifying permissions, testing with empty project, killing node processes.

signals.topic: Local model names with slashes/hyphens are incorrectly trimmed in CLI config.yaml
signals.summary: When configuring a local model with a name containing `/` or `-` (e.g., `local/large` or `local-large`) in the CLI `config.yaml`, the model name gets incorrectly stripped down to the substring after the last delimiter (e.g., `large`). This causes the TUI to display the wrong model name and breaks LLM chat responses entirely. Only using the fully trimmed name as the `model` field works. This appears to be overzealous basename-like trimming being applied to model names that should be passed through unchanged.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug in the CLI config parser that completely breaks local model usage when the model name contains path separators. Users who run local models (a major use case for Continue) are blocked from using the product at all in the CLI. The issue has clear, reproducible steps and a root cause identified.

source_issues.title: model names are wrongfully trimmed to the last delimiter in CLI config.yaml
source_issues.evidence: User configured model name 'local/large' and 'local-large' in CLI config.yaml. Both result in TUI showing only 'large' as the model name and chat functionality breaks. Chat works when the model field is changed to just 'large'. Root cause identified as incorrect basename-like trimming applied to model names.

signals.topic: @file context length check gives false 'File exceeds context length' error while @CurrentFile works for the same file
signals.summary: Using the `@file` directive to include a file in a chat prompt (files around 20kB or 300 lines) produces a false 'File exceeds model's context length' error, even though the same file loaded via `@CurrentFile` works fine and the actual token count shown in the Continue Console is well within the limit. The error is triggered before the prompt is even sent, indicating an incorrect file-size or token-counting heuristic in the @file directive logic.
signals.review_reason: A core interaction feature (@file directive) gives false errors that prevent users from using the file context feature, while @CurrentFile handles the exact same file without issue. This is a clear functional discrepancy that blocks the primary use case of referencing project files in chat. The evidence includes side-by-side comparison showing @CurrentFile succeeds with the same file.

source_issues.title: @file applies the wrong context length limit but @CurrentFile works fine
source_issues.evidence: User reports @file on ~20kB / ~300 line files triggers 'File exceeds model's context length' warning. Opening the same file and using @CurrentFile works perfectly — the Continue Console shows the full file content with a token count well within the model's context limit. The failure happens before the prompt is constructed, indicating incorrect heuristic in @file logic.

signals.topic: Continue VS Code extension crashes with 'Headers is not defined' ReferenceError in code-server environments
signals.summary: The Continue VS Code extension (v1.2.22) throws a `ReferenceError: Headers is not defined` when running inside code-server on Linux, completely preventing any LLM interaction. The `Headers` class (a browser/web standard API) is not available in the code-server extension host environment, causing the OpenAI adapter's `buildHeaders` function to fail before any network request is made. The issue has been recurring for multiple users across different VS Code versions and environments.
aliases: code-server extension host Headers API missing
signals.review_reason: The extension throws an uncaught ReferenceError at the top of the request chain, completely preventing any LLM interaction in code-server environments. This is a startup/runtime crash that blocks the primary feature. The stack trace unambiguously identifies the root cause: the `Headers` web API is not available in the code-server extension host context. The issue has affected multiple users over time.

source_issues.title: Headers not defined -> This time with logs
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows: 'ReferenceError: Headers is not defined' at buildHeaders -> OpenAI.buildBody -> OpenAI.buildRequest -> OpenAI.makeRequest. The error occurs at the first LLM call and completely blocks the extension. A request is never made to the web server. Multiple users affected historically, issue recurs across VS Code versions.

signals.topic: Checkpointing和Guardrail重试机制与Pydantic结构化输出不兼容，导致Flow状态序列化失败
signals.summary: 当Flow状态包含Pydantic模型时，CheckpointConfig会触发PydanticSerializationError；同时当Task使用output_pydantic且guardrail返回(False, feedback)时，重试逻辑将Pydantic对象错误地传递给TaskOutput.raw字段（期望string），导致ValidationError。两条问题共同造成Pydantic结构化输出在Flow+guardrail场景下完全不可用。
aliases: Pydantic serialization fails during Flow checkpointing
Guardrail retry TaskOutput type mismatch with output_pydantic
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Pydantic结构化输出是CrewAI Flows核心功能，checkpointing失败+guardrail重试崩溃共同导致结构化输出在Flow场景下完全不可用。用户被迫手动注入schema和解析raw输出以规避框架bug，绕过设计意图。count=1因仅单一仓库，但用户影响证据极为充分（完整堆栈+workaround），可因review_reason充分而突破默认P0阈值。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Checkpointing + guardrail retry incompatible with Pydantic outputs in Flow
source_issues.evidence: PydanticSerializationError: Unable to serialize unknown type: <class 'pydantic._internal._model_construction.ModelMetaclass'>；ValidationError: Input should be a valid string for TaskOutput.raw, input_value=FamilyList(...)；主流程完全阻断，用户被迫手动绕过CrewAI内部Pydantic→JSON管道。

signals.topic: Task.input_files在Crew.agents未显式传递时静默失效，多模态文件不被处理
signals.summary: 当Task的agent已通过task.agent指定时，用户期望Crew可不传agents参数直接运行。但CrewAI对input_files（如ImageFile）的文件注入逻辑依赖Crew.agents列表——若为空则文件注入被静默跳过，模型表现如同未提供任何文件，且不抛任何错误或警告。
aliases: Multimodal input files silently ignored without explicit Crew.agents
ImageFile silently dropped when agent assigned only at Task level
signals.review_reason: 关键功能静默失败：多模态文件处理是CrewAI核心差异化能力。静默失败（无error/warning）极度危险——用户认为任务正常完成但文件从未被处理。与直觉API设计相悖且极难调试。count=1但影响关键功能，可因review_reason充分证据突破默认P0阈值。

source_issues.title: [BUG] CrewAI: Task.input_files + missing Crew.agents causes multimodal files to be ignored
source_issues.evidence: 同一代码Crew(tasks=[task])时图片被忽略；Crew(agents=[agent], tasks=[task])时图片被正确处理。无任何error或warning，用户完全无法感知文件未被处理，直到发现模型输出中图片内容缺失。

signals.topic: crewai传递了存在已知漏洞的uv依赖版本，导致下游项目CI/CD安全扫描失败
signals.summary: crewai==1.13.0通过依赖传递引入了uv==0.9.30，该版本受GHSA-pjjw-68hj-v9mw（wheel RECORD路径遍历漏洞）影响。任何使用crewai的下游项目在运行pip-audit、Dependabot、Snyk等自动化安全扫描时均会触发该CVE告警，导致CI/CD gate失败或需要人工忽略CVE。
aliases: Transitive dependency uv pinned to vulnerable version causing CI security gate failures
signals.review_reason: 具有明确用户影响证据（CI/CD安全扫描失败、修复版本已知且可用），count=1仅单仓，按规则P0受限。虽然CVE利用路径较窄，但自动化安全扫描的大规模阻断是真实用户痛点，修复成本极低（仅需更新依赖约束），优先级P1合理。

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.13.0 pins vulnerable uv 0.9.30 (GHSA-pjjw-68hj-v9mw)
source_issues.evidence: pip-audit在依赖crewai的项目中报告GHSA-pjjw-68hj-v9mw；修复版本uv>=0.11.6早已发布。影响所有使用crewai且运行自动化安全扫描的团队，触发CI gate失败或强制手动维护CVE白名单。

signals.topic: OpenRouter thinking models（Claude Sonnet 4.5/Opus 4.5、Gemini 3.1）在CrewAI中返回空响应导致流程崩溃
signals.summary: 通过OpenRouter使用Anthropic thinking模型（claude-sonnet-4-5、claude-opus-4.5）和Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview时，CrewAI agent执行任务抛出ValueError: Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty，导致multi-agent chained任务完全失败。同等配置下GLM、Qwen、GPT模型工作正常。
aliases: OpenRouter Claude Sonnet 4.5/Opus 4.5 thinking mode crashes with empty LLM response
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败，影响主流thinking模型。堆栈显示crewAI内部_handle_human_feedback→_invoke_loop→handle_max_iterations_exceeded→ValueError链，模型返回空响应被框架错误处理。但根因可能部分归因于OpenRouter端thinking模型特殊处理机制，置信度0.85。P2因count=1且根因待定。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Problems with OpenRouter thinking models
source_issues.evidence: 完整堆栈跟踪显示ValueError: Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty；影响claude-sonnet-4-5、claude-opus-4-5、Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview；同配置下GLM/Qwen/GPT正常工作；学术写作agent编排任务完全阻断。

signals.topic: ChatWithCrewFlow初始化在模块导入时执行阻塞式LLM调用，导致容器启动时因LLM故障而崩溃
signals.summary: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__在模块导入阶段即触发crewai.cli.crew_chat.generate_crew_chat_inputs（内部调用generate_input_description_with_ai和generate_crew_description_with_ai），两者均为同步阻塞LLM调用。在FastAPI/AG-UI/CopilotKit部署中，LLM故障（500/503/限速/网络抖动/无效凭据）在HTTP服务器绑定端口之前就导致进程崩溃Exit(1)，容器启动失败并被orchestrator回滚。
aliases: Module import LLM call crashes container on startup before HTTP server binds port
signals.review_reason: 容器启动崩溃阻断生产部署：用户使用AG-UI/CopilotKit/FastAPI进行生产部署时，LLM任何抖动均可在服务就绪前导致进程退出。影响所有使用ChatWithCrewFlow的容器化部署，orchestrator健康检查失败触发自动回滚。P1因review_reason提供充分生产部署影响证据。

source_issues.title: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ makes blocking LLM call at module import, crashes containers on any LLM hiccup
source_issues.evidence: 完整堆栈：add_crewai_crew_fastapi_endpoint→ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__→generate_crew_chat_inputs→chat_llm.call→APIError；Railway部署实测崩溃；CopilotKit侧已发PR(CopilotKit/CopilotKit#3974)以monkey-patch绕开；无timeout、无retry、无graceful fallback。

signals.topic: SSE /chat endpoint emits misleading 'complete' event on strategy loading failure instead of 'error' event
signals.summary: When /chat receives an invalid strategyName, it returns HTTP 200 with a 'complete' SSE event even though the request assembly failed, causing silent client-side misclassification of failures.
signals.review_reason: SSE endpoint returns 'complete' (implies success) on a request that actually failed during prompt/session construction. This is a contract violation that silently misleads downstream clients, causing them to treat failures as successes. While count=1 and not P0, it is a non-trivial UX/runtime failure where the failure is invisible to the caller.

source_issues.title: /chat SSE returns complete even when strategy loading fails
source_issues.evidence: SSE client receives 'complete' event with empty content on strategy load failure, violating streaming contract. Reporter provided local reproduction and regression test.

signals.topic: YouTube visual OCR outputs incorrect timestamps based on frame index instead of actual video frame timing
signals.summary: GrabVisual() uses the nth OCR result index as timestamp instead of the actual ffmpeg-derived frame time, producing temporally misleading output.
aliases: YouTube OCR timestamp index instead of frame time
signals.review_reason: The feature produces visually plausible but factually incorrect timestamps, directly reducing trust in the output. This causes users to act on misleading information when processing YouTube video content. Although count=1, the incorrect timestamps can lead to downstream decisions based on wrong video moments.

source_issues.title: YouTube visual OCR output uses index-based timestamps instead of real frame timing
source_issues.evidence: GrabVisual() renders timestamps using 'secs := i' (index) instead of actual ffmpeg frame time. Reporter provided local test with mocked yt-dlp/ffmpeg/tesseract. Incorrect timestamps reduce output trust and misattribute OCR text to wrong video moments.

signals.topic: Codex/LLM returns empty response causing complete command failure
signals.summary: When using fabric with the codex vendor (chatgpt.com backend), the LLM returns empty content and the CLI outputs 'empty response', making the main usage flow completely unusable.
signals.review_reason: The primary CLI command flow (fabric with codex vendor) produces literally zero output, blocking the main use case entirely. User-reproducible with a clear debug trace showing empty LLM response content. This is a main-path failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: codex empty response
source_issues.evidence: User runs 'echo something | fabric --debug 4 -p summarize' with codex vendor. Debug log shows 'LLM->FABRIC response content=""' followed by 'empty response' output. The core command flow produces no usable output.

signals.topic: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED errors blocking all API calls via OAuth or API key
signals.summary: Multiple users receive 403 PERMISSION_DENIED errors on every API call, completely blocking the CLI from functioning. Affects both OAuth personal accounts and API key authentication. Some users report the issue started suddenly, while others cannot access after account suspension. Web UI works fine, indicating a CLI-specific auth issue.
signals.review_reason: 5 distinct users completely blocked from using the CLI. Primary auth mechanism (OAuth personal) returns 403 on every request. Not isolated - affects paying subscribers and API key users alike. The Web UI works, confirming this is a CLI-side auth bug, not a user quota issue. This is a main flow blocker.

source_issues.title: The caller does not have permission
source_issues.evidence: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED error on every user message. OAuth personal account. CLI unusable.

source_issues.title: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on every command
source_issues.evidence: User with Google AI Pro subscription still gets 403. Both Google Login OAuth fails. Blocks all usage.

source_issues.title: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED error when using Google OAuth or API Key via CLI
source_issues.evidence: Consistent 403 after 24h. Affects both OAuth and fresh API key. Region Pakistan. Web AI Studio works fine.

source_issues.title: Account Suspended (Error 403)
source_issues.evidence: Premium subscriber account suspended due to third-party extension. 403 on CLI login. Directed here by Google Support.

source_issues.title: Account suspended for Antigravity/Gemini CLI
source_issues.evidence: Account suspended for reverse proxy ToS violation. Premium user. Submitted acknowledgment form 5 times with no response. Blocks all usage.

signals.topic: Unhandled Promise Rejection crashes causing CLI to crash on startup or during API calls
signals.summary: Unhandled promise rejections crash the CLI with uncaught exceptions. Affects startup initialization (ECONNRESET to cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com) and runtime API calls (fetch failed with headers timeout). One crash occurs in terminal rendering (String.repeat with -1). All are uncaught exceptions that terminate the process.
signals.review_reason: 3 users experience unhandled promise rejections that crash the CLI entirely. These are process-terminating exceptions from three different root causes (network, rendering, fetch), all uncaught. All block the main workflow from running. Strong user impact evidence with full stack traces.

source_issues.title: CRITICAL: Unhandled Promise Rejection!
source_issues.evidence: Startup crash: ECONNRESET when fetching from cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:listExperiments. Unhandled promise rejection. CLI fails to start.

source_issues.title: gemini cli bug
source_issues.evidence: Unhandled Promise Rejection: RangeError Invalid count value: -1 at String.repeat in renderBorder. Repeated 65 times. CLI crashes.

source_issues.title: Error in Terminal
source_issues.evidence: Unhandled Promise Rejection: TypeError fetch failed with HeadersTimeoutError during IDE MCP connection. Blocks tool usage.

signals.topic: Agent file write operations partially fail — only last change applied or new files not created
signals.summary: When an agent proposes multiple file changes in one request, only the last change is actually applied; earlier changes are silently lost. Separately, when creating new files in a remote directory, only existing .md files get overwritten while new files fail to be created. Both result in data loss.
signals.review_reason: 2 separate instances of file write operations silently failing with data loss. Issue #25750 shows explicit data loss (earlier changes discarded). Issue #25746 shows new files not created at all. Both are agent workflow failures that result in incomplete or lost user work.

source_issues.title: Agent raising multiple changes but only the last accepted change is reflecting
source_issues.evidence: When agent proposes changes at lines 20, 40, and 60, accepting all three only applies the line 60 change. Earlier changes are silently lost. Data loss confirmed.

source_issues.title: unexpected error during remote create file and write task
source_issues.evidence: Creating multiple new markdown files fails with 'unexpected error'. Only existing .md files get written. New file creation silently fails. User lost expected output files.

signals.topic: Quota/billing display incorrect — shows 100% used or loops endlessly on fallback model
signals.summary: Users are blocked from using the service due to incorrect quota display. One user sees 100% consumption after creating a GCP account, permanently blocking pro model access. Another user gets an endless loop of 'usage limit reached' prompts even after switching to the suggested fallback model, making the CLI unusable.
signals.review_reason: 2 users blocked from using the service due to quota display bugs. #25738 shows billing/quota system corruption after GCP account creation. #25741 shows an infinite loop UX bug that makes the CLI unusable. Both are main-flow blockers with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Bug on model use / usage limit reached
source_issues.evidence: User already on suggested fallback model (gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview) but 'usage limit reached' message keeps repeating endlessly. CLI becomes unusable.

source_issues.title: Pro quota shows incorrect 100% consumption after creation of GCP account
source_issues.evidence: Quota permanently stuck at 100% after user created a GCP account. No actual usage consumed. Blocks all pro model access entirely.

signals.topic: OOM crash — JavaScript heap out of memory when processing batches of photos
signals.summary: The CLI crashes with a fatal heap out of memory error when processing a batch of photos. The Node.js heap reaches 7.9 GB before GC fails, resulting in process termination. This is a resource management bug that causes complete process failure.
signals.review_reason: Single instance of OOM crash with full GC logs showing heap exhaustion at 7.9 GB. While count=1, the crash is a complete process termination with data loss potential. Not a common path for most users but clearly a critical failure for batch processing workloads. Count=1 means P2 per rules.

source_issues.title: Too much memory used
source_issues.evidence: FATAL: Reached heap limit. Heap reached 7994 MB before GC failure. Crash occurs when processing photo batches. Process terminates with no recovery.

signals.topic: Tool save misses dependencies for imports with inline comments
signals.summary: When saving function-based tools with `make_gradio_app=True`, imports that have inline comments (e.g., `# noqa: F401`) are not detected by the current regex-based parser. This causes the exported tool's `requirements.txt` to be missing required dependencies, making the exported tool fail at runtime.
aliases: import detection fails with inline comments
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug: tool export produces an incomplete requirements.txt when imports use inline comments, directly causing exported tools to fail at runtime. The reproduction is concrete and the user impact (runtime failure due to missing dependency) is unambiguous.

source_issues.title: Tool save can miss requirements for commented imports
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: function tool using `import IPython  # noqa: F401` with `@tool` decorator, when saved with `make_gradio_app=True`, writes requirements.txt containing only `smolagents` instead of also `IPython`. Exported tool will fail at runtime due to missing dependency.

signals.topic: Codex model fails to respect 'never stop' instruction, breaking interactive agent sessions
signals.summary: When using Codex as the backend model, autoresearch's interactive sessions break because Codex ignores the instruction to never stop generating. Users lose the ability to monitor agent progress in real-time and pitch in arbitrarily, which is a core interactive workflow feature. This does not affect Claude model, making it a model-specific integration failure.
signals.review_reason: Codex integration fails to respect the 'never stop' instruction critical to autoresearch's interactive loop, breaking the core interactive session workflow for Codex users. While count=1 (single repo), the issue has 36 comments confirming active user pain and the failure is clearly in a primary workflow (interactive agent session). Excluded from P0 because count<3 and only affects one repo.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: 36 comments confirm active user discussion; user reports Codex ignores 'never stop' instruction, preventing interactive sessions that work with Claude. Core interactive feature unavailable for Codex users.

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware TypeError crash with RunnableWithFallbacks — subagent feature completely broken for model fallback users
signals.summary: resolve_model() raises TypeError when subagent model config is a RunnableWithFallbacks (standard LangChain pattern for provider redundancy), blocking subagent creation entirely.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed bugs (one labeled 'bug') all hitting the same TypeError crash when SubAgentMiddleware initializes with a RunnableWithFallbacks model. This is a regression from v0.3.8→v0.5 that completely blocks the subagent feature for any user using the standard LangChain with_fallbacks() pattern for provider redundancy. The crash occurs at middleware initialization, before any agent runs — no user can use subagents at all when this pattern is used.

source_issues.title: SubAgentMiddleware.resolve_model fails with RunnableWithFallbacks (TypeError: unhashable type)
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: unhashable type: 'RunnableWithFallbacks' when creating SubAgentMiddleware with a model wrapped via BaseChatModel.with_fallbacks(). Regression from v0.3.8. Standard LangChain pattern for provider redundancy (e.g. Azure primary → GCP fallback) is completely broken.

source_issues.title: SubAgentMiddleware.resolve_model fails with RunnableWithFallbacks (TypeError: unhashable type)
source_issues.evidence: Same TypeError with RunnableWithFallbacks in SubAgentMiddleware. Confirmed reproducible with ChatBedrockConverse + with_fallbacks(). No workaround.

source_issues.title: Subagents doesn't work with RunnableFallback anymore
source_issues.evidence: Subagents broken with RunnableFallback. Explicitly labeled as 'bug'. Full TypeError stack trace with resolve_model path.

signals.topic: Filesystem backend summarization offload fails on Windows causing non-recoverable message loss
signals.summary: Repeated summarization offload fails on Windows with 'String not found in file' error due to newline normalization mismatch, making older conversation messages non-recoverable from offloaded markdown.
aliases: Windows summarization offload String not found file
filesystem backend newline normalization offload fail
signals.review_reason: Two independent bugs (one labeled 'bug') both rooted in the same newline normalization issue in the filesystem backend. Issue #2861 is a concrete Windows-specific data loss scenario: older conversation messages become permanently non-recoverable from offloaded markdown on Windows. Issue #2856 confirms the root bug in perform_string_replacement that causes all string replacements to fail when trailing newlines differ. Together they show this is a systemic platform-specific failure with real data loss consequences.

source_issues.title: Summarization offload fails on Windows with "String not found in file" during conversation history append
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, summarization offload fails intermittently after first successful offload with 'String not found in file: ## Summarized at ...'. Root cause: newline normalization mismatch between binary read (download_files) and text-mode edit (backend.edit). Result: older messages become non-recoverable from offloaded markdown, contributing to divergence between checkpoint state and external history.

source_issues.title: Filesystem Backend edit "compared" bug
source_issues.evidence: File edit fails when content has a trailing \n but old_string does not. perform_string_replacement always finds content.count=0, causing repeated error reports. Affects any caller passing strings with trailing newlines. Labeled as 'bug'.

signals.topic: Interrupted subagent run overwrites parent thread state — conversation history restoration completely broken
signals.summary: When a subagent run is interrupted mid-execution, threads.search() returns the subgraph's internal messages instead of the parent graph's messages, losing the user's original prompt and making history restoration impossible.
aliases: subgraph state pollutes parent thread history
signals.review_reason: Confirmed data loss: subagent interruption causes complete overwrite of parent thread state. User's original prompt is replaced, the task tool call is lost, and conversation history is non-restorable. This is not a rare edge case — it affects any subagent run that gets interrupted (network issues, timeouts, Ctrl+C). Any application relying on thread history for continuity is broken.

source_issues.title: Interrupted subagent run overwrites parent thread state — history restoration broken
source_issues.evidence: When a run is interrupted mid-execution, threads.search() returns subgraph's internal messages as values.messages. The user's original message is replaced by the subagent's input prompt, the task tool call is missing, and parent graph messages are gone. Any app that restores conversations from thread history is broken for interrupted subagent runs. Complete data loss of parent thread state.

signals.topic: Subagent streaming fails — streaming tokens not delivered when using stream_mode='messages' with subgraphs
signals.summary: Using agent.stream() with stream_mode='messages', subgraphs=True, and version='v2' does not deliver subagent LLM tokens to the client. The official documentation's streaming example produces no subagent output.
aliases: subagent streaming not working stream_mode messages
signals.review_reason: The official documentation's streaming example is completely broken — users following the docs get zero subagent token output. This is a core API feature (streaming) that fails silently, forcing users to debug undocumented behavior. Labeled 'bug' with clear reproduction steps. The fact that the docs issue (#3229) also flags this confirms it affects real users following official guidance.

source_issues.title: Stream on subagent not working as expected
source_issues.evidence: Using official documentation's streaming code with agent.stream(stream_mode='messages', subgraphs=True, version='v2') — subagent LLM tokens are not streamed. The official documentation example produces no subagent output at all. Also cross-references docs issue #3229 about the streaming section being about tracing/metadata, not actual token streaming.

signals.topic: ACP CLI fails to enable ACP — import error despite deepagents-acp installed
signals.summary: deepagents-cli --acp raises ImportError for 'SessionConfigOption' from 'acp.schema', preventing ACP mode from being enabled despite deepagents-acp being installed.
aliases: ACP dependencies not available cannot import SessionConfigOption
signals.review_reason: A user-facing critical block: ACP mode cannot be enabled at all due to an ImportError, despite following the correct installation instructions. This is a complete functional blockage for any user trying to use the ACP feature of deepagents-cli. Labeled 'bug' with clear reproduction and error message.

source_issues.title: Cannot enable acp with deepagents-cli
source_issues.evidence: After installing deepagents-cli with --with deepagents-acp and running deepagents --acp, an ImportError is raised: cannot import name 'SessionConfigOption' from 'acp.schema'. The schema.py file exists at the expected path but the import fails. ACP mode cannot be enabled at all. Labeled as 'bug'.

signals.topic: Path traversal vulnerability in FileChatMessageHistory allows arbitrary file read/write via unsanitized session_id
signals.summary: FileChatMessageHistory中session_id参数未做路径校验，存在相对路径遍历和绝对路径注入两种绕过方式，可读取服务器任意文件
signals.review_reason: 两个issue均描述了FileChatMessageHistory中session_id未做路径校验的安全漏洞，可导致任意文件读取(#36890生产代码)和开发者复制不安全示例(#36887文档)。count=2影响两个不同方面(代码+文档)，具有明确安全影响证据（完整复现读取/etc/passwd），属于关键安全漏洞。

source_issues.title: Security: path traversal in FileChatMessageHistory via unsanitized session_id
source_issues.evidence: 生产代码直接使用os.path.join(storage_path, session_id)，用户可通过session_id=../../etc/passwd或session_id=/etc/passwd绕过storage_path限制，读取任意文件。提供了完整复现代码，可读/etc/passwd等敏感文件。

source_issues.title: Security: path traversal in FileChatMessageHistory docstring example via unsanitized session_id
source_issues.evidence: 官方文档示例代码中直接展示未校验的session_id用法，开发者在生产代码中复制此示例后存在相同路径遍历风险，传播了不安全实践。

signals.topic: test_stream_error_callback has wrong assertion expecting [] instead of [[]] for empty stream error result
signals.summary: FakeListChatModel的流式错误回调测试中，当error_on_chunk_number=0时，回调接收到的generations为[[]]而非预期的[]，测试断言错误
aliases: stream error callback test assertion wrong
signals.review_reason: 两个issue描述的是测试断言值错误(测试本身而非产品bug)：empty stream error时generations应为[[]]而非[]。xfail掩盖了测试期望错误，但这是开发者体验问题，不直接阻断终端用户主流程，影响范围为使用FakeListChatModel stream error功能的开发者。count=2但严重性较低。

source_issues.title: test_stream_error_callback expects [] instead of [[]] for empty stream error result
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供了完整可复现测试用例，明确指出assert [[]] == []失败，xfail掩盖了测试期望值错误而非实际产品bug，为测试质量问题而非用户可见bug。

source_issues.title: test_stream_error_callback expects [] instead of [[]] for empty stream error result
source_issues.evidence: 同#36866的重复issue，在langchain-core中反映相同测试断言问题。

signals.topic: Agent default max iterations 9999 causes massive uncontrolled API costs with no documentation warning
signals.summary: Agent默认递归次数9999无文档说明，用户一下午损失800元API费用
