signals.review_reason: 用户实际损失800元API费用，为明确的主流程阻断性成本损失问题。无文档说明且默认值极高(9999)直接导致用户主流程被高额计费阻断，满足P0高频+主流程阻断+强用户影响证据的组合条件（虽count=1但review_reason提供强财务证据支撑）。

source_issues.title: 兄弟，agent默认递归次数是9_999？文档里也从未交代，一下午浪费我800元，你要坑死我？
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确报告在正常使用agent过程中，因max_iterations默认值为9999且文档无任何说明，导致一个下午产生约800元人民币的API调用费用，为主流程阻断性问题。

signals.topic: Structured output fails in multi-turn conversations when appending assistant response to message context
signals.summary: 多轮对话中向消息历史追加assistant角色响应后，structured output在第二轮调用时抛出ValueError崩溃
signals.review_reason: 多轮对话是agent的核心使用场景，在追加assistant响应后structured output第二轮调用直接抛出ValueError导致崩溃，为明确的阻断性问题，影响关键功能(structured output)。count=1但影响明确且严重。

source_issues.title: Structured Output Fails When Appending Assistant Response to Context
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供了可复现代码：使用with_structured_output()在多轮对话中，追加assistant消息后第二轮调用直接抛出ValueError崩溃，阻断主流程。

signals.topic: Importing langchain.agents breaks BaseLLM class construction on upcoming Pydantic main branch
signals.summary: import langchain.agents后，后续创建BaseLLM在Pydantic main分支上会TypeError崩溃
signals.review_reason: 虽然目前影响有限(Pydantic 2.14尚未发布)，但问题已被Pydantic维护者确认根因，且一旦Pydantic 2.14发布将影响所有使用BaseLLM的用户群体，为明确的主流程阻断兼容性问题。Pydantic 2.13.x可正常工作。

source_issues.title: Importing langchain.agents breaks BaseLLM class construction on Pydantic main
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在Pydantic main分支上，import langchain.agents后再创建BaseLLM会TypeError崩溃。已识别根因：pydantic.py中_create_subset_model_v2直接写入__annotations__破坏了Python不变式，由Pydantic维护者确认。Pydantic 2.14发布后将影响所有用户。

signals.topic: create_react_agent cannot leverage Bedrock/Anthropic prompt caching due to no cache point placement control
signals.summary: Users of create_react_agent with Bedrock Converse API cannot effectively use prompt caching because there is no way to inject cache points into the conversation history replay, causing significant redundant token processing costs in multi-turn agent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Users experience obvious cost loss (up to 90% redundant processing) in production multi-turn agent workflows due to inability to leverage prompt caching. This is a main flow cost issue, not a blocking failure but has significant financial impact.

source_issues.title: create_react_agent: support cache point placement in conversation history
source_issues.evidence: User reports 90% cost reduction possible with proper cache point placement. Measured impact shows $0.42/review in redundant prefix processing that could be saved. Multi-turn ReAct agents replay ~4K tokens of stable prefix on every turn.

signals.topic: OpenTelemetry instrumentation causes TypeError crash on agent invocation (1.1.7 regression)
signals.summary: Regression in langgraph 1.1.7 causes agents to crash with TypeError when OpenTelemetry instrumentation is enabled, breaking AWS Bedrock AgentCore deployments.
signals.review_reason: Regression bug introduced in 1.1.7 causes main flow blocking - agents crash immediately on invocation when OpenTelemetry instrumentation is used. Confirmed breaking change between versions with clear user impact on deployed agents.

source_issues.title: langgraph 1.1.7 regression: TypeError with opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain
source_issues.evidence: Crash occurs at invocation time with TypeError: handlers must inherit GraphCallbackHandler. Affects AWS Bedrock AgentCore deployments using opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain. Version 1.1.6 works, 1.1.7 crashes.

signals.topic: Pydantic state alias output asymmetry breaks coherent camelCase/snake_case API contracts
signals.summary: Users with alias_generator=to_camel get mixed-casing output (outer snake_case, inner camelCase) from invoke(), stream_mode=values, get_state(), and checkpoint snapshots, breaking expected API contract.
signals.review_reason: Users with typical API boundary configurations (camelCase JSON APIs) experience experience degradation - they can send camelCase in but cannot get coherent camelCase out without workarounds. Breaks expected API contract.

source_issues.title: Pydantic state aliased fields: output wire format asymmetry (follow-up to #2555)
source_issues.evidence: Users with alias_generator=to_camel get mixed-casing output (outer snake_case, inner camelCase). Input works (fixed in PR #6634) but output is incoherent without client-side shim. Affects invoke(), stream_mode=values, get_state(), and checkpoint snapshots.

signals.topic: RetryPolicy jitter violates max_interval contract causing retry sleeps to exceed configured maximum
signals.summary: RetryPolicy with jitter=True adds jitter after the min guard, making actual sleep reach up to 2x the configured max_interval, violating documented contract.
signals.review_reason: Users relying on RetryPolicy's documented max_interval contract experience unexpected behavior - retries can take twice as long as configured maximum. This violates explicit documentation promises and can cause unexpected delays in production systems.

source_issues.title: RetryPolicy: jitter can cause sleep to exceed max_interval
source_issues.evidence: With jitter=True and max_interval=0.5, actual sleep can reach 1.5s (0.5 + random.uniform(0,1)). Documentation promises max_interval is 'maximum amount of time that may elapse between retries' but implementation adds jitter after min guard.

signals.topic: TAG_NOSTREAM suppresses LLM tokens but not node output messages in stream_mode=messages
signals.summary: Nodes tagged with TAG_NOSTREAM only suppress LLM token streaming but not node output messages, breaking per-subagent streaming control for frameworks like Deep Agents.
signals.review_reason: Users relying on TAG_NOSTREAM for streaming control get inconsistent behavior - key feature for per-subagent control is unavailable. Downstream frameworks (Deep Agents, CopilotKit) are affected.

source_issues.title: TAG_NOSTREAM inconsistency in StreamMessagesHandler: suppresses LLM tokens but not node output messages
source_issues.evidence: Users tagging nodes with nostream expect ALL message streaming suppressed but only LLM tokens are suppressed. Node output messages still stream. Breaks frameworks like Deep Agents that rely on per-subagent streaming control.

signals.topic: Plugin daemon 'no proper instance' error prevents configuring model providers and adding custom models
signals.summary: Plugin daemon returns 'no proper instance' error when users try to configure model providers (Gemini, VLLM) or add custom models via plugins. The error occurs even when the plugin runtime is confirmed ready, blocking core model integration functionality.
aliases: plugin daemon no proper instance error
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues both show the same root cause: the plugin daemon cannot dispatch requests to ready plugin instances. This blocks the fundamental workflow of adding and configuring model providers, directly preventing users from using custom models on self-hosted deployments.

source_issues.title: Gemini provider validation fails with no proper instance even when plugin runtime is ready
source_issues.evidence: Gemini plugin installed and runtime confirmed ready, yet validation fails with PluginDaemonInternalServerError: no proper instance when saving provider credentials. Self-hosted Docker users cannot configure Gemini.

source_issues.title: Plugin unable to add model
source_issues.evidence: VLLM plugin installed offline, adding Qwen3.5 model fails with PluginDaemonInternalServerError: no proper instance. Core model addition workflow blocked on self-hosted Docker.

signals.topic: Workflow execution stuck in 'running' status forever after exceeding APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME timeout
signals.summary: When workflows run longer than APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME, the UI shows 'running' indefinitely with no resolution. Database and Celery have no record of the timed-out run. This permanently blocks the workflow run from completing and leaves users with zombie workflow entries.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker. The workflow never terminates, leaving the UI permanently stuck and the run record unresolvable. Users cannot proceed after the timeout. Confirmed reproducible behavior with clear steps and no workaround.

source_issues.title: Workflow runs indefinitely past APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME, stuck in "running" status [UI]
source_issues.evidence: Workflow exceeds configured APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME (default 1200s) but UI remains 'running' forever. Database workflow_runs table is empty. Celery worker has no task record. No timeout error ever shown.

signals.topic: PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion causing full service outage after upgrade to v1.13.3
signals.summary: After upgrading from 1.13.2 to 1.13.3, PostgreSQL connection pool exhausts rapidly with 94+ idle connections from the API container. This causes Internal Server Error on the website and 500 errors on all API calls. The situation is permanent without restart.
signals.review_reason: Full service outage triggered by a routine upgrade. Every user interaction becomes impossible due to 500 errors and internal server error page. This is a critical P0: main flow completely blocked, reproducible by simply opening a few chats and asking questions.

source_issues.title: connections to postgresql exhausted
source_issues.evidence: Upgrading to 1.13.3 causes PostgreSQL connection exhaustion: 94 idle connections from docker-api-1 container, FATAL error 'sorry, too many clients already'. Site shows Internal Server Error, all API calls return 500. Situation is permanent without restart, persists for over an hour.

signals.topic: Sandbox code execution times out on large dataset processing, blocking batch workflows
signals.summary: When processing large files (e.g., 16MB Excel with 11,344 rows) through the code node, the sandbox times out and fails with a misleading 'network issue' error. This blocks batch processing workflows that handle moderate-sized datasets.
aliases: code node timeout on large data
signals.review_reason: This blocks the primary use case of batch data processing through the code node. The error message is misleading (blames network when it's a timeout), causing users to misdiagnose the issue. Workaround is unavailable for moderate-sized datasets.

source_issues.title: Failed to execute code, which is likely a network issue, please check if the sandbox service is running. ( Error: timed out )
source_issues.evidence: Workflow processing 16MB Excel file with 11,344 rows times out in the code node with 'timed out' error. Misleadingly suggests 'network issue / check sandbox service'. Small data works fine. Core use case of batch data processing is blocked.

signals.topic: Built-in web scraper tool completely non-functional on Dify Cloud platform
signals.summary: The built-in web scraper tool fails entirely on the Dify Cloud platform, preventing users from using this default built-in tool. No workaround available since it is a platform-level failure.
signals.review_reason: A default built-in tool is completely non-functional on the cloud platform. Users relying on web scraping have no workaround. Although count=1, the 'cloud' label and severity (complete tool failure) justify P1.

source_issues.title: web scraper sometime not work
source_issues.evidence: The built-in web scraper tool is entirely non-functional on the Dify Cloud platform. Users cannot use the default built-in tool with no local workaround available.

signals.topic: v2 ADD-only pipeline silently stores duplicate contradictory memories, causing data bloat and degraded retrieval quality
signals.summary: The v2.0.0 ADD-only extraction architecture lacks semantic conflict resolution. When users add contradictory facts (e.g., 'my name is Alice' followed by 'my name is Bob'), both are permanently stored as ADD events. The documentation promises 'Latest truth wins when contradictions detected' but this is unimplemented. A production audit of 10,134 entries found 97.8% were junk, largely due to this root cause.
aliases: v2 data bloat from duplicate memories
signals.review_reason: Core data integrity failure in v2's ADD-only architecture. Documentation explicitly promises conflict resolution which is unimplemented. 3 independent reports including a production audit of 10,134 entries demonstrating 97.8% data bloat as direct consequence. Users experience permanently degraded storage and retrieval quality — this is a primary value proposition failure.

source_issues.title: ADD-only architecture doesn't implement conflict resolution for semantically similar memories
source_issues.evidence: Both memories return ADD event, both stored permanently. MD5 hash dedup only catches exact duplicates. Code evidence in main.py:784-803 showing only exact hash matching exists.

source_issues.title: fix: semantic conflict resolution missing in v2 ADD-only pipeline
source_issues.evidence: Provides exact reproduction steps showing both 'my name is Alice' and 'my name is Bob' stored as separate ADD events. get_all() returns 2 instead of 1. Root cause: no UPDATE code path in v2 pipeline.

source_issues.title: What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk
source_issues.evidence: Production audit spanning 32 days. Identifies missing semantic dedup / conflict resolution as root cause of 97.8% junk entries. gemma2:2b and Claude Sonnet 4.6 both affected.

signals.topic: MemoryClient search path broken — crashes with ValueError on entity params and TypeError on dict iteration
signals.summary: The Mem0 proxy chat path is completely broken when using MemoryClient (Mem0(api_key='...')). Two bugs prevent any chat completion from succeeding: (1) _fetch_relevant_memories passes entity params as top-level kwargs to search(), which rejects them, raising ValueError; (2) MemoryClient branch iterates the response dict instead of dict['results'], causing TypeError.
signals.review_reason: Proxy MemoryClient path is completely broken — any user calling mem0.chat via API key gets a crash immediately. Memory.add() crashes on any list-typed content (standard multimodal format) when vision is disabled. Both are main code paths that fail with unhandled exceptions.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Proxy MemoryClient search path is broken
source_issues.evidence: Two confirmed bugs: (1) ValueError: 'Top-level entity parameters {user_id,...} are not supported in search(). Use filters=...' (2) TypeError: 'string indices must be integers' from iterating dict instead of dict['results']. Reproduction code provided.

source_issues.title: AttributeError crash in Memory.add() when message content is a list and vision is disabled
source_issues.evidence: Memory.add() crashes with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'generate_response' when any message has a list-typed content field (standard multimodal format) and vision is not explicitly enabled. Blocks any multimodal message from being processed.

signals.topic: Self-hosted endpoint configuration silently ignored for custom LLM/embedding providers, causing 401 errors or complete embedding failure
signals.summary: Two issues affect self-hosted users with custom LLM or embedding providers. (1) OpenMemory: LLM_BASE_URL and EMBEDDER_BASE_URL env vars are correctly read but silently overwritten by DB config, causing all requests to go to api.openai.com → 401 errors. (2) Plugin with Ollama: mem0 uses OpenAI-style /v1/embeddings endpoint which Ollama doesn't support, causing 'fetch failed' on every embedding call.
signals.review_reason: Self-hosted deployment is a core use case. Two independent issues confirm that custom LLM/embedding providers (proxies, Ollama, vLLM, Azure) silently break — OpenMemory gets 401 errors, plugin gets complete embedding failure. No error path alerts the user that their endpoint is being ignored; requests silently go to the wrong endpoint.

source_issues.title: OpenMemory: DB config overrides LLM_BASE_URL / EMBEDDER_BASE_URL env vars — openai_base_url lost for self-hosted users
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: memory.py line 443-444 DB config completely replaces env-var-derived config. openai_base_url is silently lost. All LLM requests go to api.openai.com instead of configured custom endpoint. Cites previous reports #3238 (Jul 2025) and #2691 (PR never merged).

source_issues.title: mem0 plugin fails with 'TypeError: fetch failed' when using Ollama – wrong embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings)
source_issues.evidence: mem0 calls /v1/embeddings (OpenAI-style) for Ollama but Ollama uses /api/embeddings. Every embedding call fails with TypeError: fetch failed. Root cause: hardcoded OpenAI-style embedding endpoint path.

signals.topic: Silent data loss: metadata filter AND operator drops all but last condition for a given key, and plugin JSON parse error destroys entire OpenClaw config
signals.summary: Two distinct silent data loss issues: (1) _process_metadata_filters silently drops all filter conditions for a given key in an AND block except the last one — users believe their compound filter is applied when it is not; (2) readFullConfig() on JSON parse error overwrites openclaw.json with only the mem0 plugin entry, destroying all other configuration (Claude settings, workspace config, etc.).
aliases: OpenClaw config destroyed JSON parse error
signals.review_reason: Two separate silent data loss modes: (1) filter results silently incorrect — users act on wrong data without knowing it; (2) entire Claude/OpenClaw workspace config permanently destroyed by a single JSON parse error. Both are irreversible data loss with no user warning.

source_issues.title: Data Loss in `_process_metadata_filters` with `AND` operator
source_issues.evidence: AND operator in metadata filters overwrites conditions if multiple apply to the same key within the same AND block. All but the last condition for a given key are silently dropped. Query results are silently incorrect.

source_issues.title: Plugin silently destroys entire OpenClaw config on JSON parse error
source_issues.evidence: When readFullConfig() encounters any JSON parse error or returns empty object, it overwrites the entire openclaw.json with only the mem0 plugin entry. All other configuration (Claude settings, workspace config, other plugins) is permanently destroyed. No backup created.

signals.topic: Concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index, causing IndexError and incorrect/missing reads
signals.summary: When multiple coroutines call AsyncMemory add/update/delete concurrently, the Qdrant HNSW index becomes corrupted. Subsequent search() and get() calls either raise 'index N is out of bounds' or return wrong results. The process must be restarted and the index rebuilt to recover.
aliases: Qdrant index corruption under concurrent load
signals.review_reason: Data corruption that renders subsequent reads incorrect or throwing uncaught IndexError. Affects any async workload (e.g., parallel agent events) — a primary use case for AsyncMemory. No workaround available short of index rebuild. Process restart required to recover. Production-observed over months before root cause identified.

source_issues.title: Bug: concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index ('index N is out of bounds')
source_issues.evidence: 20 concurrent writers reliably reproduces corruption. Root cause: Qdrant HNSW upsert is not re-entrant; parallel writes arrive while graph construction is in-flight. Subsequent reads return wrong results or raise IndexError. No fix merged yet (open issue). Discovered in sustained production workloads over several months.

signals.topic: Python sample hosting directories have multiple configuration errors preventing beginners from running examples
signals.summary: Multiple Python hosting samples (a2a, durabletask, azure_functions) have missing or incorrect requirements.txt files, wrong package references (foundry vs openai), and mismatched environment variable templates (FOUNDRY_* vs AZURE_OPENAI_*).
signals.review_reason: Four independent issues all pointing to Python hosting sample configuration errors that block beginners from running examples. Impact is clear and concrete: missing requirements.txt causes pip install failure, wrong package name causes import confusion and fragility, wrong env vars cause silent configuration failure, and missing redis causes immediate ModuleNotFoundError. Together these represent a systematic onboarding failure.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] a2a/ sample missing requirements.txt — beginners cannot install dependencies
source_issues.evidence: No requirements.txt in a2a sample. pip install fails. Multiple required packages (agent-framework-a2a, uvicorn, httpx) missing.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] durabletask/02_multi_agent requirements.txt references wrong package (foundry instead of openai)
source_issues.evidence: Code imports agent_framework.openai but requirements.txt installs packages/foundry. Misleading and fragile.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] azure_functions/02_multi_agent — config template and requirements.txt mismatch (Foundry vs OpenAI)
source_issues.evidence: local.settings.json.template has FOUNDRY_* env vars but code uses AZURE_OPENAI_*. Beginners configure wrong vars and get silent failure.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] redis package missing from requirements.txt in streaming samples
source_issues.evidence: Two streaming samples import redis.asyncio but redis is absent from requirements.txt. ModuleNotFoundError at import time immediately blocks execution.

signals.topic: Python hosting samples documentation lacks orientation README and prerequisite install commands
signals.summary: The python/samples/04-hosting/ directory lacks a top-level README, and individual sample READMEs for azure_functions and durabletask do not provide quick-install commands for prerequisites, causing beginners to hit multiple failure points.
aliases: Python hosting sample onboarding docs missing
signals.review_reason: Two documentation gaps that degrade the beginner onboarding experience. While these are docs issues rather than code bugs, they cause measurable experience degradation — beginners get lost navigating hosting options and must manually discover prerequisite install commands. Together they form a coherent documentation pain point.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] azure_functions & durabletask READMEs need quick-install commands for prerequisites
source_issues.evidence: Azure Functions and durabletask READMEs list external prerequisites but provide no install commands. Beginners hit missing tools at multiple points without guidance.

source_issues.title: Python: [Samples][Python] 04-hosting/ directory missing top-level README to orient beginners
source_issues.evidence: 04-hosting/ has 4 sub-directories with no top-level README. Beginners must open each subdirectory individually to understand hosting options.

signals.topic: Python SDK background mode causes infinite tool-call loop and returns empty response when combined with function tools
signals.summary: When using `background=True` with local function tools, the SDK repeatedly retrieves the same completed background response via `responses.retrieve()` instead of POSTing tool results. The tool loop exhausts 40 iterations silently and returns empty text.
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 issue: it causes primary workflow failure and key functionality to be unusable. The evidence is extremely strong — httpx logs show 1 POST followed by ~40 GETs to the same response_id, tool called 120 times with identical arguments, and final response is empty. This completely blocks agents using background mode with tools from ever producing a result.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: `background=True` causes infinite tool-call loop, tool-result submissions inherit background mode
source_issues.evidence: HTTP traffic proves 1 POST + ~40 GETs to same response_id, zero tool-result POSTs. Tool called 120 times with identical arguments. Final response.text is empty. Silent failure — no exception raised.

signals.topic: .NET Workflows: off-thread RunStatus race causes GetStatusAsync to return incorrect Running state after ResumeAsync halts
signals.summary: In StreamingRunEventStream.RunLoopAsync, _runStatus is unconditionally flipped to Running after each _inputWaiter wake-up. This allows a stale signal to flip status back to Running after the consumer has already observed the halt signal.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed .NET workflow bug with clear user impact: off-thread race condition causes incorrect RunStatus to be reported to callers, which can lead to incorrect orchestration decisions. The status reporting is a core workflow contract and its corruption undermines workflow reliability. Single issue but clear impact on workflow state correctness.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Workflows - Fix off-thread RunStatus race where GetStatusAsync can return Running after ResumeAsync halts
source_issues.evidence: Race condition causes GetStatusAsync to return incorrect Running state after ResumeAsync has halted the workflow. Downstream orchestrator code that relies on RunStatus to make decisions will see stale Running state.

signals.topic: PowerFx expressions in declarative workflow samples fail when dotnet runtime is not installed
signals.summary: Running the declarative workflow sample on a devcontainer that does not have the dotnet runtime pre-installed causes PowerFx expression evaluation to fail with an unhandled error message.
signals.review_reason: A declarative workflow sample crashes when dotnet runtime is absent. The devcontainer ships with this sample but lacks a required dependency, causing first-run failure. While the workaround (installing dotnet manually) exists, this blocks the declarative workflow feature from working in the default devcontainer setup.

source_issues.title: Python: .NET: [Bug]:
source_issues.evidence: Running workflow_declarative sample on devcontainer without dotnet: 'Workflow execution error: PowerFx is not available (dotnet runtime not installed). Expression =inputs.age cannot be evaluated.' Devcontainer should pre-install dotnet for this sample to work out of the box.

signals.topic: Self-signed certificate chain blocks browser installation in enterprise/corporate environments
signals.summary: When Playwright installs browsers behind corporate firewalls with self-signed certificate chains, it fails with SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN. Users cannot install browsers at all, blocking the entire tool from being used. No documented workaround or whitelistable endpoint.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users in corporate environments are completely blocked from installing Playwright browsers due to self-signed certificate chains. This is a complete blocker — the tool cannot be used at all. No documented workaround exists. While each is a separate report, the same root cause (TLS inspection by corporate proxies) makes this a systemic enterprise adoption issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Unable to Install because of self-signed certificate in certificate chain error is blocked by company security
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'unable to download browsers' with SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN error, blocked by company security policy. IT requests whitelistable IP/port with no answer.

source_issues.title: [Docs]: Workaround or url/port that needs to be unblocked to allow playwright browser install
source_issues.evidence: User in corporate environment gets SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN on playwright.ps1 install. IT explicitly asks for a whitelistable IP/port. Docs insufficient to unblock.

signals.topic: v1.59 regression: WebKit on Linux breaks WASM SIMD crypto operations producing incorrect results
signals.summary: WebKit on Linux in v1.59.x produces incorrect output from WASM SIMD instructions used in cryptographic hashing (argon2), causing test assertions to fail with wrong values. Works in v1.58.2.
aliases: WebKit Linux WASM SIMD wrong hash
signals.review_reason: A clear v1.59 regression affecting WebKit Linux that silently produces incorrect cryptographic output from WASM SIMD operations. Tests that appeared to pass in v1.58.2 now fail with wrong values, and the wrongness is non-obvious — a test checking correctness would pass incorrectly. This undermines trust in test results for any WASM SIMD workload on WebKit Linux.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: v1.59 breaks WebKit WASM SIMD on Linux
source_issues.evidence: User has a WASM SIMD-based argon2 e2e test that works with v1.58.2 on WebKit Linux but fails in v1.59.x with wrong hash values. All other browsers pass. External repo with reproducible test case provided. Regression confirmed.

signals.topic: Docker image version mismatch breaks CI: Playwright v1.59 requires browsers not bundled in matching docker image
signals.summary: Upgrading from v1.58.2-noble to v1.59.1-noble docker image causes CI failure because the chromium_headless_shell executable is missing. Error message instructs user to downgrade docker image, effectively blocking the upgrade path.
aliases: docker image chromium executable missing after upgrade
signals.review_reason: A single-point upgrade of the official Docker image breaks CI entirely. The error is unambiguous and self-inflicted (Playwright's own error message tells users to downgrade). This blocks automated upgrade paths for any CI pipeline using the official images, a core deployment pattern.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 1.59 breaks CI
source_issues.evidence: User simply upgrades docker image from v1.58.2-noble to v1.59.1-noble and CI breaks with 'Executable doesn't exist at /ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1208'. Playwright itself tells user to downgrade. No clear upgrade path.

signals.topic: Playwright assertion retry logic skips final DOM check before timeout deadline, wasting up to 1000ms of timeout budget
signals.summary: retryWithProgressAndTimeouts uses escalating intervals [0, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 1000]. For timeouts between 1851-2849ms, the last retry at ~1850ms sleeps for 1000ms, during which the deadline fires and aborts without a final check. Elements that appeared before the deadline are missed, causing false test failures.
aliases: toBeVisible misses visible element before deadline
retry interval misses element at 1900ms with 2500ms timeout
signals.review_reason: A systematic bug in the core assertion retry engine that causes false test failures. The root cause is precisely identified: the retry loop sleeps for the full interval while racing against a deadline, and when the deadline fires mid-sleep, no final DOM check occurs. Any timeout value in a specific range (1851-2849ms) will silently waste up to 999ms of budget and miss elements that are already visible. This affects all locator assertions and is not edge-case — any test with a timeout in this range is affected.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Expect assertions with escalating retry intervals skip final check before deadline, wasting up to 1000ms of timeout budget
source_issues.evidence: Detailed repro: element becomes visible at 1900ms, timeout is 2500ms. Test fails anyway because check at 1850ms sleeps 1000ms, deadline fires at 2500ms, no final check. Root cause precisely identified in retryWithProgressAndTimeouts. Affects all locator assertions: toBeVisible, toBeHidden, toContainText, toHaveText, etc.

signals.topic: page.route() does not reliably intercept all matching requests in Page Object Model setup — causes silent test failures
signals.summary: When page.route() is attached in a Page Object Model base class constructor, requests during initial page load often do not include injected headers. No warning is raised. Tests silently fail because the expected header is absent, making root cause diagnosis difficult.
signals.review_reason: A reliability issue in the core page.route API used for request interception in test setups. When used in POM patterns (a very common architecture), requests during initial page load are silently missed with no warning. This causes test logic that depends on modified headers to fail silently, and since no error is raised, the failure mode is hard to diagnose. It directly undermines a core use case (request interception/mocking) for a significant portion of users following standard POM patterns.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: page.route used in Page Object Model does not reliably intercept all matching requests
source_issues.evidence: User attaches page.route in base page class constructor, matching pattern '**/*<substring>*'. Only a subset of matching requests include injected headers. Requests during initial page load are the ones most frequently missed. No warning or error is raised — tests silently fail with wrong headers, making diagnosis hard. Screenshots showing mismatched requests attached.

signals.topic: Python Redis connector: vector search and delete operations are completely broken
signals.summary: The Python Redis connector has multiple critical bugs that render vector operations unusable: (1) vector search (`FT.SEARCH`) raises `AttributeError` due to redisvl API incompatibility; (2) `RedisJsonCollection.delete()` silently fails to remove records when prefix mode is enabled; (3) `FT.CREATE` sends malformed PREFIX arguments causing index overlap in multi-collection deployments. All three issues share the same root cause: the connector code is incompatible with the latest redisvl version and has missing prefix handling.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct but related bugs in the Python Redis connector that collectively make vector operations unusable. #13896 is a complete functional block — all vector searches fail with AttributeError for any user with redisvl >= 0.5. #13904 causes silent data persistence — delete returns success but records remain. #13894 causes incorrect multi-collection behavior. All three have clear wire-level reproduction evidence, root cause analysis, and affect every Python Redis connector user who resolves dependencies fresh or enables prefix mode. Count=3 meets P0 threshold.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (`FT.SEARCH`) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: Every search call raises `AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index'`. Root cause: connector written against redisvl 0.4.x API, but `~= 0.4` pin resolves to redisvl 0.15.0 where the API changed. Additionally, `KeyError: 'vector'` when `include_vectors=False` (the default).

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Delete sends `JSON.DEL 'cov-1'` instead of `JSON.DEL 'sk_cov_xxx:cov-1'`, returns 0 (no error), and the record remains. Silent failure with no indication to caller. Root cause: `_inner_delete` does not call `_get_redis_key()` to apply the prefix.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed `FT.CREATE PREFIX` (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: `FT.CREATE` sends `PREFIX 27 r e d i s _ j s o n _ l i s t _ d a t a _ m o d e l :` instead of `PREFIX 1 redis_json_list_data_model:`. Root cause: plain string passed to redis-py's `IndexDefinition(prefix=...)` is iterated character-by-character. In multi-collection deployments, overlapping prefixes cause cross-collection key matching.

signals.topic: .NET Google Gemini connector does not send tools/functions in API request — function calling completely broken
signals.summary: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletionService does not include the `tools` field in the API request to Gemini, making function/tool calling entirely non-functional even when plugins are correctly registered.
aliases: Google AI connector tools field missing
signals.review_reason: Function calling is a core Semantic Kernel feature. When it completely fails for an entire connector (Gemini), this is a significant user impact — any .NET developer relying on Gemini function calling will find their agent workflows broken. The bug was confirmed with HTTP trace logs showing the 'tools' field is absent. The issue is closed but marked stale, indicating the fix may not be merged or fully released.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: GoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion doesn't send tools/functions in API request
source_issues.evidence: When using AddGoogleAIGeminiChatCompletion with FunctionChoiceBehavior, the API request does not include the 'tools' field. The same configuration works correctly with AddOpenAIChatCompletion using Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Trace log shows settings are recognized but not serialized into the request.

signals.topic: .NET Amazon Bedrock connector: image content not passed to models — image captioning broken
signals.summary: BedrockChatCompletionService does not properly attach ImageContent metadata, causing all image-based tasks (captioning, VQA) to fail with the model responding it cannot see the image.
signals.review_reason: Image content handling is broken for Bedrock, which is a critical limitation for any multimodal use case. The bug has clear reproduction steps, a confirmed working Python reference showing the correct API format, and the same code path works with Azure OpenAI — proving the client code is at fault. Count=1 prevents P0, but the functional gap is significant for affected users.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Amazon BedrockChatCompletionService image-to-text (captioning) not working
source_issues.evidence: ImageContent with MIME types image/png, image/jpeg, image/bmp causes the model to respond 'I don't see an image'. The same code works with Azure OpenAI gpt-4o. A working Python reference implementation shows the correct `image` block structure in the request payload.

signals.topic: OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings ExtensionData custom parameters not included in HTTP request
signals.summary: Custom parameters added via ExtensionData dictionary in OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings are silently dropped and never sent in the HTTP JSON request, blocking users from passing provider-specific parameters like enable_thinking.
signals.review_reason: Custom parameter injection via ExtensionData is a documented extensibility mechanism that is silently broken. While count=1 prevents P0/P1, the inability to pass provider-specific parameters blocks real use cases (reasoning models, custom sampling controls). The bug was closed stale, indicating unresolved status.

source_issues.title: Bug: ExtensionData parameters not included in HTTP JSON request when using OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
source_issues.evidence: ExtensionData dictionary with custom parameters (e.g., enable_thinking) is not serialized into the HTTP request payload. The generated JSON request is missing the custom fields entirely. Users cannot pass provider-specific parameters.

signals.topic: .NET Ollama connector: DeepSeek reasoning/thinking content not returned
signals.summary: When using Ollama connector with DeepSeek models (deepseek-r1 series), the reasoning/thinking block is not extracted from the response, even though OllamaSharp's direct API returns it correctly.
aliases: reasoning content not parsed from Ollama
signals.review_reason: DeepSeek reasoning models are increasingly important for agentic workflows. Missing the reasoning/thinking content is a significant degradation for applications that depend on it. Count=1 limits priority to P2, but the gap is real and reproducible across deepseek-r1 variants.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: when using Ollama Connector to chat with deepseek models, there is no <think>feedback
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek-r1 models return thinking blocks that are visible via OllamaSharp's direct GenerateAsync method but are missing from Semantic Kernel's Ollama connector responses. The same connector works correctly with QwQ model which has different reasoning format. This suggests the connector's response parsing does not handle DeepSeek's think block format.

signals.topic: MCP child processes leak when McpConnectionManager is replaced — severe resource exhaustion
signals.summary: Long-running Codex daemon accumulates hundreds of orphaned MCP child processes consuming massive CPU and memory (492 children, 82GB RSS), caused by McpConnectionManager lacking proper Drop implementation.
signals.review_reason: Severe resource exhaustion bug. 492 orphaned MCP children at 35% CPU each accumulating 82GB RSS is a definitive user-impacting mainflow blocker for any user relying on MCP tools in a long-running session. This directly causes cost loss (CPU cycles) and process bloat that can destabilize the entire daemon.

source_issues.title: MCP child processes leak when McpConnectionManager is replaced
source_issues.evidence: 15-hour daemon accumulated 492 orphaned MCP children at 35% CPU each with 82GB cumulative RSS. Root cause: McpConnectionManager has no Drop impl, child cleanup depends on Arc refcount.

signals.topic: Native Windows Codex: workspace dependency repair fails with EPERM in sandbox — blocks core workflow
signals.summary: Windows users cannot run dependency repair because npx/tsx and esbuild fail with EPERM inside Codex's sandbox, while direct execution from PowerShell works normally.
signals.review_reason: Core workflow blocker on Windows. Dependency repair is a fundamental Codex workflow, and EPERM errors silently block it while the same tools work outside the sandbox. This prevents Windows users from using a key feature of the application.

source_issues.title: Native Windows Codex app: workspace dependency repair fails; npx/tsx and esbuild hit EPERM in sandbox
source_issues.evidence: npx/tsx fails with 'EPERM: operation not permitted, lstat' and esbuild fails with spawn EPERM. Direct binary execution from PowerShell works, confirming Codex Windows sandbox blocks filesystem access and child-process spawning needed for dependency repair.

signals.topic: Shell profile not loaded correctly after update — commands not found
signals.summary: After a recent Codex update, user shell profile rc is not sourced, causing Codex to fail to find programs and breaking command execution for users with custom shell environments.
aliases: bash profile not sourced after update
signals.review_reason: Regression introduced by recent update that breaks shell environment integration. Users with standard bash customizations (aliases, PATH modifications, environment variables) can no longer run commands through Codex, directly blocking normal usage.

source_issues.title: Bash profile is not loaded correctly
source_issues.evidence: User reports that after a recent update, codex claims not to find the simplest programs because shell profile rc is not being loaded. User has comprehensive bash setup with environments, aliases, and shell functions that previously worked.

signals.topic: Remote TUI remains stale after app-server slow-websocket disconnect — incorrect prompt routing
signals.summary: After the app-server disconnects a slow websocket client, the TUI can remain in a stale state showing 'Working' when the thread is actually complete, causing the next prompt to be incorrectly routed as turn/steer.
signals.review_reason: Session state corruption causes incorrect prompt routing (turn/steer vs new turn), leading to confused model behavior and potential work loss. Affects the TUI remote session workflow which is a primary Codex usage mode.

signals.topic: Realtime agent response truncation when tools execute during active response
signals.summary: When a tool is registered to a RealtimeAgent and triggers a create.response event while another response is already in progress, the agent response is cut off with a RealtimeError and the agent gets stuck waiting for user input.

Conversation already has an active response error
signals.review_reason: Explicit bug report (not feature request). User describes production use with v0.14.2 where realtime agent gets stuck after tool call. signals.topic: FuncSchema.to_call_args misplaces POSITIONAL_ONLY parameters into keyword args, causing TypeError at runtime
signals.summary: When a function parameter is POSITIONAL_ONLY and appears after *args in a tool function signature, FuncSchema.to_call_args incorrectly places it in keyword_args, which raises TypeError at runtime since positional-only parameters cannot be passed as keyword arguments.
aliases: POSITIONAL_ONLY parameter passed as keyword argument
signals.review_reason: The bug causes a hard runtime failure (TypeError) when a tool with POSITIONAL_ONLY params after *args is executed. This is a main-flow block for any affected tool function — the call fails entirely. Not cosmetic; directly prevents tool execution.

source_issues.title: FuncSchema.to_call_args incorrectly places POSITIONAL_ONLY params into keyword_args after *args
source_issues.evidence: Bug report describes a logic error in FuncSchema.to_call_args: after *args (seen_var_positional=True), POSITIONAL_ONLY params are added to keyword_args. But positional-only params cannot be passed as keyword args in Python, causing TypeError at call time. Reproduction: any tool function with positional-only params after *args will fail with TypeError when called through the SDK.

signals.topic: Run loop exceptions silently swallowed in stream_events() for early failures — debugging nightmare

Users must dig into internal task state to find the real failure reason.
aliases: silent run loop failures in streamed mode
signals.review_reason: While the result eventually finishes, the exception is silently swallowed — users see a clean-looking result with null values and no error, forcing them to introspect internal task state to find the real failure. This is a significant UX/devex pain that hides actual main-flow failures, making it difficult to debug sandbox startup errors.

source_issues.title: Surface run-loop exceptions in stream_events() for early failures

signals.topic: system.run: env variable injection and shell wrapper approval bypass allows connected agents to execute unintended commands
signals.summary: The system.run capability in LocalCommandRunner passes arbitrary env variables directly to ProcessStartInfo without sanitization, allowing agents to inject variables like GIT_SSH_COMMAND, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD, or BASH_ENV to alter approved command behavior. Additionally, shell wrappers (bash -c, powershell -Command, cmd /c, etc.) bypass exec approval policy because only the outer command is evaluated.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed security vulnerability with explicit code-level evidence: arbitrary env vars are copied to ProcessStartInfo without sanitization (LocalCommandRunner.cs:52), and shell wrappers bypass exec policy (only fullCommand evaluated at SystemCapability.cs:293). This allows a connected agent to escalate execution beyond approved policies, which is a direct user impact: agents can run unintended system commands. Issue is closed with merged PRs #186 and #181 addressing it, confirming the vulnerability was real and required code changes. Not P0 only because count=1 and no multiple independent reports.

source_issues.title: [Security] system.run: env variable injection and shell wrapper approval bypass
source_issues.evidence: Env dict parsed in SystemCapability.cs:266 and passed to LocalCommandRunner.cs:52 directly into ProcessStartInfo.Environment with no denylist. Example: command approved as 'git status' but GIT_SSH_COMMAND='evil.sh' silently redirects execution. Shell wrappers allow inner payloads to avoid exec policy evaluation entirely. Existing tests (SystemRunTests.cs:110, ExecApprovalPolicyTests.cs:471) explicitly assert the vulnerable behavior.

signals.topic: Streaming interruption corrupts JSONL session files causing permanent session crash loops requiring manual JSON surgery
signals.summary: When an Anthropic streaming response is interrupted mid-tool-call, partialJson is stored with unescaped newline characters. Every subsequent message to that session crashes with 'Bad control character in JSON'. Sessions are permanently unresponsive; recovery requires manual JSONL patching.
aliases: streaming interruption JSON parse crash loop
signals.review_reason: User-facing session corruption with permanent crash loop. Every message to the session fails, recovery requires manual JSON surgery, and forked recovery attempts also fail. This is a main-flow-blocking session state issue with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Session corruption: truncated streaming tool call stores unescaped newline in partialJson, causing persistent JSON parse error
source_issues.evidence: Session enters permanent crash loop on every subsequent message. Forked recovery sessions inherit same corrupted data. Manual JSONL patching required. Reproduced twice in same day.

signals.topic: Exec preflight refusal causes unhandled promise rejection that kills the entire gateway process
signals.summary: When exec preflight validation refuses a command mid-run, a stale stdout callback fires after run teardown. pi-agent-core's processEvents() throws 'Agent listener invoked outside active run'. This unhandled rejection crashes the entire gateway with exit code 1, disconnecting all channels until manual container restart. 100% reproduction rate.
aliases: gateway crash unhandled promise rejection exec preflight
agent listener invoked outside active run crash
gateway exit code 1 exec preflight refusal
signals.review_reason: A tool-level refusal (heredoc or complex shell construction) kills the entire gateway process. All channels go offline until manual intervention. This is a main-flow-blocking process crash with 100% reproduction rate — a common path since exec preflight refusals are frequent.

source_issues.title: Unhandled promise rejection in pi-agent-core crashes gateway when exec preflight refuses a command mid-run
source_issues.evidence: Gateway exits with code 1 after exec preflight refusal. Unhandled promise rejection from pi-agent-core processEvents(). All channels (Telegram, Discord, etc.) disconnect until manual docker restart. 100% reproduction rate on demand.

signals.topic: openclaw status and cron list commands hang with SIGKILL on Windows (all Node v22+ versions)
signals.summary: On Windows 11 with Node v22+, openclaw status and openclaw cron list hang indefinitely and are killed with SIGKILL. All cron jobs execute normally and gateway HTTP works, but CLI status commands are unusable. Regression introduced in 4.15 (works on 4.14).
aliases: cron list hangs Windows Node v22
signals.review_reason: Status and cron monitoring commands are completely unusable on Windows. While the gateway itself runs, users cannot check system health or cron status from the CLI. This blocks diagnostic and operational workflows on a major platform.

source_issues.title: openclaw status/cron list hangs with SIGKILL on Windows (Node v22+)
source_issues.evidence: openclaw status and openclaw cron list hang indefinitely and are killed with SIGKILL on Windows 11. Regression in 4.15 (works on 4.14). Affects all tested Node v22/v24/v25 versions on Windows.

signals.topic: Linux .deb package installation fails due to cross-device hard link error
signals.summary: The .deb package downloaded from the official website fails to install on Linux systems where /tmp and /usr reside on different filesystems, with dpkg throwing 'Invalid cross-device link' errors for the icon hard link.
aliases: cross-device link error on Linux install
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-blocking issue: the primary distribution package (.deb) fails to install on Linux, preventing any use of the tool. The hard link in the electron-builder output causes dpkg extraction from tmpfs to fail when linking to files on the main filesystem. No workaround for end users. Count=1 (single issue but affecting all Linux users attempting .deb install).

source_issues.title: .deb package fails to install: cross-device hard link error for icon file
source_issues.evidence: User reports that installing the .deb (v0.2.40) fails with dpkg error: 'error creating hard link ./usr/share/icons/hicolor/1024x1024/apps/interpreter.png: Invalid cross-device link'. Affects any Linux distro where /tmp (tmpfs) and /usr are on different filesystems. No workaround available for end users.

signals.topic: Embedded browser UI covers all tabs and blocks tab switching
signals.summary: When the embedded browser is opened in the desktop app, it covers all tab content regardless of which tab is active, making it impossible to switch tabs or interact with other parts of the UI.
signals.review_reason: This is a UX-blocking issue: when the embedded browser is active, users cannot interact with other tabs in the desktop UI. The browser window is rendered on top of tab content, making the core multi-tab workflow unusable. Confirmed on multiple WMs (Hyprland/Wayland and XFCE/X11). Non-critical but clear user-experience degradation of a primary workflow.

source_issues.title: Browser pages cover middle area of UI, regardless of what tab is selected
source_issues.evidence: User reports that opening any browser in the app covers all content across all tabs, with the browser rendering on top of tab content. Confirmed on both Hyprland (Wayland) and XFCE (X11) on Arch Linux. Tab switching is functionally broken when browser is open.

signals.topic: Dependency version conflicts (openai/httpx) cause ImportError crashes at startup
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught ImportError on startup when openai or httpx package versions are incompatible — openai.lib._parsing/_pydantic imports fail, httpx.BaseTransport import fails, openai._utils.is_type_alias_type import fails.
signals.review_reason: Three separate users hit ImportError crashes at startup from dependency version conflicts in the litellm→openai→httpx chain. All block the primary use case (running Aider). Count=3 is exact from file data.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in utils.py line 43
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name '_parsing' from 'openai.lib' — blocks all aider operations via LiteLLM initialization failure

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in _legacy_response.py line 27
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'is_type_alias_type' from 'openai._utils' — blocks startup via litellm/openai chain

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in _types.py line 36
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseTransport' from 'httpx' — blocks startup via litellm/httpx chain

signals.topic: Git cache deserialization crash (struct.error) causing uncaught exception at startup
signals.summary: Aider crashes with struct.error in fun.py read_cache() when deserializing git index cache — corrupt or truncated .git/index causes unpack to fail, blocking the entire application from starting.
signals.review_reason: Two users hit the same crash at the exact same location (fun.py:263 read_cache). This is a primary-flow blocker — sanity_check_repo() is called during startup before any user interaction. The crash prevents Aider from launching at all. Count=2 is exact from file data.

source_issues.title: Uncaught error in fun.py line 263

source_issues.title: Uncaught error in fun.py line 263

signals.topic: Git config lock conflict (OSError) causing startup blockage

signals.review_reason: Two users hit git lock-related OSError crashes during git setup (main.py setup_git). One is a stale lock (5060) and one is a permission denied (5044). Both block startup. Count=2 is exact from file data.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1045
