signals.topic: Windows console encoding errors crash output rendering
signals.summary: On Windows with legacy console (cp1252 encoding), Aider crashes with uncaught UnicodeEncodeError or OSError when Rich console tries to render Unicode characters — crashes during output display, preventing users from seeing responses.
aliases: Rich console Windows legacy terminal crash
signals.review_reason: Two Windows users hit crashes in Rich console's legacy Windows renderer due to encoding incompatibility. Both crash during output display, making the tool unusable for affected users. Count=2 is exact from file data.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in _win32_console.py line 403
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument during flush() in legacy Windows console renderer — crash during output stream rendering

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u25ba' — crashes when Rich console renders Unicode output to Windows cp1252 terminal

signals.topic: Architect mode transforms repository prompt injection into committed backdoored code
signals.summary: In architect mode, attacker-controlled content in repository files (e.g., README.md) can inject ARCHITECT OVERRIDE instructions that the architect model emits as malicious code, which the editor model commits — exfiltrating .env data to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
aliases: trust boundary bypass in architect mode
signals.review_reason: Security-relevant trust boundary violation with a validated retest. The author demonstrated a concrete exploit: malicious README.md content causes Aider to commit code that exfiltrates .env. This is a high-severity security issue affecting any user of architect mode with potentially untrusted repository content. Count=1 is exact from file data.

source_issues.title: Architect mode can turn README prompt injection into committed backdoored code
source_issues.evidence: Validated retest: malicious README.md → architect output → editor applies malicious import to auth.py → aider commits backdoored file that exfiltrates .env via base64 to attacker.com. Call chain: architect_coder.py:17,44, base_coder.py:912-930. Root cause: architect output forwarded with preproc=False bypassing normal input preprocessing.

signals.topic: API credentials (Authorization headers, apiKey) exposed in plain text in UI and SQLite database
signals.summary: When users run evals with providers that inject credentials into headers (e.g., Authorization: Bearer), the rendered credential values are stored verbatim in ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db and displayed in the UI "Details" panel. This causes live API keys/tokens to leak when users share debug blobs, exports, or shared eval URLs.
aliases: API key exposure in eval results
signals.review_reason: Direct credential exposure — user shares a debug Details blob or exports eval results and leaks a live API key/token. Affects all users who evaluate against authenticated providers. The victim does not see the risk until the secret is already shared. Count=1 here but severity is critical: a single occurrence of live credential exposure is a high-severity incident.

source_issues.title: UI and stored eval record expose rendered Authorization / apiKey in plain text
source_issues.evidence: Credentials rendered in headers (e.g., Authorization: Bearer sk-realLiveSecret_xxx) are stored verbatim in SQLite ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db and displayed in UI Details panel. Users leak live keys when sharing debug blobs, exports, or shared eval URLs.

signals.topic: OpenRouter provider silently ignores user-supplied apiBaseUrl config, routing requests to wrong endpoint
signals.summary: The OpenRouter provider hardcodes apiBaseUrl after spreading user config, so any user-supplied apiBaseUrl (e.g., for a corporate proxy) is silently discarded. Requests go to openrouter.ai directly, causing unexpected 401 errors from the proxy.
signals.review_reason: Functional blocker for users routing OpenRouter traffic through a proxy (compliance, caching). The override is silent with no warning, making it hard to diagnose. Users discover it only via 401s or packet capture, which is a significant workflow disruption for proxy-based deployments.

source_issues.title: openrouter provider: hardcoded apiBaseUrl silently overrides user config
source_issues.evidence: super() call in OpenRouterProvider hardcodes apiBaseUrl after user config spread, silently dropping any user-supplied apiBaseUrl. Requests go to openrouter.ai instead of the user's proxy, surfacing as unexpected 401 errors.

signals.topic: Embedding promptfoo library in TypeScript projects fails with 'enum not supported in strip-only mode' error
signals.summary: When users try to use promptfoo as a library in their own TypeScript project, eval crashes with 'TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode'. NODE_OPTIONS workaround fails with module resolution error (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Users cannot embed promptfoo for custom workflows.
signals.review_reason: Blocks the entire use case of embedding promptfoo as a library in TypeScript projects. Users cannot evaluate their own providers at all when using strip-only mode, and the documented workaround fails with a different error. This is a direct workflow blocker for programmatic usage.

source_issues.title: Integrating Promptfoo with a Frontend TypeScript Project
source_issues.evidence: Users embedding promptfoo as a library get 'TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode' error on eval, and the NODE_OPTIONS workaround fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The entire integration workflow is blocked.

signals.topic: GET /eval/:id/table endpoint crashes with RangeError for large evals, making result viewing impossible
signals.summary: When an eval produces large outputs (e.g., base64-encoded images, large prompts with many test cases), the table endpoint JSON.stringify() exceeds V8's ~512MB string limit and throws an unhandled RangeError, returning a 500 error. Users cannot view eval results in the UI at all.
aliases: RangeError V8 string limit eval results
signals.review_reason: Core workflow failure: users with large evals (image-based prompts, many test cases) cannot view their results at all in the UI. The endpoint returns a 500 error with no graceful degradation, making the primary results-viewing experience completely unavailable for affected users.

source_issues.title: RangeError crash on GET /eval/:id/table for large evals
source_issues.evidence: Endpoint crashes with unhandled RangeError when eval payload exceeds V8's ~512MB string limit during JSON.stringify(). Users see a 500 error and the UI fails to load results for large evals with base64 images.

signals.topic: model_dump() in-place mutation corrupts structured LLM responses when telemetry is active
signals.summary: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() converts ChatResponse.raw from Pydantic model to dict permanently for the caller. Any code using StructuredLLM.achat() with active OpenTelemetry subscriber receives a dict instead of Pydantic model, causing AttributeError on all callers accessing structured response fields.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for users using structured LLMs with OpenTelemetry/telemetry enabled. Silent corruption in production telemetry environments. Clear root cause identified, proposed fix available.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, corrupting caller's response object
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() converts ChatResponse.raw from Pydantic model to dict permanently for the caller. With OpenTelemetry subscriber active, callers get AttributeError accessing structured response fields.

signals.topic: Cross-provider agent workflows broken due to unserialized tool_kwargs in Chat Completions API
signals.summary: OpenAI Chat Completions API returns 400 BadRequestError when Anthropic hands off to OpenAI sub-agent because function.arguments is sent as a JSON object instead of a JSON string. to_openai_message_dict places block.tool_kwargs directly into 'arguments' without json.dumps().
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for users running multi-provider agent workflows (e.g., Anthropic orchestrator with OpenAI sub-agent). One-line fix identified but blocks key use case.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs and breaks cross-provider agent workflows
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI API returns 400 BadRequestError when Anthropic hands off to OpenAI sub-agent. Root cause: to_openai_message_dict places block.tool_kwargs directly into 'arguments' without json.dumps(), while to_openai_responses_message_dict correctly serializes.

signals.topic: Bedrock Nova 2 Lite model throws ValidationException due to unsupported textGenerationConfig parameter
signals.summary: Using model 'global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0' with Bedrock causes ValidationException: 'Malformed input request: extraneous key [textGenerationConfig] is not permitted'. Model completely unusable.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for users of this specific Bedrock model. Model completely unusable with clear ValidationException error and known affected model ID.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Error with Bedrock's `global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0`
source_issues.evidence: Using model 'global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0' with Bedrock causes ValidationException: 'Malformed input request: extraneous key [textGenerationConfig] is not permitted'. Works fine with other models.

signals.topic: AgentStream.thinking_delta missing when using Anthropic LLM with FunctionAgent streaming
signals.summary: FunctionAgent/AgentWorkflow streaming only forwards thinking content from ChatResponse.additional_kwargs['thinking_delta']. Anthropic streaming integration does not normalize thinking deltas into additional_kwargs, causing AgentStream.thinking_delta to remain empty for all chunks.
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation - users with Anthropic thinking/reasoning enabled do not see thinking content in agent output. Non-blocking but obvious quality degradation affecting a key Anthropic feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Missing AgentStream.thinking_delta when using Anthropic LLM with FunctionAgent
source_issues.evidence: FunctionAgent streaming only forwards thinking content from ChatResponse.additional_kwargs['thinking_delta']. Anthropic streaming integration does not normalize thinking deltas into additional_kwargs, causing AgentStream.thinking_delta to remain empty.

signals.topic: Falsy metadata values (0, empty string, empty list) incorrectly stored as None in Azure AI Search
signals.summary: Azure AI Search vector store uses 'if metadata_value:' check instead of 'if metadata_value is not None:'. This causes falsy values (0, '', []) to be stored as None. Clear one-line fix identified.
signals.review_reason: Data integrity issue - users lose actual falsy values (0, '', []) and get None instead. Causes incorrect data retrieval. Simple fix identified but silently corrupts user data in production.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: falsy metadata values stored as None in Azure AI Search index
source_issues.evidence: Azure AI Search vector store uses 'if metadata_value:' check instead of 'if metadata_value is not None:'. Falsy values (0, '', []) stored as None instead. Silent data corruption affecting retrieval accuracy.

signals.topic: Daemon process silently crashes/exits on Windows due to `ps -o` incompatibility — blocks daemon lifecycle management
signals.summary: On Windows (Git Bash/msys2), both `daemon start` and `daemon status` fail silently because the code uses Unix `ps -o pid` syntax which the Windows `ps` port does not support. `daemon start` prints '[OK]' but the process dies within ~2s, leaving an orphaned PID file. `daemon status` always reports STOPPED even when the daemon is running. This blocks the entire daemon lifecycle on Windows.
aliases: daemon status false STOPPED on Windows
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm daemon lifecycle (start + status check) is fully broken on Windows. Issue #1635 shows daemon start prints '[OK]' but exits within ~2s, leaving orphaned state. Issue #1633 shows daemon status always reports STOPPED. Combined, users cannot start daemons reliably or verify their status on Windows — this is a main-flow block for the platform.

source_issues.title: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on v3.5.7 and v3.5.80. Process exits within ~2s after '[OK] Daemon started'. PID file orphaned, daemon.log stays 0 bytes. `ruflo daemon start --foreground` works as workaround.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Daemon status shows STOPPED on Windows — ps -o pid command not supported
source_issues.evidence: ruflo daemon status always shows STOPPED immediately after starting, despite process running. Error: 'ps: unknown option -- o'. Affects all Windows Git Bash/msys2 users.

signals.topic: Session management commands crash/corrupt data — session save TypeError, session list broken, session-end hang
signals.summary: Multiple session commands fail on v3.5.80: `session save` throws TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'agentCount') and prints contradictory 'Session saved' + 'Failed to save session'. `session list` renders corrupted rows with empty ID/name and 'Invalid Date In...' timestamps. `session-end` hangs indefinitely (0% CPU, open DB handle). The schema writer and reader are out of sync.
signals.review_reason: Issue #1634 and #1626 together document session lifecycle fully broken: save crashes with TypeError and writes partial/corrupt records, list reads nothing meaningful, and session-end hangs forever leaving orphaned processes. Users cannot reliably persist or retrieve session state — this is a main workflow blocker for anyone using swarm/session features.

source_issues.title: ruflo/claude-flow session save crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)'
source_issues.evidence: session save prints 'Session saved' then '[ERROR] TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)'. Partial record written to disk. session list shows ~10 rows with empty ID, empty name '-', 'Invalid Date In...' timestamps. session current reports 'No active session' immediately after save.

source_issues.title: CLI v3.5.80: session-end hang, session save TypeError, session list broken rendering
source_issues.evidence: Bug 1: session-end hangs forever after writing state to disk (holds memory.db open, 0% CPU, process never exits). Bug 2: session save throws TypeError when no swarm active (same agentCount issue). Bug 3: session list renders 10 empty rows with 'Invalid Date In...'. Bug 4: session-end summary shows undefined counters.

signals.topic: MCP hooks post-task and session-end hang indefinitely after completing work — orphaned Node processes
signals.summary: `ruflo hooks post-task` records outcomes successfully but the Node process never exits until externally killed (timeout required). `ruflo hooks session-end` similarly hangs forever after writing session state to disk. Both hang due to unclosed async handles (timers, MCP clients, fs watchers) keeping the event loop alive. Slash commands and CI scripts that invoke these hooks stall until manually killed.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm hooks post-task and session-end both hang indefinitely after successfully completing their work. This is not a functional failure in the core logic — the work IS done — but the process never exits, blocking CI pipelines and slash commands. The hang is caused by unclosed async handles keeping the Node event loop alive. This is a main workflow blocker for any automation that calls these hooks.

source_issues.title: ruflo hooks post-task hangs indefinitely after recording outcome (v3.5.80)
source_issues.evidence: post-task completes work in ~1.1s then hangs indefinitely. exit=124 from timeout SIGTERM, not a clean exit. All stdin variations tested (empty string, {}, null) — same hang. Impact: slash commands and CI scripts stall until externally killed. Workaround: wrap with 'timeout 10'.

source_issues.title: CLI v3.5.80: session-end hang, session save TypeError, session list broken rendering
source_issues.evidence: session-end prints 'State saved to: .claude/sessions/...' then hangs forever. Process state after 4+ minutes: S (sleeping), 0.0% CPU, 1.76s total CPU time. lsof shows it still holds memory.db open (fd 18). Workaround: kill <pid>.

signals.topic: MCP worker dispatch and workflow_run report false success — fabricated completions without real execution
signals.summary: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns status:completed synchronously without routing to the daemon's actual worker implementations; daemon runCount does not increment. workflow_run returns agentsSpawned:0 for both dryRun:true and live invocations. process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs that don't match the real daemon worker registry. The CLI daemon trigger (ruflo daemon trigger --worker) DOES work correctly, proving the daemon pipeline is functional but MCP surfaces are stubbed/mis-routed.
aliases: workflow_run returns zero agents spawned live
process workers list hardcoded demo IDs
signals.review_reason: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch claims to have completed work but the daemon runCount never incremented, meaning no real worker ran. workflow_run fabricates zero-spawn metrics even in live mode. Users relying on MCP responses as execution truth will make incorrect decisions. This is a reporting-vs-execution gap that causes silent failures in automation pipelines built on the MCP tool layer.

source_issues.title: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns fabricated completion independent of daemon; process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs
source_issues.evidence: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns {status:'completed'} in <1s but daemon runCount is UNCHANGED — no real worker executed. workflow_run returns agentsSpawned:0 for both dryRun modes. process workers --action list returns 'worker-task-001', 'worker-coord-001' etc. — hardcoded demo IDs unrelated to real daemon state.ruflo daemon trigger --worker audit DOES increment runCount and returns real output, proving the daemon pipeline works but MCP surfaces are disconnected.

signals.topic: Memory search threshold:0 returns empty results due to JS falsy-coercion bug in `||` operator
signals.summary: memory_search with threshold:0 silently returns empty results because the code uses `|| 0.3` instead of `?? 0.3`, coercing the falsy 0 to the default. Users who explicitly set threshold:0 (intent: 'show me everything') get no results while threshold:0.001 works correctly. The same `||` numeric-default anti-pattern exists in 6 other handlers (embeddings-tools, claims-tools, neural-tools, daa-tools), all dropping user-supplied 0 values.
signals.review_reason: When a user explicitly passes threshold:0 (documented intent: 'show all results'), the search returns nothing due to JS `||` coercion treating 0 as falsy. This is a silent data-loss bug — users get empty results with no indication that their explicit parameter was ignored. The same anti-pattern exists in 6 other handlers, meaning multiple numeric parameters can be silently replaced with defaults.

source_issues.title: Bug: memory_search with threshold: 0 returns empty results due to || coercion (sibling to #1489)
source_issues.evidence: memory_search with threshold:0 returns {results:[], total:0} even when matching entries exist. Same call with threshold:0.001 returns 1 result with similarity:0.6998. Root cause: 'input.threshold || 0.3' coerces falsy 0 to 0.3. Same || anti-pattern in 6 other handlers. Fix verified locally: change to 'input.threshold ?? 0.3' restores documented behavior.

signals.topic: Chrome orphan processes after network blip degrade main Chrome performance by 17x on macOS
signals.summary: When a network blip occurs during an agent-browser session bootstrapped with --profile or --session-name, the Chrome CDP connection drops and the CLI exits abnormally. The spawned Chrome process becomes orphaned, continues listening on port 9222, and shares profile state with the user's real Chrome, causing main Chrome throughput to drop from ~700 Mbps to ~36 Mbps. This is a regression from the v0.25.2 fix that removed PR_SET_PDEATHSIG — now no cross-platform watchdog kills the Chrome child when the parent CLI dies abnormally.
aliases: Chrome orphan on macOS after network loss
macOS Chrome process leak on network blip
Chrome PDEATHSIG regression causing orphan + main-Chrome degradation
signals.review_reason: High user impact: network blip during a session leaves a persistent orphan Chrome that degrades the user's own Chrome performance 17x (from 700Mbps to 36Mbps) until manually killed. This blocks daily development workflow on macOS and is a direct regression from the v0.25.2 PDEATHSIG removal. Main Chrome workflow is impaired until user performs multi-step manual cleanup.

source_issues.title: Chrome orphan after network blip during --profile / cookie-bypass sessions on macOS (v0.26.0, regression counterpart to #1157)
source_issues.evidence: Orphaned Chrome process persists after network blip, holding port 9222 and temp profile dir. Main Chrome degrades to 36 Mbps (from ~700 Mbps). Incognito and Safari unaffected. Reproduction consistent across multiple cycles. Recovery requires manual process kill + profile cleanup.

signals.topic: Windows Git Bash `open` command hangs indefinitely with no timeout or error on Windows 11
signals.summary: On Windows 11 with Git Bash, `agent-browser --session <name> open <url>` hangs indefinitely with no stdout, no error, and never returns — even with a fresh OS reboot, unique session names, and plain public URLs. No Chromium processes are spawned before the hang, indicating the hang is in the Chromium launcher path itself (socket handshake, pipe handler, or profile-creation retry). This completely blocks the primary workflow of opening pages.
aliases: Windows Git Bash open hangs forever
agent-browser open command freezes on Windows Git Bash
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow blockage on a major platform (Windows 11 Git Bash). The `open` command — the most fundamental operation — hangs indefinitely with no error output, preventing users from using agent-browser at all. User explicitly states their verification gate stalls because of this.

source_issues.title: open <url> hangs indefinitely on Windows Git Bash (post-reboot + clean pid files, no Chromium zombies)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on plain public URLs (example.com), fresh post-reboot state, no stale PID/port files, no Chromium processes present. CLI hangs before spawning Chromium. timeout 25s eventually kills it. User's entire verification workflow stalls as a result.

signals.topic: Windows: `open` reports success but `get url`/`snapshot` return stale `about:blank` state
signals.summary: On Windows, when connecting to an externally launched Chrome via `agent-browser connect <port>` followed by `open <url>`, the `open` command reports success and the real browser window navigates correctly, but `get url` and `snapshot` still report `about:blank` or an empty page. This is a session/active-page/tab-state mismatch on Windows — the CDP target tracked by the daemon diverges from the actual active tab.
aliases: Windows CDP connect + open state desync
Windows session tab state mismatch after open
signals.review_reason: Primary workflow failure on Windows: `open` reports success while the actual state is `about:blank`. Users get completely wrong content from `get url` and `snapshot` commands, making the tool unreliable for any automation on Windows. The browser visually navigates but agent commands operate on a stale tab.

source_issues.title: Windows: agent-browser connect/open succeeds but get url / snapshot still stay on about:blank or an empty page
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Windows 11 with Chrome launched manually and connected via agent-browser. open returns success, browser window navigates, but get url returns 'about:blank' and snapshot returns empty page. Session/tab state desynchronization on Windows.

signals.topic: Semantic locators silently fail to find elements inside Shadow DOM
signals.summary: Semantic locators (e.g., `find placeholder Password fill testpass`) return 'Element not found' error when the target element is inside a Shadow DOM. Unlike CSS selectors that can pierce shadow roots via `>>`, semantic locators have no mechanism to traverse Shadow DOM boundaries. This causes agent-driven automations to fail on many modern web applications (Web Components, Material Design, Chrome extensions).
aliases: Semantic locators fail in Shadow DOM
Shadow DOM element lookup broken for semantic locators
signals.review_reason: Semantic locators are a core agent-facing feature designed for natural-language element selection. Their failure in Shadow DOM is a direct functional gap causing agent-driven workflows to fail on any Shadow DOM-based web application (increasingly common with Web Components, Material Design, Chrome extension UIs). This is an expected capability gap.

source_issues.title: Semantic locators do not work throw shadow dom
source_issues.evidence: Command 'agent-browser --session test123 find placeholder Password fill testpass' returns 'Element not found' when element with placeholder 'Password' is inside shadow DOM. Modern web apps using Web Components / Shadow DOM are affected.

signals.topic: Snapshot serializer strips whitespace around HTML comment nodes, producing incorrect text for React JSX whitespace
signals.summary: React/Next.js compilers emit `` HTML comment nodes between sibling elements (e.g., `<>prefix{' '}suffix`). Real browsers and screen readers render these as a space. The agent-browser snapshot serializer strips both the comment and the adjacent whitespace text node, causing StaticText to concatenate adjacent words with no space (e.g., 'yesterday.Two' instead of 'yesterday. Two'). This creates false-positive 'typo' or 'accessibility bug' reports for agents inspecting React pages.
aliases: Snapshot drops spaces in React JSX whitespace expressions
Accessibility tree serializer strips comment-adjacent whitespace in React pages
signals.review_reason: Snapshot output is the primary data interface for agents reading page content. Incorrect serialization causes agents to draw wrong conclusions about page content (false 'typo' reports), wastes reasoning turns investigating non-bugs, and affects all React/Next.js applications using standard JSX whitespace patterns. User explicitly states this caused a false-positive issue report during dogfooding.

source_issues.title: Snapshot text serializer strips whitespace around HTML comments (JSX {' '} false-positive)
source_issues.evidence: React Next.js page renders correctly in browser but snapshot concatenates 'yesterday.Two' with no space due to stripped comment + whitespace. Confirmed against superseller.agency (Next.js 15). Causes agents to report false accessibility bugs and wastes reasoning turns.

signals.topic: Chatbot main flow throws generic "Oops, an error occurred!" and is unusable
signals.summary: 用户在正常使用 chatbot 时反复遭遇通用错误提示，主流程被阻断，聊天功能完全不可用。
aliases: Generic error message on every interaction
signals.review_reason: Issue #1488 有明确用户影响证据：用户截图证明主流程（聊天交互）持续抛出通用错误提示，核心功能不可用。该问题属于主流程阻断，截图附件进一步佐证了问题的真实性和可复现性。虽 count=1（非高频），但影响严重（关键功能不可用），符合 P1 定级。

source_issues.title: Well it doesn't work it always says : Oops, an error occurred!
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports the app 'always says: Oops, an error occurred!' with screenshot attached, indicating a blocking, reproducible failure of the core chat interaction.

signals.topic: Tool-only assistant messages send content:"" in xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral providers — API rejection
signals.summary: The message converter in four provider packages emits `content: ""` (empty string) for assistant messages that contain only tool calls. This violates the OpenAI spec (content must be null when tool_calls is present) and causes API rejection on multiple providers.
aliases: empty string content for tool-only assistant messages across xai/deepseek/groq/mistral
signals.review_reason: P0: count=4 (4 provider packages affected by the same root-cause bug), blocks tool calling entirely on xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, and Mistral providers. Follows the same pattern as previously fixed for Bedrock in #13466/#13744. Reproduction confirmed. All four packages share identical faulty code pattern.

source_issues.title: Bug: tool-only assistant messages send content:"" in xai, deepseek, groq, mistral providers
source_issues.evidence: Same bug pattern across 4 provider packages (xai, deepseek, groq, mistral). Proposed fix is to change `content: text` to `content: text || null`. Bedrock-backed endpoints already rejected this pattern in OpenAI-compatible providers (issues #13466, #13744). Confirmed against OpenAI spec (content is nullable when tool_calls present).

signals.topic: Google-Vertex rejects includeServerSideToolInvocations on Gemini 3.x with function tools
signals.summary: The SDK hard-codes `includeServerSideToolInvocations: true` in the tool config for Gemini 3-or-newer + function tools, but Vertex's global endpoint now rejects this field with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. Every Vertex request using function tools with gemini-3-flash-preview fails unconditionally.
signals.review_reason: P0 despite count=1: this is a main-process-blocking bug that makes function tools completely unusable for every Gemini 3.x Vertex user (the entire Gemini-3+function-tools code path is dead). Exact reproduction path and error response from Vertex API provided. No valid user-facing workaround besides downgrading.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google: Vertex rejects tool_config.includeServerSideToolInvocations on gemini-3-flash-preview with function tools
source_issues.evidence: Every Vertex request to gemini-3-*-preview with function tools fails with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. Workaround is to downgrade to gemini-2.5, losing Gemini-3-only features like native google_search grounding + function tools mixing. Direct API call to Vertex endpoint confirmed the field is rejected server-side.

signals.topic: xAI/Grok tool calling broken: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema adds additionalProperties:false which xAI rejects
signals.summary: The SDK's addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema function unconditionally adds `additionalProperties: false` to all object schemas during tool serialization. xAI's validator explicitly rejects schemas with boolean property schemas and considers the field redundant since it already defaults to false. All xAI/Grok tool calls fail with a schema validation error.
aliases: xAI Grok tool schema validation error additionalProperties:false
signals.review_reason: P1: main-process-blocking for xAI/Grok tool calling users. All xAI tool calls fail unconditionally with a schema validation error. Workaround disables the feature entirely. Reproduction provided. Slightly narrower scope than PP-002 (single provider), hence P1.

source_issues.title: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema breaks xAI/Grok tool calling: xAI rejects additionalProperties: false
source_issues.evidence: Every tool call with xAI/Grok models fails with: '[xAI] Invalid request content: Schema validation failed: [standard_violation] /properties/properties/additionalProperties: property schema 'false' is not supported'. Affects direct xAI provider, OpenRouter xAI models, and any OpenAI-compatible provider routing to xAI. xAI docs confirm the field is rejected. Workaround disables tools entirely for xAI.

signals.topic: streamText stops mid-generation after first tool call when maxSteps > 1 in Node.js streaming context
signals.summary: When using streamText with tool calls and maxSteps > 1 in a Node.js server context (e.g. Next.js API Route), the stream terminates silently after the first tool invocation. The client receives a truncated stream with no error. The multi-step tool-use loop never completes.
aliases: streamText stream truncation with tool calls maxSteps > 1
stream terminates after first tool step Node.js
signals.review_reason: P1: blocks multi-step tool-use streaming workflows in Node.js server environments. The stream terminates silently without error, making the failure opaque and hard to debug. This is a key use case for AI SDK streaming applications.

source_issues.title: streamText response stops mid-generation when used with tool calls and maxSteps > 1 in Node.js streaming context
source_issues.evidence: User provides exact repro steps: streamText with tools + maxSteps:3 in Next.js API Route. Stream cuts off silently after first tool call. No error thrown. Full multi-step generation never completes. Affects real streaming applications using multi-step tool loops in Node.js server contexts.

signals.topic: MCP HTTP/SSE transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after version negotiation — breaks Figma Dev Mode MCP
signals.summary: The MCP transport always sends LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION in the mcp-protocol-version header, ignoring the version negotiated during initialize. This violates MCP spec and causes post-initialization requests to fail against any server that does not support the latest version (e.g. Figma Dev Mode MCP supports max 2025-06-18, client sends 2025-11-25).
aliases: MCP protocol version header not negotiated down after init
Figma Dev Mode MCP connection failure
signals.review_reason: P1: blocks entire MCP integration workflow for any server not supporting the latest protocol version. Verified against real Figma Dev Mode MCP (widely-used product). The client hangs indefinitely on connection, providing a completely broken experience. Fix validated via local patch.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/mcp] Streamable HTTP transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after version negotiation
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced against real Figma Dev Mode MCP Server: initialize succeeds (server negotiates 2025-06-18), but all subsequent requests fail with 400 'Unsupported protocol version'. Direct curl with negotiated version succeeds, confirming bug is client-side. Affects both 1.x and 2.0-beta lines. 6 tools available but completely inaccessible.

signals.topic: Build crashes prerendering /_global-error with TypeError across multiple Node versions
signals.summary: next build crashes during prerender of the built-in /_global-error route with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading useContext)'. Affects fresh create-next-app scaffolds on Node 20+ and Node 25, breaking the build for any project whose root layout uses React context.
signals.review_reason: Build process crashes for a fresh scaffold — the most common first experience for new Next.js users. Any project using React context in its root layout (extremely common with providers) cannot build. This is a main flow failure (build pipeline blocked) affecting multiple Node versions, not just an edge case.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16: isPageStatic() hardcodes _global-error as isStatic with empty appConfig, causing prerender crash when root layout uses React context
source_issues.evidence: isPageStatic() hardcodes appConfig: {} for /_global-error, causing revalidate check to pass and route to be added to staticPaths. Prerender attempt crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext'). Affects any project with React context in root layout.

source_issues.title: next build fails on Node 25 during prerender (Next 15 and 16 scaffolds)
source_issues.evidence: Fresh create-next-app scaffold (no user code) crashes at prerender step on Node 25.4.0. Same app builds cleanly on Node 20. Reproduces with both Turbopack and Webpack.

source_issues.title: Next 16.2.4: next build crashes prerendering /_global-error with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed crash on next@16.2.4. Pinning next@16.3.0-canary.2 resolves it, confirming the fix exists but is not yet in stable.

signals.topic: Memory leak in stable releases causes production OOM with confirmed kill events
signals.summary: Fixes from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) addressing a memory leak that causes arrayBuffers to accumulate until OOM have not been backported to any 16.x stable release for 45+ days. Real production services on Render and similar PaaS are OOM-killed every ~8 hours.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed production OOM kills with 4 events in 7 days on a real deployment. Memory climbs monotonically at ~30 MiB/hour even at idle, eventually causing SIGKILL. Main production flow (deploying and running a Next.js service) is blocked for all users of 16.x stable. Not a theoretical issue — real cost loss (deployment churn, service disruption) and key functionality (production server) becomes unavailable repeatedly.

source_issues.title: Memory leak fix from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) still not in any 16.x stable release 45+ days later — production OOMs ongoing on 16.2.4
source_issues.evidence: Production Render service (512 MiB cap) climbs 30 MiB/hour at 0% CPU, hits cap in ~8 hours, gets SIGKILLed. 4 confirmed oomKilled events in 7 days. Idle-but-leaking profile proves leak is not traffic-driven. Fix exists in canary but not backported to stable.

source_issues.title: Memory leak fix from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) still not in any 16.x stable release 45+ days later — production OOMs ongoing on 16.2.4
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #93069 with same root cause and real-world OOM evidence on Render.

signals.topic: Blank page after POST action with cacheComponents: true
signals.summary: When a POST action uses headers(), the subsequent page render results in a completely blank page with zero console or server errors. No error is thrown, making this an invisible failure that blocks form submission flows entirely.
aliases: blank page after form submit cacheComponents
signals.review_reason: Invisible failure — zero error output makes this extremely hard to debug. POST form submissions are a core user workflow. The page renders completely blank, which is a main flow failure. Users have no indication of what went wrong or how to work around it.

source_issues.title: Blank page after post with `cacheComponents: true`
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction with video evidence: after clicking submit button on a POST action that uses headers(), the page goes blank with no console errors and no server errors. Page expected to merely refresh but instead renders nothing. Affects next start (production).

signals.topic: Turbopack SSR: CSP nonce not applied to framework-emitted script tags, breaking strict-dynamic CSP in production
signals.summary: In production Turbopack builds, the nonce propagated to SSR via x-nonce header is missing from all /_next/static/chunks/*.js script tags. With script-src strict-dynamic + nonce CSP, the browser blocks all framework chunks and the page loads completely blank.
signals.review_reason: Pages load blank in production under a legitimate CSP configuration (strict-dynamic + nonce), which is a security-hardening pattern widely recommended. The page renders no content at all — this is a production-blocking functional failure. Users are forced to downgrade CSP to unsafe-inline, losing the hardening benefit.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production SSR: nonce not applied to /_next/static/chunks/* script tags even when x-nonce and Content-Security-Policy request headers are present
source_issues.evidence: Live production site curl shows 28 script tags on page, 0 with nonce attribute. Root layout meta tag confirms nonce is propagated correctly. With script-src 'nonce-...' 'strict-dynamic', browser refuses all chunks and page loads blank. Root cause: bootstrapScript object in required-scripts.ts never receives the nonce parameter. Dev-mode equivalent was fixed in PR #65508 but production SSR path in 16.x still broken.

signals.topic: Turbopack workspace root misdetection causes unbounded RAM growth (40+ GB) and machine freeze
signals.summary: An orphan package-lock.json in a parent directory causes Turbopack to infer the wrong workspace root, leading to infinite module-resolution retries and unbounded worker spawning. Observed reaching 43.5 GB RAM with dozens of child workers, freezing the machine.
signals.review_reason: Causes uncontrolled resource exhaustion that makes the developer machine unusable. A single dev session can allocate 40+ GB RAM, potentially triggering OOM kill or OS freeze. On machines with less RAM than the reporter's 64 GB, this would freeze or crash before the user can respond. Windows users are particularly exposed as running npm install in home directory is a common accidental trigger.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: misdetected workspace root (from stray parent lockfile) causes RAM exhaustion (40+ GB) and infinite module-resolution retry on first request
source_issues.evidence: Orphan package-lock.json in parent directory (common on Windows from accidental npm install in home folder) causes Turbopack to infer wrong root. Module resolution fails repeatedly, spawning infinite worker processes. Observed 43,516 MB RAM with 20+ child workers. Machine becomes unresponsive. Fix requires either deleting the orphan lockfile or explicitly setting turbopack.root in config.

signals.topic: getProjects API response Zod validation failure after SDK upgrade breaks project listing
signals.summary: 用户在升级 SDK (1.18.7 → 1.18.9) 后，getProjects API 响应触发 Zod schema 校验失败，表现为 alias 字段期望 array 实际为 undefined，以及 security 字段类型不匹配（期望 undefined/null/object 但实际接收到不兼容结构）。主流程完全阻断，用户无法通过 SDK 正常获取项目列表。
aliases: SDK upgrade causes API response validation to fail
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 明确展示了主流程阻断问题：getProjects 是 SDK 最核心的 API 之一，Zod 校验失败导致用户完全无法获取项目列表。用户在升级后直接遇到，属于 regression 问题，而非边缘场景。review_reason 说明了用户影响（主流程阻断）和具体技术表现（Zod validation error on alias/security fields），而非仅强调技术严重性。count=1 符合实际数据，由于单仓且非高频，不升 P0。

source_issues.title: `getProjects` response validation error
source_issues.evidence: 用户在升级 SDK 1.18.7→1.18.9 后，getProjects 返回的 JSON 触发 ZodError，错误涉及 projects[N].alias 字段（expected array, received undefined）以及 projects[2].security 字段的 union 类型不匹配，覆盖所有项目条目，主流程阻断。

signals.topic: Turborepo 错误地将 peer dependency 识别为 workspace 依赖，导致构建图不正确
signals.summary: 当存在指向同一 workspace 包的 peer dependency 时，Turborepo 将该 workspace 错误地纳入依赖图，导致额外包被构建（如 buffer、d、e），与 Yarn 实际行为产生偏差。
aliases: peer deps treated as local deps
signals.review_reason: 两处 issue 均证明用户在使用 Yarn 4 npm: 协议或 peer deps 时，Turborepo 的 workspace 依赖解析与 Yarn 实际行为产生偏差，造成错误的构建图和额外包的构建。这是明确的用户体验问题：构建结果与预期不符，且浪费 CI 资源。虽然仅单仓问题但有具体复现场景和代码定位，用户影响明确。

source_issues.title: Turborepo incorrectly viewing as peer deps as workspace dependencies when concrete npm dependency exists
source_issues.evidence: Only `b` and `a` should build, but `buffer`, `d`, and `e` also build due to incorrect workspace graph inclusion. Concrete npm devDependency 与 peer dependency 共存时，peer dep 被错误识别为 workspace dep。

source_issues.title: Yarn 4: Respect `enableTransparentWorkspaces: false` when resolving workspace dependencies
source_issues.evidence: 当 workspace 名称与 npm 包名相同时，Turborepo 错误构建该 workspace，与 Yarn 的 transparentWorkspaces=false 行为不符。FFI 包被错误构建，导致 CI 问题和开发机不可构建。

signals.topic: Turborepo AI skill 命令分发器与 SKILL.md 文档矛盾，拒绝有效的 root task 配置
signals.summary: Turborepo skill 的 command dispatcher 有绝对规则禁止创建 root task，与其自身的 SKILL.md 文档（承认存在合法 root task 场景）矛盾，导致 AI agent 对 Vitest Projects 等合法配置生成错误指导。
aliases: root task rejection by AI agent
signals.review_reason: 此问题影响使用 Turborepo skill 的 AI agent 用户，使其对合法的 Turborepo 配置（如 Vitest Projects 的 //#test、changesets、release tooling）生成错误指导。虽然非构建阻断，但直接损害 AI 辅助开发体验，属于用户体验退化而非纯功能请求。

source_issues.title: Turborepo skill: command dispatcher contradicts SKILL.md on Root Tasks
source_issues.evidence: command/turborepo.md 绝对禁止 root task，但 SKILL.md 承认 Vitest Projects 等合法场景。AI agent 遵循 dispatcher 会拒绝正确配置如 //#test，导致下游代码审查失败（ValescoAgency/millsreg-sanity#67）。

signals.topic: turbo query affectedPackages 在 Yarn 4 catalog: 协议下返回空的 LockfileChanged delta，破坏 CI 锁文件过滤
signals.summary: 当根 package.json 使用 Yarn 4 的 catalog: 协议时，affectedPackages 查询对所有未变更的 workspace 均报告空的 LockfileChanged，导致下游 CI 过滤逻辑（added==0 && removed==0）失效。
aliases: affectedPackages empty LockfileChanged with Yarn catalogs
turbo query yarn catalog false positives
signals.review_reason: 用户在生产环境（约 110 个 workspace 的 Yarn 4 monorepo）中实际遇到 affectedPackages 完全失效，导致 CI 锁文件变更检测逻辑失效。这直接导致 CI 资源浪费和构建流程的人为扩大，是明确的用户体验损失和流程阻断问题（非阻断但严重影响）。虽然 count=1 但用户提供了详尽的生产复现证据和根因分析。

source_issues.title: `turbo query affectedPackages` reports empty `LockfileChanged` deltas when root package.json uses Yarn 4 `catalog:` protocol
source_issues.evidence: 在生产 monorepo（~110 workspaces，Yarn 4）中，采用 catalog: 后 100% 的 LockfileChanged 条目变为 { added: [], removed: [] }，导致下游 CI 常用过滤条件（added == 0 && removed == 0）全部失效，CI 管道无法正确收窄 fanout。用户明确报告在 Yarn 4 迁移后此功能完全失效。

signals.topic: Turborepo skill 命令分发器拒绝合法 root task，导致 AI 辅助配置错误
signals.summary: Turborepo skill 的 slash-command dispatcher 以绝对规则拒绝创建 root task，与其官方 SKILL.md 中承认的合法场景（Vitest Projects、changesets 等）矛盾，使 AI agent 对正确配置生成错误指导。
aliases: AI agent rejects valid //#test root tasks
signals.review_reason: AI agent 工具与文档不一致导致辅助生成错误配置的明确证据，属于用户体验退化。虽然非主流程阻断，但影响使用 AI 辅助配置 Turborepo 的开发者群体，且已有下游实际触发案例。

source_issues.title: Turborepo skill: command dispatcher contradicts SKILL.md on Root Tasks
source_issues.evidence: command/turborepo.md:44 硬编码绝对禁止规则，与 SKILL.md:77 矛盾。AI agent 在实际代码审查中发现此矛盾（ValescoAgency/millsreg-sanity#67），agent 对 Vitest Projects 等合法配置拒绝生成或错误生成 root task。

signals.topic: Vercel Toolbar iframe fails to load in COEP-strict apps (credentialless/require-corp), breaking toolbar functionality
signals.summary: When customer apps set Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP) to credentialless or require-corp, the Vercel Toolbar iframe embedded from vercel.live is blocked by the browser because the response lacks a Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (CORP) header. This causes the iframe to load as chrome-error://, which breaks the postMessage handshake and prevents the toolbar from rendering. Users are forced to drop COEP to unsafe-none on preview deployments, sacrificing security isolation.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-impacting bug: COEP-strict apps (a recommended security posture per Chrome's Spectre guidance) cannot use the Vercel Toolbar on preview deployments without compromising their isolation policy. The issue is reproducible, affects all frameworks using COEP, and has no fix other than the user disabling their security policy. Count=1 prevents P0.

source_issues.title: @vercel/toolbar iframe from vercel.live missing CORP header, fails to embed under COEP=credentialless
source_issues.evidence: The toolbar iframe from vercel.live is blocked by COEP policy. Browser shows 'Unsafe attempt to load URL' error. Users must drop COEP to unsafe-none on preview environments, reducing security isolation.

signals.topic: vercel dev fails for Python serverless functions when uv >= 0.10.11 is installed, blocking local dev
signals.summary: getDevPythonVersion() in the Python builder hardcodes minor: 0, which causes vercel dev to invoke `uv venv --python 3.0`. uv 0.10.11 rejects this as Python <3.7 is not supported. Every API call to a Python function returns HTTP 500, making local development with Python serverless functions completely unusable.
aliases: Python local dev broken with newer uv
signals.review_reason: Complete local development flow failure for Python serverless function users. The hardcoded minor: 0 causes uv >= 0.10.11 to reject the version, making every Python function call fail with HTTP 500. This is a direct, reproducible, workflow-blocking bug. Count=1 prevents P0 despite severity.

source_issues.title: getDevPythonVersion() hardcodes minor: 0, breaks local dev with uv >= 0.10.11
source_issues.evidence: vercel dev calls uv venv --python 3.0 which uv 0.10.11 rejects with 'Invalid version request: Python <3.7 is not supported'. Python functions return HTTP 500 in local dev.

signals.topic: vc link links to wrong project and pulls wrong environment variables, causing deployments to target incorrect project
signals.summary: When a user tries to link a specific project (e.g., covillage-portal), vercel link downloads environment variables from a different project (covillage) and writes the wrong OIDC token to .vercel/project.json. Subsequent deployments go to the wrong project, potentially causing wrong env vars to be used and deployments to hit production of the wrong project.
aliases: vercel link downloads wrong project env vars
OIDC token mismatch after vc link
signals.review_reason: Critical flow failure: vc link consistently associates the wrong project, downloads wrong env vars, and writes wrong OIDC tokens. This directly causes deployments to target the wrong project, which can lead to wrong code reaching wrong environments. This is a data-misassociation bug that can have serious consequences in multi-project setups.

source_issues.title: CLI: I can't deploy because `vc link` keeps linking wrong project
source_issues.evidence: User runs vc link for project covillage-portal but vercel downloads env vars from covillage and writes wrong OIDC token. Deploys go to wrong project with wrong env vars.

signals.topic: vercel link --repo fails with SSH host aliases (e.g., github-golden), blocking monorepo Git linking
signals.summary: When a Git remote uses an SSH alias instead of the standard github.com hostname (e.g., git@github-golden:org/repo), the vercel link --repo command fails with 'Failed to parse Git URL'. Single project linking works, but monorepo workflows are blocked for users with SSH alias configurations.
aliases: vercel link --repo SSH alias parsing fails
monorepo git linking with custom SSH hostnames broken
signals.review_reason: Specific monorepo workflow blocked for users with custom SSH aliases. While the single-project linking works as a workaround, users who need multi-identity SSH setups for different projects are unable to use the --repo flag for monorepo linking. This is a regression of intended functionality for a specific but legitimate use case.

source_issues.title: vercel link --repo with aliased host not working
source_issues.evidence: Error: Failed to parse Git URL: git@github-golden:xxx/yyy.git when running vercel link --repo. Single project linking works fine.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.7 context window incorrectly capped at 200K tokens instead of 1M
signals.summary: Zed enforces a 200K token hard cap on Opus 4.7 conversations (triggering reset at ~144K), whereas the model natively supports 1M tokens and competing tools (VS Code Copilot, Claude Code CLI) already expose the full window. Users lose the ability to run long-running AI coding sessions.
aliases: AI assistant context limit too low for Opus 4.7
signals.review_reason: High-impact: directly degrades the primary AI assistant feature. Two independent reports confirm the 200K cap bug on Opus 4.7. Explicit comparison to competing tools proves real user cost.

source_issues.title: Opus 4.7 capped at 200K context instead of 1M (GitHub Copilot offers 1M, Zed does not)
source_issues.evidence: Zed prompts for new context at ~144K tokens reflecting a 200K cap instead of the full 1M window. vscode/copilot and claude code cli already expose 1M. Configured max_tokens: 1000000 is ignored.

source_issues.title: Opus 4-7 not showing up in model list
source_issues.evidence: User cannot select Opus 4.7 model from the model list in agent new thread UI. Blocking AI assistant from using the higher-capability model.

signals.topic: Disabling AI in one project window disables AI globally across all other windows
signals.summary: The 'Disable AI' toggle in Zed settings appears per-project/per-window in the UI, but actually mutates a global state — resulting in AI being shut off in all open Zed windows simultaneously. Breaks multi-window workflows where different projects have different AI policies.
aliases: AI disabled globally instead of per-window
Disable AI setting not scoped per project
signals.review_reason: State management bug: user expectation of per-window AI control conflicts with actual global behavior. While count=1, the misleading UI and cross-window side effects constitute a significant UX and workflow issue.

source_issues.title: Disabling AI in one project window disables AI in all other windows/projects
source_issues.evidence: Two separate Zed windows with different projects: toggling 'Disable AI' in Window A also disables AI in Window B. The UI falsely indicates project-scoped settings while behavior is global. Screenshot evidence of mismatched state across windows.

signals.topic: Agents cannot access custom remote MCP servers that require OAuth authentication
signals.summary: Remote MCP servers configured with OIDC/OAuth authentication show a green status indicator and expose tools correctly in the Zed UI, but the built-in AI agent only sees 'authenticate' stub tools — it cannot use the actual MCP tools. Local MCP servers with the same configuration work fine.
aliases: Remote MCP servers with OAuth not accessible to AI agents
Agent MCP tool injection fails for remote OAuth MCPs
signals.review_reason: Agent-MCP integration failure for OAuth-authenticated remote servers — key extensibility feature is broken for a specific auth path. The same server works via global config, isolating the bug to the per-project MCP + OAuth + agent injection path.

source_issues.title: Agents do not see custom remote MCPs with OAuth authentication
source_issues.evidence: Remote MCP server with OAuth works in Zed UI (shows green, tools listed). Agent only sees authenticate/__complete_authentication stubs and cannot invoke actual MCP tools. Same server works fine when added via global config. Blocks agent-centric MCP workflows.

signals.topic: AI agent file write operations target main git worktree instead of the intended git worktree subdirectory
signals.summary: When Zed opens a project that contains git worktrees as subdirectories (e.g., .worktrees/FEAT-abc/), the AI agent's edit_file/write_file calls resolve paths relative to the main working tree, not the intended worktree. Files are silently written to the wrong location or silently dropped.
aliases: edit_file/write_file resolves paths to main repo in worktree projects
Git worktree agent file operations target wrong directory
signals.review_reason: Core agent capability (file editing) silently fails in a specific directory structure — git worktree setups are increasingly common in monorepo workflows. Silent misrouting means users may not notice corrupted file state until later.

source_issues.title: `write_file` not working for sub-agents within git worktrees?
source_issues.evidence: Agent called edit_file with path '.worktrees/FEAT-abc-my-feature/internal/service/foo.go' but the file was written to the main working tree instead. Requires manual workaround via terminal tool. Blocks multi-worktree development workflows with AI agents.

signals.topic: Remote server binary upload over SSH fails on Windows due to path format incompatibility
signals.summary: On Windows, the remote server upload path uses Windows extended-length path prefix (\\?\) which the system SSH binary cannot parse. This causes 'Could not resolve hostname' errors and blocks users from opening remote SSH projects on Windows when upload_binary_over_ssh is enabled.
aliases: SSH remote upload fails on Windows with extended path prefix
Remote server deployment broken on Windows due to path format
signals.review_reason: Remote development workflow is completely blocked on Windows for SSH setups requiring binary upload. Specific platform path handling bug with clear error log evidence. Priority label in repo is P2 but the block is absolute for the affected scenario.

source_issues.title: Remote server upload over SSH is broken on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'Could not resolve hostname \\\\?\\c: No such host is known.' Windows SSH binary cannot parse the \\\\?\\c: path prefix generated by Zed. Blocks remote SSH project workflow on Windows entirely when binary upload is needed.
